## 1 Management service O&M

### 1.1 Basic Service Control

#### 1.1.1 Rule Center

> On the Rule Center page, you can query the business rules of basic services to facilitate dynamic business logic adjustment.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation** > **Management and control**
**service operation and maintenance** > **Basic Service Control**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Rule Center**.
4. On the **Rules** tab, you can query business rules by **product code**. You can also click
**Advanced Filter** to query rules by **product code** and **action**. The information is displayed
in the following columns: Product code action tag Configuration Status Registered At
5. Find the rule that you want to view and click **Details** in the Operation column to view the
details of the rule. nt service O&M
6. On the **Operation Logs** tab, you can query operation logs by **status**. The information is
displayed in the following columns: Basic Feature Status Type Created At Approved At Workflow ID nt service O&M

#### 1.1.2 Configuration Center

Configuration Center allows you to dynamically query and manage service configurations, such as enabling and disabling service configurations and throttling.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation** > **Management and control**
**service operation and maintenance** > **Basic Service Control**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Configuration Center**.
4. On the **Settings** tab, configuration information is listed by **Data Id** by default. You can
click **Advanced Filter** to query configuration information based on **Data Id** or **Group**. The configuration information is displayed in the following columns: Data Id Group Scenario tag Configuration Status Registered At nt service O&M
5. Find the configuration that you want to view and click **Details** in the Actions column to
view the details of the configuration.
6. On the **Operation Logs** tab, configuration information is listed by **status** by default. The
configuration information is displayed in the following columns: Basic Feature Status Type Created At Approved At Workflow ID

#### 1.1.3 Load Balancing Middleware

On the Load Balancing Middleware page, you can query the load balancing configurations of software and domain names and the status of backend server IP addresses.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation** > **Management and control**
**service operation and maintenance** > **Basic Service Control**.
nt service O&M
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Load Balancing Middleware**.
4. Data is listed by **domain name**. The information is displayed in the following columns:
Domain Name Scenario tag Configuration Status Registered At
5. Find the configuration that you want to view and click **Details** in the Actions column to
view the details of the load balancing configuration. nt service O&M

**Delete a scheduled job**

nt service O&M
1. Find the job that you want to delete and click Delete in the Actions column.
2. After you perform Step 1, a message appears. Click Create Delete Workflow Job in the
message.
3. After you perform Step 2, a dialog box appears. You need to review the information in the
dialog box. The ticket title and description are automatically generated. You can modify the title and description. Enter a reason for the change and click OK.
4. After you perform Step 3, the following message appears. You can follow the instructions to
view the approval information.
5. Follow the instructions in Step 4 to go to the corresponding page. Users who have
administrator permissions can approve the workflow on this page. After the workflow is approved, the O&M operation is performed and the job will be deleted.

**similar to the delete operation.**

### 1.2 CMDB

#### 1.2.1 Getting started

nt service O&M

##### 1.2.1.1 Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console

**Operations Console**

This topic describes how to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

**Prerequisites**

The endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console and the username and password used to log on to the console are obtained from the deployment engineer or an administrator. The endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console is in the following format: regi on-id.ops.console.intranet-domain-id. A web browser. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.
1. Open your browser.
2. In the address bar, enter the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
Press the Enter key. nt service O&M

> **Note:** You can click the current language in the upper-right corner to switch to another language. Simplified Chinese, English, and Traditional Chinese are supported.

3. Enter your username and password.

> **Note:** Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console from the deployment engineer or an administrator.

If you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console for the first time, you must change the password of your username. To enhance security, your password must meet the following requirements: The password contains uppercase and lowercase letters. The password contains digits. nt service O&M The password contains at least one of the following special characters: ! @ # $ % The password is 10 to 20 characters in length.
4. Click **Log On**.

##### 1.2.1.2 Go to the CMDB platform

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation** > **Management and control**
**service operation and maintenance** > **CMDB**.

#### 1.2.2 Overview

This topic describes the Overview page of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) platform.

**Data Dashboard**

Displays the statistics on models in the current CMDB platform and the detailed data. The following table describes the statistical metrics.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|

| psara Uni-manager Operati onsole | ons nce Operations Guide·Managem nt service O&M |
|---|---|

| Models | The total number of models in the current CMDB platform. |
|---|---|
| Model Associations | The total number of relationships among all models in the current CMDB platform. |
| Resource Instances | The total number of instance data rows in all models in the current CMDB platform. |
| Archived Instances | The number of instance data rows that have been archived in all models in the current CMDB platform. |
| Model Statistics | The number of all models in the current CMDB platform. |
| Statistics on Model Association Types | The statistics on the types of relationships among models. |
| Resource Instance Changes | The number of instances added, modified, or deleted within a specific time range. |
| Calls | The number of times internal and external systems call the API operations of CMDB. The data is collected for statistical analysis by caller and day. |

#### 1.2.3 Resource topology

Configuration Management Database (CMDB) provides resource-oriented management capabilities. You can query the resources of a single model and the resource topology among multiple models, and view resource change logs.

##### 1.2.3.1 Manage resources

On the Resource Management page, you can view the resources of a single model by model category.

**View resources**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. Go to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) platform.

### 1.3 Base Container O&M Platform

#### 1.3.1 Introduction to Base Container O&M Platform

**Platform**

This topic describes the background, basic capabilities, and design architecture of Base Container O&M Platform.

**Background**

In the past, the O&M system of Apsara Stack lacked a unified view from the perspective of containers. In a unified base, O&M personnel need to be familiar with the technical systems of both Apsara Infrastructure Management and Kubernetes, which leads to high O&M costs. In addition, the lack of a unified container profile makes it impossible for O&M personnel to gain a comprehensive view of containers. Data support cannot be provided for the evolution of container technologies in the future. Therefore, we designed Base Container O&M Platform to address the preceding pain points.

**Basic capabilities**

You can view the status of container engines of all machines where Apsara Infrastructure Management and PaaS are deployed from the global perspective. You can view the status of all container instances of all machines where Apsara Infrastructure Management and PaaS are deployed from the global perspective. You can use Base Container O&M Platform to collect the operational logs, stack traces, and performance analysis logs of container engines for specified machines with a few clicks. You can use Base Container O&M Platform to perform diagnostics on container engines and container instances with a few clicks, and the system automatically provides related KB documents for known issues. You can use Base Container O&M Platform to fix container engines and container instances with a few clicks. This way, known issues are automatically fixed.

#### 1.3.2 Overview

This topic describes the two modules of Base Container O&M Platform in order. The following figure shows how to log on to Base Container O&M Platform. In the top navigation bar of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console, choose Platform Operation > Management and control service operation and maintenance > Base Container O&M Platform. nt service O&M

##### 1.3.2.1 Container Engines

This topic describes the sections of the Container Engines page, including the container engine list, container engine diagnostics and fixing, and container engine log collection.
1. . Container engine list**
As shown in the following figure, the container engine list displays the machine name, architecture, status, engine version, and start time of container engines for all machines where Apsara Infrastructure Management and PaaS are deployed. You can also filter container engines by machine, status, and architecture to quickly obtain required information.
2. . Container engine diagnostics and fixing**

**Full diagnostics**

By default, the system automatically performs diagnostics on all container engines every 15 minutes. This means that the data in the list is refreshed every 15 minutes. If you want to manually perform diagnostics on all container engines, you can click the `Full diagnosis` button above the list to immediately perform diagnostics. Wait patiently because the full diagnostics takes a while. After the diagnostics process is complete, the list is automatically refreshed.

**Single diagnostics**

If you want to perform diagnostics only on a single container engine, you can click `Diagnosis` in the Operation column that corresponds to the container engine. After the diagnostics process is complete, the list is automatically refreshed.

**View diagnoses**

nt service O&M Diagnoses are provided only for abnormal container engines. Therefore, the `Processing` and `Ignore` options in the Operation column are unavailable for normal container engines. You can select To be repaired from the Status drop-down list above the container engine list to filter abnormal container engines. If you click `Ignore` in the Operation column that corresponds to a container engine, the information about the container engine is temporarily hidden. However, if the error of the container engine is identified in the next diagnostics, the information about the container engine will be displayed again. After you click Processing in the Operation column, you can view specific diagnoses which include diagnostics items, and fixing suggestions. You can also click `View KB` in the Operation column to download the corresponding KB document. Click `One-click repair` in the upper-right corner of the page to fix some known issues. The diagnosed issues may not be fixed. You can use only the automatic fix feature. For more information, see the related KB document.
3. . Container engine log collection**
nt service O&M On the Container Engines page, find the desired container engine and click `Log Collection` in the Operation column to go to the Container Engine log collection page. Click `Start` `collection` in the upper-right corner of the page to start log collection. After log collection is complete, the names, sizes, and download links of log files are displayed in the log File list section. The log Collection tab displays the operational logs of the engine process, the stack Collection tab displays the stack traces of the container engine process, and the pprof collection tab displays the performance logs of the container engine which include flame graphs and latency. Only the log Collection and stack Collection tabs allow you to preview the last 5,000 rows of collected logs. The pprof collection tab does not support preview, and pprof collection takes minutes because it needs to collect the running status of programs.

##### 1.3.2.2 Container Instances

This topic describes the sections of the Container Instances page, including the container instance list and container instance diagnostics and fixing.
1. . Container instance list**
As shown in the following figure, the container instance list displays the container ID, container name, status, service role, and machine of container instances for all machines where Apsara Infrastructure Management and PaaS deployed. You can also filter container instances by container ID, container name, machine, and status to quickly obtain the required information.
2. . Container instance diagnostics and fixing**

**Full diagnostics**

By default, the system automatically performs diagnostics on all container instances every 15 minutes. This means that the data in the list is refreshed every 15 minutes. If you want to manually perform diagnostics on all container instances, you can click the `Full diagnosis` button above the container instance list to immediately perform diagnostics. Wait patiently because the full diagnostics takes a while. After the diagnostics process is complete, the list is automatically refreshed.

**Single diagnostics**

nt service O&M If you want to perform diagnostics only on a single container instance, you can click `Diagnosis` in the Operation column that corresponds to the container instance. After the diagnostics process is complete, the list is automatically refreshed.

**View diagnoses**

Diagnoses are provided only for abnormal container instances. Therefore, the `Processing` and `Ignore` options in the Operation column are unavailable for normal container instances. You can select To be repaired from the Status drop-down list above the container instance list to filter abnormal container instances. If you click `Ignore` in the Operation column that corresponds to a container instance, the information about the container instance is temporarily hidden. However, if the error of the container instance is diagnosed in the next diagnostics, the information about the container instance will be displayed again. After you click Processing in the Operation column, you can view specific diagnoses which include diagnostics items, and fixing suggestions. You can also click `View KB` in the Operation column to download the corresponding KB document. Click `One-click repair` in the upper-right corner of the page to fix some known issues. The diagnosed issues may not be fixed. You can use only the automatic fix feature. For more information, see the related KB document. nt service O&M

#### 1.4.1 Temporary Throttling

**Create a throttling mode**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation** > **Management and control**
**service operation and maintenance** > **API O&M**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane of the **API O&M** platform, click **Temporary Throttling**.
4. Specify the **Gateway type**, **Status**, and **Operation type** parameters to search for the
desired throttling mode.
5. Click **Create a throttling mode**. In the Create a throttling mode dialog box, specify the
parameters that are described in the following table and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Gateway type | Select a gateway type. Valid values: POP OPSAPI |
| identifier | Select a throttling object. Valid values: Product dimension throttling API dimension throttling UID dimension throttling |

nt service O&M

| Product name | Select a service on which throttling is performed. |
|---|---|
| Operation type | Only FLOE CONTROL is available. _ |
| grad | Only QPS is available. |
| value | Enter the maximum queries per second (QPS) for the object. If the QPS of the object exceeds this value, excess requests will be rejected by the gateway. The value of the value parameter must be greater than 0. |
| Maximum Queue Time | Enter the maximum queue time. Unit: milliseconds. |

**Other operations**

**Modify a throttling mode**

1. Find the desired throttling mode and click **Edit** in the **Operation** column.
2. Modify the values of parameters and click **OK**.

> **Note:** You can modify only the value and Maximum Queue Time parameters.

**Enable a throttling mode**

1. Find the desired throttling mode and click **Start** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

> **Note:** You can enable throttling modes that are in the **Stopped** state.

**Disable a throttling mode**

1. Find the desired throttling mode and click **Stop** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**. A disabled throttling mode does not take effect.

> **Note:** You can disable throttling modes that are in the **Enabled** state.

**Delete a throttling mode**

1. Find the desired throttling mode and click **Delete** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

## 2 Disaster recovery management

#### management

### 2.1 ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery

**Recovery**

#### 2.1.1 ASR introduction

##### 2.1.1.1 What is Apsara Stack Resilience for Zone-disaster Recovery?

**disaster Recovery?**

Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR) for Zone-disaster Recovery consists of a primary site and a secondary site. The primary and secondary sites are deployed in the same region but in different zones. This deployment method is used to combat local disasters with a small impact. ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery is adopted on all core cloud products such as networking, cloud computing, database, storage, middleware, and big data products. This can be used in cross-AZ deployment for high availability. When a disaster occurs, your business can be quickly failed over to a secondary AZ. The service domain names of the cloud products remain unchanged. ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery can be deployed in two or three data centers in the same region.

##### 2.1.1.2 ASR deployment architecture

This topic describes the deployment architecture of Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR). ASR does not rely on other Apsara Stack services. When a data center fails, ASR can still provide services to ensure business continuity. An ASR system is deployed in each of the primary and secondary data centers to handle data center-level failures in different scenarios. The following figure shows the deployment architecture: covery management
1. ASR in the primary data center implements failovers when the secondary data center
encounters power and network outages or when split-brain issues occur in two data centers-based zone disaster recovery scenarios.
2. ASR in the secondary data center implements failovers when the primary data center
encounters power and network outages.

Failed: indicates that some monitoring items directly lead to the failures of forced switchovers. Risky: indicates that certain monitoring items may affect forced switchover. ##### 2.1.3.2 Platform monitoring

###### 2.1.3.2.1 Usage scenarios

This topic describes the usage scenarios of platform monitoring and precautions.

**Features**

Platform monitoring consists of three parts: product monitoring, synchronization monitoring, and ASR dashboard. These parts support the following features and check items: The Product Monitoring page displays the disaster recovery mode, service status in the primary, secondary, and quorum data centers, synchronization component status, and failover capabilities by product. The Synchronization Monitoring page displays the data synchronization latency compliance rates of databases and storage products. The ASR Dashboard page allows you to view the metrics of overall business continuity, such as the data synchronization latency compliance rates, drill duration, product status, and recent disaster recovery drills.

**Scenarios**

Routine monitoring: During the daily operations of the cloud platform, you need to regularly inspect various check items. Check before drills: Before switchover and switchback drills, you need to check platform monitoring information. Ensure that monitoring items do not have exceptions. For some products, you need to perform inspections in addition to the product monitoring check. Contact the ASR R&D team to perform inspections before a drill.

###### 2.1.3.2.2 Service monitoring

Before a switchover or switchback, the total number of products and the number of exceptions are counted by service type. The information about each product, node locations of base components, feature status, and inspection results are displayed in cards. If a product or base component is in an abnormal state, fix the issue before performing the switchover or switchback. covery management

**View the status of products**

If the exception persists after the services are deployed and reach the desired state, submit a ticket.

##### 2.1.3.3 Platform check

###### 2.1.3.3.1 Check an environment

This topic describes how to check a deployed environment. After a check, you can learn more about information such as the versions of disaster recovery services, service baselines, Domain Name System (DNS) resources, VIP resources, and database resources. Additionally, you can verify that all check items meet disaster recovery conditions. covery management
1. Log on to the ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery (Primary Zone) console or the ASR for Zone-
disaster Recovery (Secondary Zone) console. For more information, see Log on to the ASR console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Platform Check > Environment Check**.
3. On the **Environment Check** page, click **Check Now** in the upper-right corner of each
section to view corresponding check items. Check item descriptions:
**Product Configuration Upgrade**: After services are redeployed or service
configurations are upgraded, rolling must be performed on the services in the primary data center so that ASR can obtain the latest configurations of the data center. Check whether the list of products with configuration upgrades is consistent with the products that are redeployed or whose configurations are upgraded.
**Cluster Deployment**: displays whether products are deployed in symmetric mode,
based on which you can learn about the clusters where the products are deployed.

> **Note:** Feature in yellow: This feature is deployed in asymmetric mode but is not required for the secondary cluster. This information can be ignored.
> Feature in red: This feature is deployed in asymmetric mode and is required for the secondary cluster. You need to resolve the issue.

**Product Version**: ASR checks whether the versions of products are consistent between
the primary and secondary data centers. If the versions are inconsistent, ASR shows that the products are abnormal. You must upgrade the product versions to ensure that the versions are the same between the primary and secondary data centers. This way, failover failures caused by inconsistent product versions are prevented. covery management
**Product Baseline**: ASR checks whether the baseline configurations in the environment
are the same as the baseline configurations in Apsara Infrastructure Management. If ASR returns a message indicating check passed, the baseline check is successful. If ASR returns a message indicating check failed, check the relevant configurations.
**DNS Resources**: ASR obtains the DNS resource information of services from Apsara
Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR obtains a VIP that maps a domain name from the resource information, and compares the actual VIP with the VIP obtained from the resource information in Apsara Infrastructure Management. If the two VIPs are inconsistent, the value of the **Comparison Result** column is **Abnormal**. Check and modify corresponding configurations.
**VIP Resources**: ASR obtains the VIP resource information of products from Apsara
Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR queries the actual IP address of a server that corresponds to the VIP from Server Load Balancer (SLB) based on the VIP in resource information, and compares the actual IP address of the server with the list of node controllers (NCs) in the VIP resource information. If the actual IP address and the list of NCs are inconsistent, ASR marks the corresponding RealServer IP value in red. Check and modify corresponding configurations. covery management
**Database Resources**: ASR obtains the database resource information of products from
Apsara Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR connects to the database based on the information and checks the read-only attribute of the primary database. If the primary database is read-only, the value of the **Status** column of the service is **Abnormal** in the ASR console. Modify the configurations of the database.
**Conditions of the Network Between Data Centers** : ASR checks whether switches
can advertise routes of SLB and CIDR blocks of virtual private cloud (VPCs). If abnormalities exist, contact O&M engineers. covery management
**BGP Route**: ASR checks whether switches can advertise routes of OPS-DNS, Apsara
Stack DNS, SLB, and VPC and whether the routes are propagated to Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peers. If abnormalities exist, contact O&M engineers.

##### 2.1.3.4 Disaster recovery drills

You can perform disaster recovery drills to switch over or back services between the primary and secondary data centers when no power or network outages occur.

###### 2.1.3.4.1 Usage notes

Disaster recovery drills are classified into two types: custom drills and predefined drills. Custom drills allow you to select one or more products to perform drills based on your needs. Predefined drills allow you to select all products or a single product to perform drills.

**Overview**

Zone-disaster recovery drills are an important part of the delivery acceptance and periodic inspection of the disaster recovery platform. By performing disaster recovery drills on a regular basis, you can test the capabilities of the disaster recovery platform to handle major issues and improve the disaster recovery response mechanism. If any problems occur during a drill, contact the Apsara Stack disaster recovery R&D team immediately to solve the problems, thereby avoiding affecting the normal operation of your business. Custom drills: You can select multiple services to create and run drill plans based on your requirements. Predefined drills: You can select a service drill plan predefined on ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery or select the overall drill plan that includes all services.

> **Note:** In a scenario where three data centers are deployed, ASR allows you to switch the primary database of your instance back to the zone where the database resides during instance creation, including but not limited to **service switchback after single-service** **faults** and **service switchback after power outages**.

You can select a single product or all products to perform a predefined drill.

##### 2.1.3.5 Disaster recovery

covery management This topic describes disaster recovery. It ensures continuous operation or quick recovery to the running state after natural disasters, system faults, or other emergencies. It is suitable for scenarios where a cloud platform disaster occurs. If no disasters occur, you can use the fault injection feature of ASR and then perform disaster recovery for drills.

**Features**

**Disaster recovery** refers to quickly recover a cloud platform and its business systems in
the event of major faults or disasters. It is designed to ensure continuous operation or quick recovery to the running state after natural disasters, system faults or other emergencies.
**Fault simulation** refers to inject faults for simulating power, network, and split-brain
outage scenarios in data centers.

> **Note:** In a scenario where three data centers are deployed, ASR allows you to switch the primary database of your instance back to the zone where the database resides during instance creation, including but not limited to **service switchback after single-service** **faults** and **service switchback after power outages**.

###### 2.1.3.5.1 Disaster recovery

This topic describes disaster recovery. Disaster recovery refers to quickly recover a cloud platform and its business systems in the event of major faults or disasters. It is designed to ensure continuous operation or quick recovery to the running state after natural disasters, system faults or other emergencies.

**Scenarios**

Disaster recovery has the following scenarios: Power outage recovery in the primary data center: If the primary data center is powered off, cloud services in the secondary and third data centers are started to quickly recover online business. Network outage recovery in the primary data center: If the external networks and ones connected to the secondary and third data centers fail in the primary data center, services in the secondary and third data centers are started to ensure business continuity. Single-service fault recovery: If a service in the primary data center fails, the corresponding services in the secondary and third data centers are started. This does not guarantee zero data loss. Fault recovery in the secondary data center: If the secondary data center is powered off, cloud services in the primary and third data centers are started to quickly recover online business.

**Flowchart**

covery management You must manually perform platform switchover and switchback operations during disaster recovery. However, after the arbitration feature is enabled, automatic arbitration switchover capabilitiesare supported for the base middleware service(including Zookeeper, Tair, and Schedulerx middleware components), quickly recovering online business.

**data center**

3. Click the **Power Outage Recovery** tab.
covery management

**primary data center**

This topic describes how to perform platform switchover and switchback in the ASR for Zonedisaster Recovery console to ensure system continuity and reliability when network outages occur in a real primary data center. Failover for network outages of the primary data center This topic describes how to start cloud services in the secondary data center when the primary data center is disconnected from both the Internet and the secondary data center. This ensures business continuity.

Zone) console. For more information, see the "Escape logon scenarios" section in Log on to the ASR console.

###### 2.1.3.5.2 Fault simulation

Fault simulation is a testing and verification technique used to evaluate the resilience of a cloud platform in the event of a fault or disaster. It simulates potential system faults by artificially introducing faults to observe and analyze the disaster recovery process of the cloud platform.

**Flowchart**

From the perspective of the deployment modes, zone-disaster recovery scenarios can be divided into two data centers and three data centers. The following fault scenarios may be involved:

**Fault scenarios of two data centers**

Power outage: The entire power facility of the primary or secondary data center is faulty, no UPS is available, and all devices are powered off. covery management Network outage: The network devices, optical fibers, or leased lines of the primary or secondary data center for external connections are faulty. Therefore, the data center cannot communicate with external systems outside the cloud. Split-brain: The leased lines or optical fibers between the primary and secondary data centers are faulty. As a result, the primary and secondary data centers cannot communicate with each other. Single-product fault: A product in the primary or secondary data center is faulty and in the abnormal state.

**Fault scenarios of three data centers**

Power outage: The entire power facility of the primary, secondary, or quorum data center is faulty, no UPS is available, and all devices are powered off. Network outage: The network devices, optical fibers, or leased lines of the primary, secondary, or quorum data center for external connections are faulty. Therefore, the data center cannot communicate with external systems outside the cloud. Single-connection failure: One of the three data centers fails to communicate with the other two data centers. Single-product fault: A product in the primary, secondary, or quorum data center is faulty and in the abnormal state. covery management

> **Note:** Fault simulation refers to manually inject fault types similar to (but not) real disasters in a data center. It is used to verify disaster recovery capabilities and help business personnel quickly get familiar with disaster recovery services.

#### 2.1.4 System settings

##### 2.1.4.1 Monitoring center

###### 2.1.4.1.1 Check an environment

This topic describes how to check a deployed environment. After a check, you can learn more about information such as the versions of disaster recovery services, service baselines, Domain Name System (DNS) resources, VIP resources, and database resources. Additionally, you can verify that all check items meet disaster recovery conditions.
1. Log on to the ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery (Primary Zone) console or the ASR for Zone-
disaster Recovery (Secondary Zone) console. For more information, see Log on to the ASR console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Platform Check > Environment Check**.
3. On the **Environment Check** page, click **Check Now** in the upper-right corner of each
section to view corresponding check items. Check item descriptions:
**Product Configuration Upgrade**: After services are redeployed or service
configurations are upgraded, rolling must be performed on the services in the primary data center so that ASR can obtain the latest configurations of the data center. Check whether the list of products with configuration upgrades is consistent with the products that are redeployed or whose configurations are upgraded.
**Cluster Deployment**: displays whether products are deployed in symmetric mode,
based on which you can learn about the clusters where the products are deployed.

> **Note:** Feature in yellow: This feature is deployed in asymmetric mode but is not required for the secondary cluster. This information can be ignored.
> Feature in red: This feature is deployed in asymmetric mode and is required for the secondary cluster. You need to resolve the issue.

covery management
**Product Version**: ASR checks whether the versions of products are consistent between
the primary and secondary data centers. If the versions are inconsistent, ASR shows that the products are abnormal. You must upgrade the product versions to ensure that the versions are the same between the primary and secondary data centers. This way, failover failures caused by inconsistent product versions are prevented.
**Product Baseline**: ASR checks whether the baseline configurations in the environment
are the same as the baseline configurations in Apsara Infrastructure Management. If ASR returns a message indicating check passed, the baseline check is successful. If ASR returns a message indicating check failed, check the relevant configurations.
**DNS Resources**: ASR obtains the DNS resource information of services from Apsara
Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR obtains a VIP that maps a domain name from the resource information, and compares the actual VIP with the VIP obtained from the resource information in Apsara Infrastructure Management. If the two VIPs are inconsistent, the value of the **Comparison Result** column is **Abnormal**. Check and modify corresponding configurations. covery management
**VIP Resources**: ASR obtains the VIP resource information of products from Apsara
Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR queries the actual IP address of a server that corresponds to the VIP from Server Load Balancer (SLB) based on the VIP in resource information, and compares the actual IP address of the server with the list of node controllers (NCs) in the VIP resource information. If the actual IP address and the list of NCs are inconsistent, ASR marks the corresponding RealServer IP value in red. Check and modify corresponding configurations.
**Database Resources**: ASR obtains the database resource information of products from
Apsara Infrastructure Management. Then, ASR connects to the database based on the information and checks the read-only attribute of the primary database. If the primary database is read-only, the value of the **Status** column of the service is **Abnormal** in the ASR console. Modify the configurations of the database. covery management
**Conditions of the Network Between Data Centers** : ASR checks whether switches
can advertise routes of SLB and CIDR blocks of virtual private cloud (VPCs). If abnormalities exist, contact O&M engineers.
**BGP Route**: ASR checks whether switches can advertise routes of OPS-DNS, Apsara
Stack DNS, SLB, and VPC and whether the routes are propagated to Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peers. If abnormalities exist, contact O&M engineers. covery management

3. Click **Check Now** in the upper-right corner of the **Server Load Balancer**, **OpsDNS**, or
**MiniRDS** section to check the status of each product.

After leased lines are configured, the network traffic between the devices in data centers is displayed on the **Overview** page. This allows you to view data transmission between the devices in different data centers. covery management

**Prerequisites**

Leased lines are created before you perform a batch import. To create a leased line, perform the following steps: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. Then, choose
**Product Operation > Networking > Network Operations Console** to go to the
**Network Operations Console**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network >**
**Leased Line Management > Leased Line Instances** to create a leased line.
1. Log on to the ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery (Primary Zone) console or the ASR for Zone-
disaster Recovery (Secondary Zone) console. For more information, see Log on to the ASR console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Settings > Leased Line Management**.
3. Add leased line information.
Adds a single leased line. a. Click **Create Leased Line**. covery management b. Configure the parameters, which are described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description | Parameter configuration |
|---|---|---|
| Current Device | Indicates the name of the local device for data transmission. | User-defined. Example: ISW- VM-G1-1.AMTEST82. |
| Current Port | Indicates the number of the outbound or inbound port on the local device for data transmission. | User-defined. Example: 10GE1/0/6. |
| Peer Device | Indicates the name of the peer device for data transmission. | User-defined. Example: ISW- VM-G1-1.AMTEST82. |
| Peer Port | Indicates the number of the outbound or inbound port on the peer device for data transmission. | User-defined. Example: 10GE1/0/6. |
| Current Data Center | Indicates the name of the data center where the local device resides. | User-defined. Example: amtest1. |
| Peer Data Center | Indicates the name of the data center where the peer device resides. | User-defined. Example: amtest2. |
| Bandwidth (Mbit/s) | Indicates the maximum rate of direct data transmission between the local and peer devices. Unit: Mbit/s. | Enter a value based on the actual data transmission rate. Example: 100. |

c. Click **OK**. Add leased lines in batches. a. Click **Import**. b. In the **Import Leased Line** dialog box, select the leased lines that you want to add. c. Click **OK**.

###### 2.1.4.2.2 Arbitration management

In the standard three-data-center deployment scenario, the arbitration service detects whether a real data center-level fault occurs. If so, the arbitration service determines whether the current conditions are met to initiate arbitration switchover and then switches the products and base to a normal data center.

**Constraints**

The arbitration switchover is subject to the following constraints: When the arbitration switchover fails, the arbitration service does not perform a switchover retry and requires human intervention. When the original data center is recovered, the arbitration service does not automatically switch back to the original data center.

**Arbitration process**

Before the arbitration switchover is executed, the arbitration service performs the detection. The following figure shows the entire process of the arbitration service: covery management
1. On the **Arbitration Management** page, you can enable the arbitration service. After ASR
for Zone-disaster Recovery determines that the data center is normal, the arbitration service is enabled.
2. The arbitration service performs the following steps in the detection:
i. Whether the heartbeat of the node service in each data center is normal: If the heartbeat is detected, the data center is normal and the detection ends. If no heartbeat is detected, the next step is performed. ii. Reference product inspection. If exceptions are detected during the inspection of Apsara Infrastructure Management, perform the next step. For more information, see Monitor products. Otherwise, the detection ends. iii. Arbitrated product inspection. If exceptions are detected during the inspection of the middleware service, perform the next detection. Otherwise, the detection ends. iv. ISW connectivity check. covery management
3. When the detection of the arbitration service ends, the arbitration decision phase starts.
The arbitration switchover is initiated only after the following conditions are met: The product in the data center is normal. The RPO of the product is lower than the specified maximum tolerance value. The specified number of arbitration detections is reached.
4. Arbitration switchover: After the arbitration conditions are met, ASR for Zone-disaster
Recovery forcibly switches over the arbitrated product. After the switchover is completed, the prompt is displayed on the page.
5. Wait for the data center recovery: After the arbitration switchover is completed, you must
recover the faulty data center. The entire arbitration process ends after the arbitration service detects that the data center is recovered. However, the arbitration service is still enabled. You must manually disable the arbitration service.

**Prerequisites**

ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery services of the primary and secondary data centers run normally. The inspection results of the arbitration service are normal. The ISW connectivity check of each data center is normal.
1. Log on to the ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery (Primary Zone) console or the ASR for Zone-
disaster Recovery (Secondary Zone) console. For more information, see the "escape logon scenarios" section in Log on to the ASR console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane of the **ASR for Zone-disaster Recovery** console, choose
**System Settings > Arbitration Management**.
3. On the **Arbitration Management** page, click **Create Arbitration**. Then, perform the
following steps to configure the parameters to enable the arbitration service.
4. Select a product for arbitration in the **Arbitrated Products** line. Only the selected product
can be forcibly switched over after it is determined that arbitration is required.

> **Note:** By default, the base middleware service is selected.

5. In the **ISW Information** line, click **Add ISW** to add the ISWs of the primary data center,
secondary data center, and third data centers in sequence.
6. In the **Service Execution Attempts** line, specify the number of service inspections. You
can enter an integer that ranges from 1 to 5.
7. If you click **Enable Arbitration**, the system immediately performs a detection. If the
success message is displayed, the arbitration service is enabled. covery management

> **Note:** The data center will be powered off when the data center is relocated. To prevent automatic switchover initiated by the arbitration service, you must disable the arbitration service before the data center is relocated.

**Other operations**

After the arbitration service is enabled, you can perform the following operations:

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Modify arbitration | 1. On the Arbitration Management page, click Modify Arbitration. 2. Modify the Execution Attempts parameter or ISW information and click Submit. |
| Disable Arbitration | 1. On the Arbitration Management page, click Disable Arbitration. 2. In the message that appears, click OK. |

| Enable Alert Threshold | Specifies whether to enable the alert threshold. You can enable this feature and specify a threshold. #### 2.1.5 Appendix

##### 2.1.5.1 Encryption and backup

Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR) ensures the security of user data by using key encryption and offline backup. ASR generates audit logs to record system security events and activities, prevent internal data misuse, track suspicious behaviors, and identify potential security threats and attacks. Key encryption: ASR stores logon passwords in the database by using the MD5 algorithm. covery management Other data such as configurations and personnel information is not encrypted. Audit logs: ASR sends operation logs to Apsara Stack Security for auditing. Logs are stored in SLS-Inner. Docker logs are not backed up. Offline backup: ASR uses mysqldump to back up database data offline every 12 hours. The backup data is stored in Object Storage Service (OSS) and deleted after 5 days.

covery management

> **Note:** Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Operations Console from a deployment engineer or an administrator.

If you enter an invalid password for three consecutive times, the system enables the image verification logon feature. If you enter an invalid password for five consecutive times, the account is locked. Contact the administrator to unlock the account.

#### 2.2.2 Homepage

The homepage of the ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery O&M console displays information in the following sections: Authorization usage statistics, Node task load statistics, Total number of abnormal synchronization entities, Unassigned task statistics, Bandwidth Usage, and Dedicated Line traffic usage.

> **Important:** When deploying the ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery O&M console, you must also configure information about the instances that are connected over Express Connect circuits. Otherwise, instance data cannot be displayed in the line charts on the homepage.
> To configure Express Connect circuit-connected instance information, contact Apsara Stack engineers.

covery management

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Authorization usage statistics | Displays the usage of protection groups and synchronization entities in a doughnut chart. The blue color indicates the usage of protection groups. The yellow color indicates the usage of synchronization entities. The numerator represents the used quota and the denominator represents the total authorized quota. |
| Node task load statistics | Displays the number of tasks distributed on each ASR for Geo- disaster Recovery node in a doughnut chart. |
| Total number of abnormal synchronization entities | Displays the number of abnormal synchronization entities based on the statistics of disaster recovery services in a doughnut chart. |
| Unassigned task statistics | Displays the unassigned synchronization tasks in a doughnut chart. |
| Bandwidth Usage | Displays the traffic and bandwidth usage of ApsaraDB RDS and Object Storage Service (OSS) in line charts. |
| Dedicated Line traffic usage | Displays the inbound and outbound traffic usage of the instances that are connected over Express Connect circuits to ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery in line charts. |

covery management

#### 2.2.3 Disaster recovery monitoring

##### 2.2.3.1 View the cloud platform monitoring

Cloud platform monitoring is designed to monitor the disaster recovery status of cloud services, including metrics such as service availability, domain name resolution, and network access. It allows you to quickly switch your cloud platform to another region when a region fails, thereby ensuring business continuity.
1. Log in to the Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR) for Geo-disaster Recovery console from the
Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Disaster Recovery Monitoring** > **Cloud**
**Platform Monitoring**.
3. Select a value from the Disaster Recovery Interconnection drop-down list to view the
service inspection information in the selected interconnected regions. covery management
4. Move the pointer over a service to view the check details of the service.
5. Click **View More**. In the panel that appears, view the details of check items.

##### 2.2.3.2 View the protection group monitoring

This topic describes how to view the check results of synchronization entities in a protection group. covery management
1. Log in to the Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR) for Geo-disaster Recovery console from the
Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Disaster Recovery Monitoring** > **Protection**
**Group Status Monitoring**.
3. Find the protection group that you want to view and click **View Check Results** in the
Actions column. In the panel that appears, view the following information about each synchronization entity in the protection group: synchronization entity name, cloud service, synchronization status, synchronization latency, primary instance status, secondary instance status, and the time when the check was performed.

##### 2.2.4.2 Manage a disaster recovery interconnection

**interconnection**

This topic describes how to create an interconnection between regions to implement crossregion disaster recovery.
1. Log in to the Apsara Stack Resilience (ASR) for Geo-disaster Recovery console from the
Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **General > Disaster Recovery Interconnection**
**Management**.
3. On the Disaster recovery Interconnection Management page, click **New Disaster**
**Recovery interconnection**. In the dialog box that appears, configure parameters as
prompted. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Disaster recovery interconnection name | The name for the disaster recovery interconnection. You can specify a custom name. |
| Description | The description of the disaster recovery interconnection. |
| Regions with Disaster Recovery Interconnections Configured | The regions to be interconnected for disaster recovery. Specify at least two regions, one as the primary region, the other as the secondary region. |
| Services with Disaster Recovery Interconnections Configured | The cloud services for disaster recovery interconnection. The system automatically identifies the cloud services that support disaster recovery in the specified interconnected regions. Use the default value. |

4. Click **Submit**.

**What to do next**

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

covery management

| Start interconnection | Click Unicom in the Operation column of the disaster recovery interconnection. If the interconnection fails, click Retry to perform a reconnection. |
|---|---|
| View details of the disaster recovery interconnection | Click Details in the Operation column of the disaster recovery interconnection. In the dialog box that appears, view the basic information and connection status of the services in the interconnected regions. |
| Modify the disaster recovery interconnection | 1. Click Edit in the Operation column of the disaster recovery interconnection. 2. In the dialog box that appears, modify settings as needed, and then click Submit. |
| Delete the disaster recovery interconnection | 1. Click Delete in the Operation column of the disaster recovery interconnection. 2. In the message that appears, click OK. |

##### 2.2.4.3 Manage a disaster recovery gateway

This topic describes how to configure peer gateway information across clouds to establish a disaster recovery relationship and a network connection between two cross-cloud ends.

**Background information**

For security purpose, API operations in control domains cannot be called across clouds. They are encapsulated and registered into POP to form an independent disaster recovery gateway, improving API operation management efficiency and providing API operations for other disaster recovery services.
1. Log on to the ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Platform O&M > Disaster Recovery**
**Gateway**. The disaster recovery regions among which a disaster recovery relationship is
established are displayed.
3. Click **Add ACL** to configure the requester information as described in the following table,
and then click **Next**. covery management Access Control List (ACL) defines and manages inbound and outbound data packets to ensure that network traffic meets security policies and access control requirements.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Requester Product | The cloud service that you want to connect to the requester cloud. Example: ASR for Geo- disaster Recovery. |
| Requester CIDR Block | The CIDR block where the API operation of the requester cloud service resides. It is in the format of *.*.*.*/mask. Example: 192.168.1.0/24. |
| Requester UID | The UID of the AccessKey pair of the requester user. You can obtain the UID from user information in the requester. |

4. In the **Manage Action Permissions** step, select services in the destination end and then
click **Next**.
5. Click **Submit**.

**Related operations**

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

covery management

| View the ACL. | 1. Click View ACL in the Actions column corresponding to a region. 2. Click Details in the Actions column. |
|---|---|
| Modify ACL | 1. Click View ACL in the Actions column corresponding to a region. 2. Click Modify in the Actions column. 3. Select another action and then click Submit. |
| Delete ACL | 1. Click View ACL in the Actions column corresponding to a region. 2. Click Delete in the Actions column. 3. In the message that appears, click OK. |

##### 2.2.4.4 Configure a dashboard map

This topic describes how to configure disaster recovery regions displayed on a dashboard. After configuration, the geo-disaster recovery data is displayed on the dashboard.

**Scenarios**

**Geo-disaster recovery**: This solution is widely used in industries such as public services,
energy, transportation, and health and medical insurance. This solution is applicable to the following scenarios: High business continuity is required. Strong data consistency is not required. Regional fault prevention is required. The distance between regions is more than 100 km.
**Three data centers across two regions** : This solution is mainly used in the financial
industry and is applicable to the following scenarios: Prevention of city-level natural disasters is required. Regional fault prevention is required. Near zero synchronization latencies for business-critical data are required. The budget is adequate.
1. Log on to the ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Platform O&M > > Dashboard Map**
**Configuration**.
3. On the Dashboard Map Configuration page, click **Create Disaster Recovery Region**. In
the Create Disaster Recovery Region dialog box, configure the parameters described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

covery management

| Region ID | The ID of the region that you want to use. |
|---|---|
| Region Name | The name of the region. Example: Hangzhou data center. |
| City | The city in which the region resides. |
| Zone | The zone of the region. The system automatically generates zone names. |

4. Click **OK**.

**Related operations**

After you create a disaster recovery region, you can also perform the operations described in the following table.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Query the disaster recovery region | Enter region and zone names, and select a city from the drop-down list. The system automatically filters the matched disaster recovery region. |
| Edit the disaster recovery region | 1. Find the disaster recovery region and click Edit in the Actions column. 2. In the Edit Disaster Recovery Region dialog box, enter a new region name or select another city. 3. Click OK. |
| Delete the disaster recovery region | 1. Find the disaster recovery region and click Delete in the Actions column. 2. In the message that appears, click OK. |

#### 2.2.5 Disaster recovery O&M

This topic describes the disaster recovery O&M features of ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery. The disaster recovery O&M features of ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery are categorized into the synchronization entity management and plan management modules. The following table describes the modules.

| Module |   | Description | Remark |
|---|---|---|---|

covery management

| Synchronization entity management |   | You can view the list and details of protection groups, delete the protection groups and synchronization entities that you no longer need, view the tasks of each synchronization entity, view the step details of each task, view the run logs of each step, retry a step, and skip a step. | If a step of a task fails, you can retry the step. This way, the task continues to be run from this step. If a step of a task fails multiple times, you can skip the step. This is applicable if the skipped step does not affect subsequent steps. This way, the task continues to be run from the next step. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plan management | Drill switchover | You can view the records of drill plans and disaster recovery plans that are run, unbind the plans that are run, view the details and step details of each record, view the running logs of each step, retry a step, skip a step, and skip all steps. | If a step of a plan fails multiple times, you can skip all optional steps. Note This operation is generally performed when the primary site fails. In this case, all steps related to the primary site are skipped at a time. |
|   | Drill switchback |   |   |

##### 2.2.5.2 Perform a site switchover drill

This topic describes how to associate disaster recovery plans with a switchover drill that simulates the scenario in which all devices at the primary site fail and all business needs to be switched over to the secondary site. During the switchover drill, the associated disaster recovery plans are executed.

**Prerequisites**

A disaster recovery plan is created. For more information, see Create a business disaster recovery plan.
1. Log on to the O&M console of ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery (ASR-DR).
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Disaster Recovery > Site Disaster Recovery**
**Drill**.
3. Associate one or more disaster recovery plans with the site switchover.
i. On the Site Switchover page, click **Bind Disaster Recovery Plan**. ii. In the Bind Disaster Recovery Plan dialog box, select one or more disaster recovery plans that you want to associate with the site switchover. iii. Click **OK**. The associated disaster recovery plans are displayed on the **Site Switchover** page.
4. Set the execution order.
i. Move the pointer over the number in the Execution Sequence column of a plan and click the icon. ii. Enter an integer from 0 to 9 in the Execution Sequence field. A smaller value indicates a higher execution priority. The plans that have the same priority are executed at the same time. iii. Click **OK**.
5. Start the disaster recovery plans.
i. In the upper-right corner of the Site Switchover page, click **Start All Failovers**. ii. In the Start All Failovers message, click **OK**. iii. All plans start to be executed to switch business from the primary site to the secondary site. iv. After all plans are executed, the plans are ready to be executed for a failback. You can click **Start Failback** to switch business from the secondary site to the primary site. v. After all plans are executed for the failback, the business at the primary site works as expected.

**Related operations**

On the Site Switchover page, you can also perform the operations described in the following table. covery management

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| View plan details | 1. Click the name of a plan to go to the plan details page. 2. View the details of the plan on the following tabs: On the Plan Steps tab, view the execution steps of the plan. On the Progress tab, view the failover progress. To terminate the failover, click Terminate. In the message that appears, confirm the task that you want to terminate and click Terminate Failover. If an exception occurs but the error does not affect the failover, click Force Pass. In the message that appears, click Force Pass. On the Associated Protection Group tab, view the protection groups that are associated with the plan and the instances in each protection group. On the Historical Records tab, view the overview of the switchover drill in the following sections: Drill Success Rate, Protection Group Failover Success Rate, Protection Group Failback Success Rate, Synchronization Latency Compliance Rate, Failover Duration Compliance Rate, and Failback Duration Compliance Rate. |
| View a failover summary | On the Historical Records tab of the plan details page, find a failover and click View Drill Summary in the Actions column. |
| Download a failover summary report | On the Historical Records tab of the plan details page, find a failover and click Download Report in the Actions column to save the failover report to your computer. |
| Disassociate one or more disaster recovery plans from the site switchover | Disassociate multiple disaster recovery plans at a time i. On the Site Switchover page, select the disaster recovery plans that you want to disassociate from the site switchover. ii. In the lower part of the page, click Unbind. iii. In the Start All Failovers message, click OK. Disassociate a single disaster recovery plan i. On the Site Switchover page, find the disaster recovery plan that you want to disassociate from the site switchover and click Unbind in the Actions column. ii. In the Unbind Independent Disaster Recovery message, click OK. |

##### 2.2.6.1 Create an independent disaster recovery plan

**plan**

After an independent disaster recovery plan is created, you can perform failovers and switchover drills by using ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery (ASR-DR) only at the secondary site.

**Prerequisites**

ASR-DR is purchased and deployed at the primary site. The independent disaster recovery feature of ASR-DR is enabled for the primary and secondary sites.

2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Independent Disaster Recovery**.

**Recovery**. In the Create Independent Disaster Recovery dialog box, specify the Disaster
Recovery Cloud and Disaster Recovery Region parameters.
4. Click **Create and Configure**. If you want to configure disaster recovery parameters later,
click **Create**.
5. Click **Verify** to verify the input values.
6. After the verification is passed, click **Create and Configure**. You can also click **Create**
and complete the configurations later.

covery management

##### 2.2.6.2 Perform a failover

If a secondary site fails when the site is used to provide services, you can switch the business back to the primary site by using the independent disaster recovery feature. This topic describes how to perform a failover in the O&M console of ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery (ASR-DR). This topic also describes how to view the failover steps and progress.

**Background information**

When a site-level fault, such as network disconnection or power outage, occurs in your secondary site when the site provides services, you can switch the business back to the primary site by using the independent disaster recovery feature. This way, your business continuity is not affected.

**Prerequisites**

An independent disaster recovery plan is created and configured. For more information, see Create an independent disaster recovery plan.
1. Log on to the O&M console of ASR-DR at the secondary site.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Independent Disaster Recovery**.
3. Perform a failover by using one of the following methods:
Find the independent disaster recovery plan that you want to manage and click **Failover** in the **Actions** column. Find the independent disaster recovery plan that you want to manage and click **View**
**Details** in the **Actions** column. On the page that appears, click **Start Failover** in the
Failover section of the Switching Steps tab. covery management
4. After the failover is started, log on to the O&M console of ASR-DR from the primary site and
view the steps and progress of the failover. For more information, see View the details of an independent disaster recovery plan.

##### 2.2.6.3 Perform a switchover drill

If ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery (ASR-DR) is deployed on the secondary cloud and your business is switched over to run on the secondary cloud, the business cannot be switched back to the primary cloud when the secondary cloud fails. To resolve this issue, ASR-DR provides the independent disaster recovery feature. You can perform a switchover drill to increase the success rate of a failover.

**Background information**

When a site-level fault, such as network disconnection or power outage, occurs in your secondary site when the site provides services, you can switch the business back to the primary site by using the independent disaster recovery feature. This way, your business continuity is not affected.

**Prerequisites**

An independent disaster recovery plan is created. For more information, see Create an independent disaster recovery task.
1. Log in to the O&M console of ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery at the secondary site.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Independent Disaster Recovery**.
3. Perform a switchover drill by using one of the following methods:
Find the independent disaster recovery plan that you want to manage and click **Drill**
**Switchover** in the **Actions** column.
Find the independent disaster recovery plan that you want to manage and click **View**
**Details** in the **Actions** column. On the Independent Disaster Recovery Details page, click
**Start Drill Switchover** in the Drill Switchover section on the Switching Steps tab.
covery management
4. After the switchover drill is started, log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console
from the primary site and view the steps and progress of the switchover drill. For more information, see View the details of an independent disaster recovery plan.

 services/dnsService/user/dns.conf  file.

##### 2.2.7.2 Configure DNS forwarding

When you set up a primary-secondary disaster recovery system between two clouds, you must configure Domain Name System (DNS) at the primary and secondary sites. Make sure that DNS queries can be smoothly forwarded across the system. This topic describes how to configure DNS forwarding.

**Important**

To configure DNS forwarding from opsDns to dnsProduct at the primary site, you must modify the tianji configuration file and roll update the tianji cluster. The risk of automated configuration is high. We recommend that you manually perform the configuration modification and roll update. Automate the configuration of other settings.

**Prerequisites**

covery management A network connection is established between the primary and secondary sites. The primary site is successfully deployed and the DNS configuration file is generated in the container.

> **Note:** If the prerequisites are not met, see the "Manually configure DNS forwarding" section in this topic.

**Automate configuration of DNS forwarding at the two sites**

1. Obtain the AccessKey ID (AK) and AccessKey secret (SK) and pop_ops_vip of the operations
administrator at the primary site. i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console as an operations administrator. ii. Click in the upper-right corner of the page and then click **User Information**. iii. Obtain the AK and SK of the operations administrator. iv. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**
**Management > Resource Management**.
v. On the **Product & Cluster O&M** page, enter webappAll in the search box to find the StandardCloudCluster cluster. vi. Click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column of the StandardCloudCluster cluster. On the cluster details page, click **Resource Details**. covery management vii. View the pop-vip-ops resource details and click the value in the Resource Application Result column to obtain and save the value of vip_ip.

> **Note:** If the pop-vip-ops of the primary site changes, you must roll update the asrdr cluster of the primary site again.

Run the following command in the ASR-DR container of the secondary site: Replace pop_vip_ops, ops_admin_ak, ops_admin_sk with the values obtained in the preceding steps. The DNS forwarding rules and IP address whitelists from the primary site to the secondary site are configured, and the DNS forwarding rules and IP address whitelists from the secondary site to the primary site are configured.

```
python alidata/bin/dns/auto_config_dns.py asrdr -v {pop_vip_ops} -a {ops_admin_ak} -s {ops_admin_sk}
```

viii. Obtain the content of the /home/admin/asrdr/config/dns/dns_conf.{regionId}.ops file of the local ASR-DR container.
2. Add a forwarding rule from OPS-DNS to DNS of the local cloud tenant.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**
**Management > Resource Management**.
iii. On the **Product & Cluster O&M** page, enter tianji in the search box to search for the tianji cluster. iv. Click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column of the cluster. On the cluster details page, click **Desired State Configuration**. covery management v. Enter dns_zone.conf.jj2 in the search box on the left and click Show Content to add the dns_conf.{regionId}.ops content obtained in Step 1 to the file. Content format:

```
zone_forwarders:
  -zone: the Internet domain of the peer cloud
    forwarders:
    - the DNS nameserver address of the local cloud tenant
    - the DNS nameserver address of the local cloud tenant
  -zone: the intranet domain of the peer cloud
    forwarders:
    - the DNS nameserver address of the local cloud tenant
    - the DNS nameserver address of the local cloud tenant
```

vi. Click **Preview and Submit**. vii. Click **Cluster Rolling**. viii. After the tianji cluster is rolled, use one of the following methods for the tianji configuration to take effect: Enter the dnsslave container of ops1 and ops2 and execute the /root/opsbuild/deploy.py command. Before you execute the command, shut down the BGP process. Otherwise, the named service is restarted during the execution of the deploy.py script, which may result in a temporary unavailability of domain name resolution of the cloud platform. In most cases, the downtime lasts a few seconds and has a minimal impact. However, the deploy.py script may get stuck. We recommend that you shut down the BGP process before you execute the command. To stop the BGP process, execute the ps aux | grep bgp command to list all processes related to BGP and then execute the kill -9 command to stop the BGP process. Restart the DnsSlave# nodes one by one. (Make sure that each DnsSlave node restarts and reaches its final state before you proceed to the next node.) ##### 2.2.7.3 Configure DTS parameters

If you configure a primary/secondary disaster recovery solution between two clouds, you must configure Data Transmission Service (DTS) for database products. This topic describes how to configure DTS.

**Prerequisites**

A network connection is established between the primary and secondary sites. ASR for Geo-disaster Recovery (ASR-DR) is deployed at the primary site and a DTS SQL template file is generated in the container. If the prerequisites are not met, manually configure local DTS.

**Automatically configure local DTS**

1. Obtain the AccessKey ID (AK) and AccessKey secret (SK) and pop_ops_vip of the operations
administrator at the primary site. i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console as an operations administrator. ii. Click in the upper-right corner of the page and then click **User Information**. iii. Obtain the AK and SK of the operations administrator. iv. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**

container.

```
python alidata/bin/dts/dts_new/auto_config_dts.py asrdr -v {pop_ops_vip} -a {ops_admin_ak} -s {ops_admin_sk}
```

Replace the pop_ops_vip, ops_admin_ak, and ops_admin_sk parameters with the values obtained from the preceding steps. After the script is executed, relevant information about the primary site is inserted into the DTS database at the secondary site.
