###### 3.3.4.3.4 Handle alerts

This section describes how to handle the alerts of managed instances.

**Prerequisites**

A managed instance is created.

**Background information**

You can handle the alerts generated by managed instances. You can ignore alerts or mark them as fixed based on the actual situation by following the same procedure for handling the alerts of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances. The detection cycle of alerts is 30 minutes.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Management Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Monitoring & Alerting > Managed Instance**
**Alerts**.
3. On the **Managed Instance Alerts** tab, click **Create an event ticket** in the Actions
column of the alert that you want to handle.
4. In the dialog box that appears, handle the alert based on the actual situation. For example,
if the alert is a false positive or the alert does not require any operations, select **Ignore**, specify **Handler** and **Closing Reason**, and then click **OK**. O&M
5. If the O&M engineer has repaired the managed instance based on the alert information and
submitted the feedback, you can select **Fixed**, specify **Handler** and **Closing Reason**, and then click **OK**.

#### 3.3.5 Basic settings

The basic settings module aggregates important information required for registering and maintaining Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances, including image metadata, network configuration, models and specifications, and GPU information. This module greatly simplifies the management of ECS bare metal instances and improves the efficiency and reliability of instance deployment.

##### 3.3.5.1 Image management

The image management feature is used to maintain image metadata required for installing Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances. It allows administrators to query custom images, manage custom image status, delete images, and export images, and query public images, manage public image status, and export public images. Administrators can upload custom images based on their business requirements.

###### 3.3.5.1.1 Upload a custom image

This topic describes how to upload a custom image.

**Prerequisites**

A custom image file that meets the specifications is prepared in the on-premises environment.

**Background information**

You can upload TGZ or QCOW2 custom image files based on your business requirements.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Management Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
3. On the **Images** page, click the **Custom Image** tab and then click **Upload Custom Image**.
4. In the panel that appears, follow the on-screen instructions to configure the parameters,
enter an image name, select a proper platform, and specify the system architecture.
5. Select a local TGZ or QCOW2 image file.
6. Click **OK** to upload the image.
O&M

> **Note:** The certificate of the environment to which you are logged in affects image uploading. Check whether the certificate is still valid. If the certificate has expired, the system prompts that image uploading failed. In this case, contact the administrator of the environment or use the following method to address the issue.

1. When you failed to upload the image, enable the developer mode of your web browser.
2. Find the error message in the developer console and copy the link that starts with
"https…".
3. Access the link in a new tab of the browser.
4. On the warning page that appears, click **Advanced** and select Continue. Then, you are
redirected to a new page.
5. After you complete the preceding operations, you can continue to upload the image.

###### 3.3.5.1.2 Query images

This topic describes how to query images and view the details of images.

**Prerequisites**

A public image or custom image is created. For more information, see Upload a custom image.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, select a filter condition, enter the keyword into the search box, and
click the Search icon to search for images that meet the filter condition. You can search images by **Image Name** or **Image ID**.
4. After you find the desired image, you can view its details in the list, including the image
name, ID, size, architecture, platform, format, creation time, whether the image is available, and whether the image is enabled.

###### 3.3.5.1.3 Delete an image

This topic describes how to delete an image.

**Prerequisites**

A custom image is created. For more information, see Upload a custom image.

> **Important:** When you delete an image, the source image file is also deleted. Proceed with caution.

1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
O&M By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, find the image that you want to delete and click **Delete Image** in the
Actions column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 3.3.5.1.4 Manage public images

This topic describes how to use public images.

**Prerequisites**

The environment to which you are logged in already has the relevant image resources.

**Background information**

Public images in the TGZ and QCOW2 formats are supported in Apsara Stack. By default, the platform provides some adapted public images. If no image is displayed on the Public Image tab or the status of the public images on the tab is not "Available", contact the developer. When a public image is disabled, it is not displayed on the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instance creation page. To use this image, you must first enable it on the Images page. Some public images are only used to migrate products that are compatible with earlier versions. You cannot export these images.

> **Note:** Public images cannot be deleted.

1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, click the **Public Image** tab.
4. The tab displays all available public images. You can manage image status and export
images. For more information, see Manage image status and Image export.

###### 3.3.5.1.5 Manage image status

This topic describes how to change the status of an image.

**Prerequisites**

A public image or custom image is created. For more information, see Upload a custom image. The image to be managed is not referenced.

**Background information**

You can change the status of an image. After you change the status of an image to Disabled, the image cannot be referenced. If the image has been referenced, you cannot change the status of the image to Disabled. O&M

**Disable the image**

1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, find the image whose status you want to change and move the
pointer over **Enabling Status** in the Actions column.
4. In the drop-down list, click **Disable Image**.
5. Then, the Available Status column of the image changes to **Unavailable,** and the Enabling
Status column of the image changes to **Disable**.

**Enable the image**

1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, find the image whose status you want to change and move the
pointer over **Enabling Status** in the Actions column.
4. In the drop-down list, click **Enable Image**.
5. Then, the Available Status column of the image changes to **Available,** and the Enabling
Status column of the image changes to **Enable**.

###### 3.3.5.1.6 Export an image

This topic describes how to export a public image or an uploaded custom image to the onpremises machine.

**Prerequisites**

A public image or custom image is created. For more information, see Upload a custom image.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Images**.
By default, the **Custom Image** tab is displayed.
3. On the **Images** page, find the image that you want to export and click **Export Image** in
the Actions column.
4. Wait until the image is downloaded.

##### 3.3.5.2 Network management

Administrators can query and view information about existing subnets and new subnets. This topic describes how to query the information about existing subnets and update subnet information.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Management Service (BMS) Operations Console.
O&M
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Network**.
3. On the **Network** page, select a filter condition, enter the keyword into the search box, and
click the Search icon to search for subnets that meet the filter condition. You can search subnets by **Subnet Name**.

##### 3.3.5.3 Model management

The model management feature allows administrators to add, query, delete, and modify models. This way, administrators can flexibly manage models to meet diverse business requirements. This feature also helps ensure the accuracy and consistency of model information, which simplifies the management and deployment of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances.

###### 3.3.5.3.1 Add a model

After you create a model, you can query and view the information about the model. This topic describes how to add a model.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Management Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Models**.
3. On the **Models** page, click **Add Model** above the list.
4. In the **Add Model** dialog box, set the model name and the CPU, memory, and disk
parameters.
5. After you complete the configuration, click **OK** to add the model.

###### 3.3.5.3.2 Modify a model

This topic describes how to modify the configuration of a model.

**Prerequisites**

A model is added. For more information, see Add a model. No Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances of the model to be modified are registered.

**Background information**

You can modify all properties of a model except the model name. After a model is modified, administrators can query and view information about the modified model.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Models**.
3. On the **Models** page, find the model that you want to modify and click **Modify** in the
Actions column.
4. In the **Modify model** dialog box, modify the model parameters.
5. After you modify the model, click **OK**.
O&M

###### 3.3.5.3.3 Query models

Administrators can query and view information about existing models. This topic describes how to query models and view the details of models.

**Prerequisites**

A model is added. For more information, see Add a model.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Models**.
3. On the **Models** page, select a filter condition, enter the keyword into the search box, and
click the Search icon to search for models that meet the filter condition. You can search models by Model Name, Disk Type, and Manufacturer.

###### 3.3.5.3.4 Delete a model

This topic describes how to delete a model.

**Prerequisites**

A model is added. For more information, see Add a model. The model to be deleted is not referenced by any Elastic Compute Service (ECS) bare metal instances.

**Warning**

This operation is a high-risk operation and is irreversible. Proceed with caution. Administrators can delete models with the specified names. If physical machines of a model are registered, the model cannot be deleted.
1. Log in to the Bare Metal Service (BMS) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Settings > Models**.
3. On the **Models** page, find the model that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the
Actions column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK** to delete the model.

##### 3.3.5.4 GPU settings

The GPU settings feature allows administrators to add, query, modify, and delete GPUs. Administrators can use this feature to add GPU settings, efficiently search GPU settings, update existing GPU settings, and delete GPU settings in certain scenarios.

###### 3.3.5.4.1 Add a GPU

### 3.5 BMCP Operations Platform

O&M

#### 3.5.1 O&M overview

This topic describes the objectives, requirements, and precautions of Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) O&M and how to obtain technical support.

**Objectives**

This guide helps O&M engineers perform preventive maintenance to ensure the long-term stability of BMCP. O&M engineers can follow the instructions in this guide to handle system issues that are identified during maintenance. For system issues that are not covered in this guide, O&M engineers can contact Apsara Stack engineers for technical support.

**Requirements**

O&M engineers must possess IT skills, including the knowledge of computer networks, computer operations, and troubleshooting. O&M engineers must pass the pre-job training and learn the knowledge for the Apsara Stack system. The required knowledge for the system includes system principles, networking, features, and the usage of maintenance tools.

> **Important:** During the maintenance, O&M engineers must follow operation procedures to ensure personal safety and system security. No part of user data may be copied or disseminated in any form or by any means without prior written consent from users.

**Precautions**

To ensure a stable system and prevent unexpected events, O&M engineers must comply with the following guidelines: Hierarchical permission management Permissions on networks, devices, systems, and data are granted based on the services and roles of O&M engineers. This prevents system faults that are caused by unauthorized operations. System security Before O&M engineers perform operations on the system, they must be aware of the impacts of the operations. This ensures that the system is not affected by high-risk operations. O&M engineers must record the details about the issues that are encountered during the operations. This helps O&M engineers troubleshoot the issues. Personal safety and data security O&M engineers must take measures to ensure safety based on device manuals when they use electrical equipment. O&M engineers must use secure devices to access the business network. Unauthorized data replication and dissemination are prohibited.

**Technical support**

O&M engineers can contact Apsara Stack technical support for help during the maintenance.

#### 3.5.2 Getting started

O&M

##### 3.5.2.1 BMCP Operations Console

The Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console is a cutting-edge O&M technical solution that focuses on intelligent computing, high-performance computing, and scenarios where intelligent computing and high-performance computing are integrated. The BMCP Operations Console provides a high-performance computing system based on an Intel architecture and an intelligent computing system based on a NVIDIA architecture. It is compatible with domestic software and hardware ecosystems. The BMCP Operations Console provides O&M engineers with computing resource topology visualization and resource O&M capabilities. O&M engineers can centrally manage and maintain computing, network, and storage resources from the job and trace perspective. It greatly improves the O&M efficiency.

**Characteristics and benefits**

Full-stack device management Provides a multi-tenant-oriented computing resource normalization and O&M platform that covers computing, storage, and network resource topology management and maintenance. Computing resource supply for various architectures Supports mainstream training and inference platforms that use intel CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs. Supports domestic software and hardware ecosystem platforms based on Hygon CPUs and Hygon GPUs or based on Kunpeng CPUs and Huawei Ascend NPUs to ensure the supply of computing resources. Visualized real-time monitoring Provides visualized topology monitoring for nodes, links, and network elements, and uses time slice labeling to display the real-time status of computing, storage, and network resources. The job path analysis feature provides a topology view to display O&M planes from the perspective of jobs in order to conduct fine-grained O&M, including monitoring, alerting, diagnostics, and logging. Intelligent device inspection and diagnostics Analyzes the status of hardware devices and logs and conducts multi-level inspection to eliminate potential job risks in clusters. Performs cluster and computing job diagnostics to quickly locate issues, isolate resources, or fix issues. ROI optimization Supports the reuse of vendor or data center-level GPUs to improve the stock of computing resources in order to optimize the Return on Investment (ROI). The BMCP Operations Console is an enterprise-class O&M solution which is suitable for scientific institutions that need to process massive computing jobs, intelligent computing jobs, large-sized Internet enterprises, and the financial industry. It is a powerful and flexible resource O&M platform.

**Features**

This module analyzes the topology of jobs in data planes and manages the lifecycle of nodes, GPUs, RDMA networks, RDMA network elements, and links in a visualized manner. O&M This module allows you to manage all physical resources that are used by your businesses, including computing, storage, and network resources. This module monitors the stability metrics of computing resources, including nodes, GPUs, and RDMA resources, and generates alerts in real time when events are detected. This module manages all computing logic resources used by your businesses, allowing you to centrally manage computing, storage, and network resources. This module inspects and diagnoses resources in different scenarios to quickly locate the cause. This module allows you to export cluster or node logs to help improve the overall O&M efficiency and system reliability.

This topic describes the content displayed on the Overview page of the Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console. The Overview page displays alerts, resource data, computing power statistics, and control services.

**Alarm Board**

The alert dashboard displays alerts related to computing, networks, and storage.

**Resource Statistics**

This section displays resource data related to intelligent computing clusters, supercomputing clusters, and storage clusters. O&M Total number of intelligent computing clusters, number of servers, and number of instances. Intelligent computing clusters are classified into **bare metal-intelligent computing**
**clusters** and **ACK-intelligent computing clusters**.
Intelligent computing instances are classified into **high-bandwidth network**
**intelligent computing** instances, **managed intelligent computing** instances, and
**basic intelligent computing** instances.
Intelligent computing instances include only bare metal instances. Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances are not included. Total number of supercomputing clusters, number of servers, and number of instances. Supercomputing clusters include **bare metal-supercomputing clusters**. Supercomputing instances include **high-performance high-bandwidth network** instances. Total number of storage clusters, number of servers, and number of file systems.

**Resource Board**

This section displays the usage of intelligent computing resources, supercomputing resources, and storage resources.

> **Note:** Supercomputing resources do not include the CPU cores and memory of intelligent computing clusters.
> Intelligent computing resources do not include the GPUs and GPU memory of supercomputing clusters.

Intelligent computing resources (number of GPUs and GPU memory) Select a GPU type from the drop-down list, such as **Nvidia** or **Hygon**, to view the GPU quantity of the selected type and total GPU memory.

> **Note:** The actual GPU types that you can select on the page shall prevail.

O&M Displays allocated resources, unallocated resources, total resources, and distribution ratio. The amount of allocated resources indicates the resources that are allocated to tenants. The amount of unallocated resources indicates the resources in the resource pool. The total amount of resources equals the sum of resources allocated to tenants and resources in the resource pool. Distribution ratio = Resources in the resource pool/(Resources allocated to tenants + Resources in the resource pool) × 100%. Supercomputing resources (number of CPU cores and memory) Select a CPU type from the drop-down list, such as **Intel** or **Hygon**, to view the CPU core quantity of the selected type and total memory.

> **Note:** The actual CPU types that you can select on the page shall prevail.

Displays allocated resources, unallocated resources, total resources, and distribution ratio. The amount of allocated resources indicates the resources that are allocated to tenants. The amount of unallocated resources indicates the resources in the resource pool. The total amount of resources equals the sum of resources allocated to tenants and resources in the resource pool. Distribution ratio = Resources in the resource pool/(Resources allocated to tenants + Resources in the resource pool) × 100%. Storage resources Select a storage resource type from the drop-down list, such as **APFS** or **CPFS**, to view usage of storage resources of the selected type. Displays **used** storage resources, **allocated** storage resources, **total** storage resources, and the **usage** of storage resources. O&M

**Computational Power Board**

This dashboard displays the usage of GPU computing power and CPU computing power. GPU computing power (unit: TFLOPS) Select a GPU type from the drop-down list to view the usage of GPU computing power of the selected type. The time range is not configurable. The dashboard displays the total computing power, allocated computing power, and distribution ratio within the last week and of the current day. CPU computing power (unit: TFLOPS) Select a CPU type from the drop-down list to view the usage of CPU computing power of the selected type. The time range is not configurable. The dashboard displays the total computing power, allocated computing power, and distribution ratio within the last week and of the current day.

> **Note:** CPU computing power refers to the computing power of supercomputing CPUs, excluding the computing power of CPUs in intelligent computing clusters.
> GPU computing power refers to the computing power of intelligent computing GPUs, excluding the computing power of GPUs in supercomputing clusters.

**Control Service**

The Control Service module displays the service status of the control services related to computing, networks, and storage. The status of a service can be **Not reaching the final**
**state** or **Has reached the final state**. **Not reaching the final state** indicates that the
service deployment has not been completed. **Has reached the final state** indicates that the service deployment is complete. O&M

##### 3.5.4.1 Job path analysis

This topic describes how to work with job path analysis.

**Limits**

Only Hygon DCUK100-AI, APG PG1 A910E, and Kunlun P800 support job path analysis.

**Prerequisites**

The cluster in which the job is deployed has the ai-task-inspector component installed. If the component is not installed, go to **Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) > Cluster**
**Management > Software Instance** to install it.

> **Note:** You can use different services to submit jobs, such as Platform for AI (PAI) or AI Studio. You can use the job path analysis feature if only the job uses the GPU resources of BMCP nodes.

1. Log on to the BMCP Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Job Path Analysis** below Visualized Monitoring.
3. On the **Job Path Analysis** page, specify **Job ID** and click **Search**.

> **Note:** Specify **Start And End Time** to select a time range. You can query historical jobs within at most the last 7 days.
> The **Node ID** parameter is optional. If you specified **Node ID**, **Cluster ID** is automatically set to the ID of the cluster that contains the node.
> The **Cluster ID** and **Namespace** parameters are required. Then, specify **Job ID**.
> By default, **Job Information** is hidden. You can click the
> icon on the left to
> view the status of the job, resources occupied by the job, and the start time and end time of the job.

4. After you click **Job Details**, the **Basic Information** and **Monitoring** tabs are displayed in
the right-side panel. The **Basic Information** tab displays the nodes occupied by the job, and the **Monitoring** tab displays the metrics of the occupied nodes, such as the average CPU utilization.
5. In the **Job view** section, click a **time slice**. Then, the canvas displays the topology and
resource usage of the job within the selected time slice. The topology displays the **GPUs,**
**RDMA cards, and vSwitches**, and the connections among them. Resource usage metrics
such as GPU utilization and RDMA network bandwidth usage are also displayed. O&M

> **Note:** Move the pointer over a GPU or RDMA card to view the name and resource usage of the resource.

###### 3.5.6.1.2.2 Manage computing nodes

This section describes how to manage idle Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) nodes in the resource pool.

**Prerequisites**

A BMCP node is registered.
1. Log on to the BMCP Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Clusters > Calculation > Node** to go to the Node
tab. You can also click **Details** in the Operation column of the node to go to the node details page. You can manage the node in the Operation column or on the details page.
3. Perform the **Resource Enable** operation on a node.
i. Make sure that the node type is **Intelligent Computing High Net** and resource owner is **Resource Pool**. You can perform the **Resource Enable** operation only on nodes of the **Intelligent Computing High Net** type in the **resource pool** on the **O&M side**. a. Click **Resource Enable** for a node in the list. The **Enable** button is dimmed for nodes that have Resource Enable enabled. After you click **Disable** for a node, the node cannot be added to clusters. b. Click **Resource Enable** for a node in the list. The **Disable** button is dimmed for nodes that have Resource Enable disabled. After you click **Enable** for a node, the node can be added to clusters. c. On the details page, if the node has **Resource Enable** disabled, choose **More >**
**Resource Enable > Enable**. Then, the node can be added to clusters.
d. On the details page, if the node has **Resource Enable** enabled, choose **More >**
**Resource Enable > Disable**. Then, the node cannot be added to clusters.
4. Perform the **Node Status** operation on a node.
O&M i. Make sure that the resource owner of the node is **Resource Pool**. You can perform the
**Node Status** operation only on idle nodes in the **resource pool** on the **O&M side**.
a. Click Node Status for a node in the list. The operations that you can perform on the node are displayed. The operations that you cannot perform are dimmed. Select an operation to perform it. b. On the details page, you can view the operations that you can perform on the node. The operations that you cannot perform are dimmed. Select an operation to perform it.
5. Modify node information.
i. Modify the gateway port: Go to **Clusters > Calculation > Node > Node details** and choose **More > Modify the Gateway port**. Select a gateway port from the drop-down list and click **OK**. ii. Modify the node name and description: Go to **Clusters > Calculation > Node > Node**
**details** and choose **More > Edit properties**. Modify the node name and description and
click **OK**.
6. Log on to the out-of-band console.
Go to **Clusters > Calculation > Node > Node details** and choose **More > Out-of-**
**band console** to log on to the out-of-band console.

4. You can view the health status, disk type, file system type, and number of nodes of the
cluster.

6. Click **Details** in the **Operation** column of the cluster to view the cluster details.
On the **Basic Information** tab, you can view **Number of file systems**, **Number of**
**nodes**, **File system type**, **Health status**, and **Disk type**.
On the **Node** tab, you can view node information, such as **Management IP**, **SN**, **Model**,
**CPU architecture**, and **Memory**.
You can search nodes by node name in exact match mode. On the **Service** tab, you can view service roles and service status. You can search services by service name in fuzzy match mode. Click **Tianji O & M** in the **Operation** column of the desired service role. The **Monitoring** tab displays monitoring data.

**View the details of a client cluster**

1. Log on to the BMCP Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
3. On the **Cluster Management** page, click the **Storage** tab.
4. Click the **Client Cluster** tab.
O&M You can view the cluster information, including the cluster status, cluster type, number of nodes, number of Quorum nodes, and **the file system mounted to the cluster** .

6. Click **Details** in the **Operation** column of the desired cluster to view the cluster details.

The **Cluster Node** tab displays the basic node information, including the node type and node status. You can also click **Details** in the **Operation** column of the desired node to view the node details, including the basic information, configuration information, monitoring data, and operation logs.

###### 3.5.7.1.1.2 Register resources

This topic describes how to register server resources. O&M
1. Log on to the Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Resource Management**.
By default, the **Calculation > Server** tab is displayed. You can view all physical servers on this tab.
3. Click **Register Resources** above the list.
4. Specify **Physical machine gateway port**, **Subnet**, **Subnet IP**, and **Out-of-band**
**information**.
5. Specify a password.
The password must be 8 to 30 characters in length, and must contain at least three types of the following characters: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Special characters include ( ) ` ~ ! @ # $ % ^ & * _ - + = | { } [ ] : ; ' < > , . ? /.

> **Important:** Keep your password confidential. If you lost the password, you can log on to the BMCP Operations Console and reset the password.

6. Specify **Resource Name**, **Hostname**, and **Resource Description**.

> **Note:** The resource name must be 2 to 128 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, periods (.), and hyphens (-). The name must start with a letter or digit.

7. After you complete the configuration, click **OK**.

#### 3.5.8 Inspection and diagnostics

##### 3.5.8.1 Inspection

###### 3.5.8.1.1 Clusters and nodes

This topic describes how to diagnose a cluster or node.
1. Log on to the Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Inspection and Diagnostics**.
3. Click **Inspection** below **Inspection and Diagnostics**. On the Cluster/node diagnosis tab,
create a diagnostic task for a cluster or node and view the diagnostic result.
4. Click **Create a task**, specify the task name, choose cluster diagnostics or node diagnostics,
confirm the diagnostic scope, and select diagnostic items.
5. Click **OK** to create the task.
6. You can search historical diagnostic tasks by task ID in exact match mode or by task name
in fuzzy match mode. You can also specify a time range or click Advanced Filter and specify multiple filter conditions.
7. Cancel the diagnostic task.
Click **Cancel** in the **Operation** column of the task.
8. View the diagnostic result.
After the diagnostic task enters the Completed state, click **Details** to view the diagnostic result.

###### 3.5.8.1.2 Jobs

This topic describes how to diagnose the cluster in which a job runs.
1. Log on to the Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Inspection and Diagnostics**.
3. Click **Inspection**.
O&M
4. On this page, you can create a diagnostic task for the cluster in which the job runs and view
the diagnostic result.
5. Click Create a task, specify **Task name**, **Cluster ID**, **Namespace**, and **Job ID**, and select
**Diagnostic items**.
6. Click **OK** to create the task.
7. You can search historical diagnostic tasks by cluster ID, namespace, and job ID.
8. Cancel the diagnostic task.
Click **Cancel** in the **Operation** column of the diagnostic task to cancel the task.
9. View the diagnostic result.
After the diagnostic task enters the Completed state, click **Details** to view the diagnostic result.

###### 3.5.8.1.3 Description of diagnostic items

The diagnostics feature provides cluster, node, and job diagnostics. This topic describes the supported diagnostic items.

**System diagnostics**

| Diagnostic item | Description |
|---|---|
| Resource QoS diagnostics | The containerd engine is abnormal, and the ctr command times out or hangs. |
| DNS configuration check | Check the DNS configuration of the physical machine /etc/resolv.conf. |
| NIC uplink mapping check | Check whether the mappings between the network interface controller (NIC) ports of each server and the switch ports are correct. |

**Network diagnostics**

| Diagnostic item | Description |
|---|---|
| NIC speed compliance check | Check and ensure that the NIC speed meets the system requirements. |
| BOND port check | Check the status and configuration of network bonding ports. |
| NIC-to-GPU connection check | Check whether the connection topology between NICs and GPUs is correct. |
| Bonding module check | Check whether the bonding network module is correctly installed. |

O&M

| OS release version | Check the OS release version. |
|---|---|
| OS kernel version | Check and ensure that the kernel version meets the system requirements. |
| Hash policy for aggregating RDMA network devices | Check the aggregation hash policy configuration of Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network devices. |
| RDMA QoS configuration check | Check and optimize RDMA Quality of Service (QoS) configuration. |
| RDMA device quantity | Check whether the number of RDMA devices meets expectations. |
| RDMA device name and status | Check the names and running status of RDMA devices. |
| RDMA device aggregation mode | Check the aggregation mode configuration of RDMA devices. |
| RDMA device MTU settings | Check and optimize the MTU settings of RDMA devices. |
| RDMA device port rate | Check whether the RDMA device port rate meets the performance requirements. |
| RDMA device aggregation status | Check the aggregation status of RDMA devices. |
| MLX LAG mode check | Check and confirm the MLX LAG mode configuration. |
| PCIe link rate and width consistency check | Check the consistency of the PCIe link rate and width. |
| Consistency check of RDMA device firmware versions | Check the consistency of RDMA device firmware versions. |
| RDMA NIC driver loading | Check whether the RDMA NIC driver is loaded correctly. |

O&M

| PCIe MRR configuration | Check the PCIe MRR configuration. |
|---|---|
| GDR module load check | Check whether the GDR module is loaded correctly. |
| LLDP service running status | Check the running status of the LLDP service. |
| Running status of NVIDIA Fabric Manager | Check the running status of NVIDIA Fabric Manager. |
| PCIe link rate and width downgrade check | Check and fix the PCIe link rate and width downgrade issues. |
| Upstream switch and port name check | Check the upstream switch and port name configuration. |
| alixpu peermem _ status check | Check the loading status of the alixpu peermem module and reload it. _ |
| XDR module installation check | Check the integrity of the XDR module installation and reinstall it if necessary. |
| APG ICN status check | Check the APG ICN for abnormal status and restart the related services. |
| GPU drop | Check whether the GPU has fallen off the bus. |
| IB NIC sequence check | Check whether the IB NIC sequence is as expected. |

###### 3.5.9.2.2 Public images

You can enable, disable, and export public images and export signature files.

**Manage public images**

You can enable, disable, and export public images.
1. Log on to the Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP) Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Configurations > Images**.
By default, the **Custom image** tab is displayed.
3. Click the **Public image** tab.
4. Search for your image by its name or ID in fuzzy match node above the image list.
5. Manage the image:
i. **Enable the image** Choose **Enable status > Enable images** in the **Operation** column of the image. ii. **Disable the image** Choose **Enable status > Disable images** in the **Operation** column of the image. iii. **Export the image** Click **Image export** in the **Operation** column of the image to export the image to your on-premises machine. O&M iv. **Export signature files** Click **Signature File Export** in the **Operation** column of the image to export the signature file to your on-premises machine.

**Verify image integrity**

BMCP allows users to verify the integrity of public images to ensure that they are not tampered with.
1. Log on to the BMCP Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Configurations > Images**.
By default, the **Custom image** tab is displayed.
3. Click the **Public image** tab.
4. Click **Download public key** above the list.
5. Click **Signature File Export** in the **Operation** column of the desired image.
6. You can run the following command to check whether the image has been tampered with:

```
 openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.key -signature signature.bin imagefile
```

> **Note:** Before you run the command, make sure that the public key, signature file, and image are downloaded.
> Set the following parameters to the actual values:
> `public.key` indicates the public key.
> `signature.bin` indicates the signature file.
> `imagefile` indicates the image file.

**proceed.** and click **OK**.

#### 4.1.2 Basic network

##### 4.1.2.1 Network element management

Network elements are network devices such as vSwitches and routers. The Network Element Management module displays the basic information and status of physical network devices. The module also supports configuration management operations on physical network devices, including device management, password management, and configuration consistency comparison. For more information about the features of the Network Operations Console that are applicable to device manufacturers, see vSwitch Monitoring Capabilities Supported by Network Operations Console.

**Manage devices**

On the Device Management tab, you can view the monitoring information about physical network devices and configure collection settings for them.

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll is deployed and has reached the desired state.

**Network monitoring**

You can view the basic information, status, and traffic monitoring information of physical network devices in Apsara Stack to stay updated with their health status.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** > **Network Element**
**Management**.
4. On the **Network Element Management** page, click the **Device Management** tab.
5. Click the **Network Monitoring** tab. A list of the physical network monitoring devices in
Apsara Stack in all data centers is displayed by default. The list includes the following information: **Device Name**, **Management IP Address**,
**SN**, **Business Domain**, **Vendor**, **Model**, **Role**, **Online Duration**, **PING Status**,
**Collection Mode**, and **Last Updated At**.
You can specify **IDC** to view the physical network monitoring devices in Apsara Stack in the data center. In the upper-right corner of the Network Monitoring tab, you can enter a device name or an IP address in the search box and then click **Search** to search for the specified physical network monitoring device, and then view its information. The **Management IP address** and **PING Status** columns can be used to sort the physical network monitoring devices. The **Role** column can be used to filter the physical network monitoring devices. perations
6. You can perform the following operations on the network monitoring device list.
Find the network monitoring device that you want to manage and choose **Collection**
**Settings > Switch Collection Mode** in the **Details** column to switch the collection
mode of the device.

> **Note:** If the properties of the selected vSwitch do not support gRPC, the **gRPC** option is dimmed in the Switch Collection Mode dialog box. Typically, this occurs when the initial collection mode is **SNMP**.
> The operation is asynchronously executed. The mode may be switched with a latency. You can refresh the page to view the latest execution result.

Find the network monitoring device that you want to manage and choose **Collection**
**Settings > Collection Configuration** in the **Details** column to view the collection
configuration. perations Find the network monitoring device that you want to manage and click the name in the

device.

**Collection Protocol Settings**

On the Collection Protocol Settings tab, you can set the collection protocol for physical network devices and manage out-of-band (OOB) CIDR blocks. Before you collect network device information, you need to configure the SNMP protocol based on your business requirements. In the OOB CIDR block management section, you can configure the management scope of a physical network device. In most cases, O&M engineers must add the loopback CIDR block in which the network device to be managed resides.

> **Note:** If you use the network element management feature of the Network Operations Console for the first time, you must add the loopback CIDR block planned for the current network device in Apsara Stack. In most cases, the loopback CIDR block is the CIDR block specified by the netdev.loopback field in the planned IP address list. To expand the network and the loopback CIDR block, you must add the CIDR block involved in the expansion to the management scope. The procedure for adding an expanded CIDR block is the same as that used to add the loopback CIDR block for the first time. ##### 4.1.2.2 Syslog

The Syslog module records and stores the logs generated by network hardware devices in the system based on dimensions such as time, log level, and module to facilitate subsequent analysis and management. This helps you identify and solve issues to improve the availability and stability of devices.

**View logs**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** >**Syslog**.
4. On the Syslog page, click **Advanced Filter**. Then, configure the **Data Center**, **Source**
**Device**, **Recorded At**, **Log Content**, **Parsing Status**, **Log Level**, **Manufacturer**, and
**Alert Module** parameters to filter logs.
5. View the information about the logs that meet the filter conditions in the columns that are
described in the following table. perations

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| Recorded At | The time when the log entry was recorded. You can sort log entries based on the column. |
| Log Content | The parsed log data, which is the content of the raw log. |
| Source Device | The source device from which the log data was collected. |
| Parsing Status | The parsing status of log data. Valid values: Parsed and Parsing Failed. Note Logs may fail to be parsed due to the following reasons: The log format does not meet the RFC 3164 specification. The network device from which the log data was collected is not produced by an asset-heavy manufacturer that is supported by Apsara Stack. |
| Log Level | The level of the log data. Valid values: Emergency, Alert, Serious, Error, Warning, Notification, Information, and Debugging. |
| Module | The module to which the log data belongs. |
| Raw Logs | The raw log data that is not parsed. |
| Manufacturer | The manufacturer of the network device. |

6. Find the log entry that you want to view and click **Details** in the Operation column. In the
Syslog Details panel, view more detailed information about the log, such as the alert matching results, module details, and location. perations

**What to do next**

**Export logs**

On the Syslog page, click **Export Logs** in the upper-left corner to export the logs to your computer for viewing.

> **Note:** By default, all logs are exported.

**Test the log parsing feature**

1. On the Syslog page, click **Test Analysis** in the upper-left corner.
2. In the Test Analysis dialog box, enter content in the **Original Text** field and click **Submit**.

> **Note:** If you click **Reset**, the content in the Original Text field is cleared.

3. In the Parsing Results section, view the parsed information, such as the description,
hostname, and log level.

###### 4.1.2.3.2 RDMA NIC O&M

To perform O&M on Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network interface cards (NICs), you must check the performance metrics of RDMA NICs. RDMA NIC O&M allows you to identify and troubleshoot issues and ensure network stability and reliability.

**Terms**

**RDMA**: RDMA is a high-speed network technology used to reduce the delay in server-side
data processing during network transmission. RDMA transfers data directly into the memory of a computer over the RDMA network and enables direct memory access between hosts without affecting the operating system. This accelerates data transmission and reduces CPU load.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** > **HPN Management** > **RDMA**
**Card O&M**.
4. On the **RDMA Card O&M** page, specify **Data Source**, **Cluster**, and **ViewType** in the
upper-right corner based on your business requirements to view the performance metrics of RDMA NICs. The following data sources are supported:
**BMS**: Bare Metal Server.
**PAI**: Platform of Artificial Intelligence.
**CPFS**: Cloud Parallel File System.
**SCC**: Super Computing Cluster.

> **Note:** If you select **PAI**, **CPFS**, or **SCC** for **Data Source**, you must also select a value for **Cluster**.
> If you select **PAI** for **Data Source**, you must also select a value for **ViewType**.

Click the **Cluster** tab. On this tab, view the monitoring information about the selected cluster.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|

perations

| Average QP | The average number of queue pairs (QPs) in the RDMA network. If you select PAI for Data Source, this parameter is not displayed. If the number of QPs is insufficient, the communication queue in the RDMA network may be congested, which compromises the efficiency and stability of data transmission. If the number of QPs is excessively large, the system overheads, complexity, and failure rate are increased. Note QP is a key term of the RDMA network. It refers to the communication queue between a pair of endpoints. |
|---|---|
| Abnormal Networks | The number of times that network device exceptions or traffic exceptions occur in the RDMA network. |
| Average Throughput Sent by RDMA (Mbit/s) | The average amount of data sent by all nodes in the RDMA network per second. |
| Average Throughput Received by RDMA (Mbit/s) | The average amount of data received by all nodes in the RDMA network per second. |
|   | By default, the throughput dashboard data and basic RDMA network monitoring data within the last one hour are displayed. Note In the upper-right corner of this section, specify a time range to view the corresponding monitoring data. Move the pointer over a point in time in a monitoring chart to view the values of the metrics at that point in time. Click a metric to view the monitoring chart of the metric. Throughput Dashboard RDMA RX BYTES: specifies the number of bytes that are received _ _ over the RDMA network per second. perations

Note CNPs are packets used for network congestion control. When network congestion occurs, CNPs are sent to notify the sender to reduce the sending rate to avoid network congestion and packet loss. RDMA TX PFC PAUSE AVG: specifies the average number of _ _ _ _ Priority-based Flow Control (PFC) packets when data is sent over the RDMA network. |---|---|

Note OOB data is a special type of data transmitted over the RDMA network. ###### 4.1.2.3.3 HPN performance analysis

The Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console provides the High Performance Network (HPN) performance analysis feature. This feature analyzes the maximum load and pressure resistance of the software and hardware by testing the performance of a machine under stress conditions. This helps you identify the pressure resistance limit of the machine and provides data support for O&M engineers to improve network performance.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
perations
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** > **HPN Management** > **HPN**
**Performance Analysis**.
4. On the **HPN performance analysis**page, click **Create a test**.
5. On the **Create an analysis task** page, configure the following parameters.

| Test Cluster | Protoc ol Type | Test Type | Required Parameter | Traffic Model | Node |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arbitrary | RDMA | Traffic Test | Test QPS Node Port Test Duration (s) GDR | MtoN | Server Client |
|   |   |   |   | FullMesh | Server |
|   |   | Latency Test | Node Port | N/A | Server |
|   | TCP | Traffic Test | Node Port Test Duration (s) Concurrent connections | MtoN | Server Client |
|   |   |   |   | FullMesh | Server |

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Test QPS | The number of test processes. This parameter determines the test bandwidth. Default value: 8. If the number of queue pairs (QPs) is insufficient, the communication queue in the Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network may be congested, which compromises the efficiency and stability of data transmission. If the number of QPs is excessively large, the system overheads, complexity, and failure rate are increased. Note QP is a key concept in RDMA networks and is used to describe a queue between a pair of endpoints. |

perations

| Node Port | The port used for the test. Default value: 8300. |
|---|---|
| Test Duration (s) | The duration of the test. Unit: seconds. Default value: 60. |
| GDR | Specify whether to enable GDR. If you turn on this switch, the system associates the RDMA network interface controller (NIC) with the corresponding GPU for traffic testing. Make sure that the machine supports this feature before you turn on the switch. |
| Concurrent connections | The number of connections that can be processed at the same time. Default value: 2. |
| Traffic Model | MtoN: The many-to-many relationship model. This model is used to test the one-way connectivity between Client nodes and Server nodes, including the one-way connectivity between a single Client node and a single Server node and between multiple Client nodes and multiple Server nodes. FullMesh: All nodes in the network topology are connected to each other. This option allows you to test the two-way connectivity between all destination nodes. |
| Client | The sender of the test traffic. You need to specify Node and Nic for each entry. Note Click Add entry to add multiple entries. Click the icon to the right of an entry to deleteN ode and Nic. |
| Server | The receiver of the test traffic. You need to specify Node and Nic for each entry. Note Click Add entry to add multiple entries. Click the icon to the right of an entry to deleteN ode and Nic. |

6. Click **Submit**. A message is displayed, indicating that the analysis task is created.
Click **Cancel** to go back to the page for creating an analysis task. You can modify the parameters based on your business requirements. perations Click **View task details** to go to the **Analysis Task details** page.

###### 4.1.2.4.2 CPN performance analysis

You can perform a Computing Platform Network (CPN) performance analysis task to test the performance of machines under stress conditions. The task analyzes the maximum load and pressure resistance of the existing software and hardware. This helps identify the pressure limits of the machines and provides sufficient data for the O&M team to improve network performance.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network > CPN Management > CPN**
**Performance Analysis**.
4. On the **CPN Performance Analysis**page, click **Create Test**.
5. In the **Create Analysis Task** dialog box, set **Task Name** and configure the parameters.
The following table describes the dynamic combinations and configurations of parameters required to create an **RDMA** analysis task.

| Test Cluster | Protoc ol Type | Test Type | Required parameter | Traffic Model | Nodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arbitrar y | RDMA | Traffic Test | Test QPS Node Port Test Duration (s) GDR | MtoN | Server Client |
|   |   |   |   | FullMesh | Server |
|   |   |   |   | Ring | Server |
|   |   | Latency Test | Node Port Test Duration (s) | N/A | Server |

perations

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Test QPS | The number of test processes. This parameter determines the test bandwidth. Default value: 8. If the number of queue pairs (QPs) is insufficient, the communication queue in the Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network may be congested, which compromises the efficiency and stability of data transmission. If the number of QPs is excessively large, the system overheads, complexity, and failure rate are increased. Note QP is a key term of the RDMA network. It refers to the communication queue between a pair of endpoints. |
| Node Port | The port number used for the test. Default value: 8300. |
| Test Duration (s) | The duration of the test. Unit: seconds. Default value: 60. |
| GDR | Specify whether to enable GDR. If you turn on this switch, the system associates the RDMA network interface card (NIC) with the corresponding GPU for traffic testing. Make sure that the machine supports this feature before you turn on the switch. |
| Traffic Model | MtoN: The many-to-many relationship model. This model is used to test the one-way connectivity between Client nodes and Server nodes, including the one-way connectivity between a single Client node and a single Server node and between multiple Client nodes and multiple Server nodes. FullMesh: All nodes in the network topology are connected to each other. This option allows you to test the two-way connectivity between all destination nodes. Ring: Multiple nodes in the network topology form a closed loop. Data packets are sent from one node to the next node in sequence and finally returned to the original node. This option allows you to test the actual available network bandwidth. |

perations

If you set the Traffic Model parameter to MtoN or FullMesh, you can select a node and enter information about the node. |

following parameters and click **OK**. perations

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Policy Name | Enter a custom name for the policy. |
| Description | Enter the description of the policy. This parameter is optional. |

perations

| Device Vendor | Select a device vendor from the drop-down list. The system automatically displays the device vendors on the RDMA Device Management tab. |
|---|---|
| Device Role | Select the role of the device to which the policy applies from the drop-down list. Valid values: RASW: the access vSwitch of the data exchange module in RDMA networking scenarios. RDSW: the core vSwitch of the data exchange module in RDMA networking scenarios. The core vSwitch is used to connect different access vSwitches. EHSW: the vSwitch that is used to connect to the custodian network in RDMA networking scenarios. |
| Device Model | Select the model of the device to which the policy applies from the drop-down list. The system automatically displays the device models on the RDMA Device Management tab based on the settings of Device Vendor and Device Role. |
| Device Interfaces | Select the device interface to which the policy applies from the following list. The system automatically displays the device names and management IP addresses on the RDMA Device Management tab based on the settings of Device Vendor, Device Role, and Device Model. You can select multiple device interfaces. After you select a device interface, you need to configure a physical port for the interface device. a. Click Select Physical Port in the Physical Port column. In the dialog box that appears, select a port name from the Port Name list. You can select multiple physical ports. You can enter a port name to filter ports. Separate multiple port names with commas (,). b. Click OK. |

perations

| RoCE Queue PFC Configurations | Specify whether to enable the RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) queue PFC configurations. If you turn on this switch, you must configure the following parameters: Headroom Buffer Threshold: Enter the size of the global buffer. It indicates the size of the RoCE queue buffer, and the maximum number of available cell resources in the headroom. Back Pressure Frame Trigger Threshold : The percentage of cell resources available for PFC PAUSE frames that are triggered by packets with an 802.1p priority. The network traffic model is analyzed to ensure that the sum of the backpressure frame trigger thresholds for all ingresses does not exceed the tail-drop threshold for the egress. Offset between Back Pressure Frame Stop Threshold and Trigger Threshold: Enter the offset between the stop threshold and trigger threshold of backpressure frames. If the number of cell resources used by packets with an 802.1p priority decreases by the value of this parameter after PFC is triggered, PFC stops sending PFC PAUSE frames to resume traffic from the peer device. PFC Reservation Threshold: the number of cell resources reserved for packets with an 802.1p priority in the guaranteed storage capacity. PFC: specifies whether to enable or disable the PFC feature. If you use PFC and congestion occurs in a specific type of traffic, the routing of other types of traffic is not affected. This ensures that different types of packets on the same link do not affect each other. Deadlock Monitoring: specifies whether to enable or disable the deadlock monitoring feature. If a link or device failure occurs, temporary loops may occur during the route reconvergence period. In this case, PFC frames are repeatedly sent and received between devices, packets cannot be forwarded, cell resources in the interface buffer are occupied and cannot be released, and the device enters the PFC deadlock state. Note You must configure at least one of the RoCE Queue PFC Configurations and RoCE Queue WRED Configurations parameters. |
|---|---|
|   | Specify whether to enable the RoCE queue WRED configurations. If you turn on this switch, you must configure the following parameters: ECN: specifies whether to enable the Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) feature. ECN uses the DiffServ field in an IP header to mark the congestion status along the packet transmission path. An ECN-capable terminal can determine whether congestion occurs on the transmission path based on the packet content. If congestion occurs, the terminal adjusts the method to send packets to prevent congestion from deteriorating. Minimum Average Queue Length: the lower limit of the length of the queue that the packets of the forwarding device enter in the outbound direction. The lower limit is also called ECN threshold. Maximum Average Queue Length: the upper limit of the length of the queue that the packets of the forwarding device enter in the outbound direction. The upper limit is also called ECN threshold. |

perations

|   | Discarding Probability: the marking probability if ECN is used. A larger value indicates that more packets are marked between the upper and lower limits. Note |
|---|---|
| RoCE Queue WRED Configurations | You must configure at least one of the RoCE Queue PFC Configurations and RoCE Queue WRED Configurations parameters. If the length of the queue that the packets of the forwarding device enter in the outbound direction is smaller than the lower limit, the forwarding device directly forwards the packets from the egress without processing the packets. When the forwarding device assigns packets to a queue in the outbound direction, if the queue size is between the lower threshold and the upper threshold, take note of the following items: If the value of the ECN field in the received packets is 00, the packets are sent by an ECN-incapable terminal. In this case, the forwarding device determines whether to drop the packets based on the drop probability. If the value of the ECN field in the received packets is 01 or 10, the packets are sent by an ECN-capable terminal. In this case, the forwarding device changes the value of the ECN field in some of these packets based on the drop probability and forwards these packets. All incoming packets are not dropped. If the value of the ECN field is 11 in a packet, the packet on the original forwarding device has experienced congestion along the transmission path. In this case, the forwarding device does not process the packet and directly forwards the packet to the egress. When the forwarding device assigns packets to a queue in the outbound direction, if the queue size exceeds the upper threshold, take note of the following items: If the value of the ECN field in the received packets is 00, the packets are sent by an ECN-incapable terminal, the forwarding device drops the packets. If the value of the ECN field in the received packets is 01 or 10, the packets are sent by an ECN-capable terminal. In this case, the forwarding device changes the value of the ECN field in these packets to 11 and forwards these packets. All incoming packets are not dropped. If the value of the ECN field is 11 in a packet, the packet on the original forwarding device has experienced congestion along the transmission path. In this case, the forwarding device does not process the packet and directly forwards the packet to the egress. |

###### 4.1.2.4.5 RDMA NIC O&M

To perform O&M on Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network interface cards (NICs), you must check the performance metrics of RDMA NICs. RDMA NIC O&M allows you to identify and troubleshoot issues and ensure network stability and reliability.

**Terms**

perations
**RDMA**: RDMA is a high-speed network technology used to reduce the delay in server-side
data processing during network transmission. RDMA transfers data directly into the memory of a computer over the RDMA network and enables direct memory access between hosts without affecting the operating system. This increases the data transfer speed and reduces the CPU load.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network > CPN Management > RDMA**
**Card O&M**.
4. On the **RDMA Card O&M** page, specify **Data Source** and **Cluster** in the upper-right
corner to view the performance metrics of RDMA NICs. You can set **Data Source** only to **CPN**. On the **Cluster** tab, view the monitoring information about the cluster.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| Average QP | The average number of queue pairs (QPs) in the RDMA network. If the number of QPs is insufficient, the communication queue may be congested, which affects the efficiency and stability of data transmission. If the number of QPs is excessively large, the system overheads, complexity, and failure rate increase. Note QP is a key term in RDMA networks. It refers to the communication queue between a pair of endpoints. |

perations

| Abnormal Networks | The number of times that network device exceptions or traffic exceptions occur in the RDMA network. |
|---|---|
| Average Throughput Sent by RDMA (Mbit/s) | The average amount of data sent by all nodes in the RDMA network per second. |
| Average Throughput Received by RDMA (Mbit/s) | The average amount of data received by all nodes in the RDMA network per second. |
| Monitoring Charts | By default, the throughput dashboard data and basic RDMA network monitoring data within the last hour are displayed. perations Computing Platform Network (CPN) supports the global traffic observability feature, including the stream-based visualization of communication relationships, communication paths, communication quality, and impacts of congestion.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the stream-based visualization feature of CPN is disabled. Before you use this feature, make sure that the cpn-lsgo database is enabled. Operations:
1. Log in to the database and execute the following SQL statement:

```
update config_detail_info set config_value='on' where config_key in ('tracing_open','cpn_gtp','cpn_gto','cpn_gts','asnet-cpn-lsgo-agent');
```

2. Restart the service.

**Network Dashboard > CPN Flow Monitor**.

##### 4.1.2.5 Cloud Gateway

You can connect bare metal instances to a virtual private cloud (VPC) by using Cloud Gateway (CGW) to manage the bare metal instances in a centralized manner. CGW instances are dedicated hybrid switches (HSWs). The system supports operations such as instance management, operation log management, VPC management and Express Connect circuit management of bare metal instances, and O&M configurations to complete routine O&M operations on CGW.

> **Note:** By default, the CGW module is not displayed in the left-side navigation pane. To use this module, click **User Authorities** in the top navigation bar of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. In the left-side navigation pane of the page that appears, click **Menu** **Management**. On the Menu management page, find Cloud Gateways and click Modify in the Actions column. In the Edit menu items panel, turn on **Show**.

**Instance Management**

On the Instance Management page, you can manage the added CGW instances in a centralized manner and view the summary information about the CGW instances in the system.

**Display devices**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** > **Cloud Gateways**.
4. On the Cloud Gateway page, click the **Instance Management** tab. On the **Display**
**Devices** tab, view the instance details.
perations

If the number of CGW licenses in Deployment Planner is less than that of used CGW instances, the CGW instances without license authorization are in the Unauthorized state. In this case, you need to increase the number of CGW licenses. |

Click the **Stacked Networking Devices** tab. The gateway device information is displayed in the **Cloud Gateway Name**, **Manage IP Address**, **IBGP Role**, **Vendor**, and
**Model** columns. Perform the following steps to set and manage the Internal BGP (iBGP)
role of a gateway device: perations a. Find the device that you want to manage and click **Manage** in the **Actions** column. Alternatively, select multiple devices that you want to manage and click **Batch**
**Manage**.
b. Select an IBGP role from the **IBGP Role** drop-down list. The iBGP role specifies the role of a CGW instance in the environment. Valid values: Client, Deploy Client and RR on a Device, and Deploy RR on a Device.
**Client**: specifies that the gateway device serves as the client of an iBGP neighbor
and provides server access.
**Deploy Client and RR on a Device** : specifies that the gateway device serves as
the route reflector (RR) of an iBGP neighbor and provides server access.
**Deploy RR on a Device**: specifies that the gateway device serves as the RR of an
iBGP neighbor and does not provide server access.

> **Important:** The iBGP role configurations must meet the following networking requirements:
> Single-data center deployment: At least one group of gateway devices whose iBGP role is an RR and other devices whose iBGP role is a client are deployed in a single data center.
> Multi-data center deployment: One group of gateway devices whose iBGP role is an RR and other devices whose iBGP role is a client are deployed in at least two data centers.
> RR role recommendations:
> We recommend that you set the role to Deploy Client and RR on a Device.
> If you have higher network stability requirements, we recommend that you set the role to Deploy RR on a Device.

c. Click **OK**. Click the **Unstacked Networking Devices** tab. The gateway device information is displayed in the following columns: **Cloud Gateway Name 1**, **Management IP**
**Address 1**, **Cloud Gateway Name 2**, **Management IP Address 2**, **IBGP Role**,
**Vendor**, and **Model**. Perform the following steps to set and manage the iBGP role of a
gateway device: a. Find the device that you want to manage and click **Manage** in the **Actions** column. Alternatively, select multiple devices that you want to manage and click **Batch**
**Manage**.
perations b. Select an IBGP role from the **IBGP Role** drop-down list. The iBGP role specifies the role of a CGW instance in the environment. Valid values: Client, Deploy Client and RR on a Device, and Deploy RR on a Device.
**Client**: specifies that the gateway device serves as the client of an iBGP neighbor
and provides server access.
**Deploy Client and RR on a Device** : specifies that the gateway device serves as
the route reflector (RR) of an iBGP neighbor and provides server access.
**Deploy RR on a Device**: specifies that the gateway device serves as the RR of an
iBGP neighbor and does not provide server access.

> **Important:** The iBGP role configurations must meet the following networking requirements:
> Single-data center deployment: At least one group of gateway devices whose iBGP role is an RR and other devices whose iBGP role is a client are deployed in a single data center.
> Multi-data center deployment: One group of gateway devices whose iBGP role is an RR and other devices whose iBGP role is a client are deployed in at least two data centers.
> RR role recommendations:
> We recommend that you set the role to Deploy Client and RR on a Device.
> If you have higher network stability requirements, we recommend that you set the role to Deploy RR on a Device.

c. Click **OK**.

**Manage the IP address of a bare metal instance**

> In the Bare Metal IP Address Management panel, you can assign an IP address to a bare metal instance. This helps you configure the network of bare metal instances.

perations

**Background information**

CGW works with Bare Metal Management Service (BMS). BMS is used to install bare metal instances, assign IP addresses, and complete network configurations. CGW is used to connect bare metal instances to VPCs. In some scenarios, you may not install bare metal instances or complete network configurations by using BMS, but you must use CGW to connect bare metal instances to VPCs. In such scenarios, the system cannot assign IP addresses to bare metal instances, and you must manually maintain IP address assignment results. This may cause IP address conflicts and poor usability. Therefore, network management of bare metal instances is supported on the Cloud Gateway page. You can manage IP addresses of bare metal instances in the Bare Metal IP Address Management panel.

**Prerequisites**

The bare metal instance is connected to a VPC.
1. Find the bare metal instance and click **Manage** in the **Bare Metal IP Address** column.
2. In the **Bare Metal IP Address Management** panel, click **Apply for Bare Metal IP**
**Address**.
3. In the **Apply for Bare Metal IP Address** dialog box, configure the **Bare Metal NIC**, **IP**,
and **IP Address Description** parameters and click **OK**.

> **Note:** If you do not specify the IP parameter, an IP address is automatically generated.

4. After you apply for an IP address for a bare metal instance, view the IP address in the **Bare**
**Metal IP Address Management** panel.
Find the IP address of the bare metal instance and click **Edit** to change the IP address. Find the IP address of the bare metal instance and click **Release** to release the IP address.

by bare metal instance name on the **VPC Management** tab. If the bare metal instance is not displayed, it is released from the VPC.

###### 4.1.2.6.6 VBR management

A virtual border router (VBR) functions as a router between a customer-premises equipment (CPE) device and a virtual private cloud (VPC). VBRs route traffic between VPCs and data centers. This topic describes how to manage VBRs. perations
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.

that appears, configure the following parameters and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| BID | The bound ID. |
| Primary account ID | The ID of the virtual private cloud (VPC) to which you want to connect the VBR. |
| Region | The ID of the region in which the VBR is deployed. |
| Physical Connection ID | The ID of the Express Connect circuit that you want to connect to the VBR. |
| VLAN ID | The virtual local area network (VLAN) ID of the VBR. Valid values: 1 to 2999. Only the owner of the Express Connect circuit can specify or modify this parameter. |

| Peer IP address | The peer IP address of the Express Connect circuit. This parameter is required when the Express Connect circuit is not in the waiting state. Only the owner of the VBR can specify or modify this parameter. |
| Subnet mask | The subnet mask that connects the local and peer IP addresses. This parameter is required when the Express Connect circuit is not in the waiting state. Only the owner of the VBR can specify or modify this parameter. |
| VBR Name | The name of the VBR. The name can be 2 to 128 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |
| Description | The description of the VBR. The description can be 2 to 128 characters in length and cannot start with http:// or https:// . |

perations

| Owner Bid | The bound ID of the VBR owner. |

| Owner AliUid | The Apsara Stack account ID of the VBR owner. |
