###### 4.1.2.7.2 opsDNS domain service

This topic describes how to configure an opsDNS domain service.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Basic Network** > **opsDNS Management** >
**opsDNS Domain Service**.
4. On the **opsDNS Domain Service** page, view the domain name resolution information,
including **Domain Name**, **Resource Type**, **DNS Record**, and **TTL**. You can click **Advanced Filter** to filter DNS records by **Domain Name**, **Record Type**,
**Record Value**, or their combinations.
perations
**Domain Name**: The name of the DNS record. You can enter any string to search for a
domain name that contains the specified string. You can use an asterisk (*) to match multiple characters or a question mark (?) to match a single character. To search for a wildcard domain name, you must use a backward slash followed by an asterisk (\*) to represent an asterisk (*) in the domain name.
**Record Type**: The type of the DNS record. Valid values: **A**,**AAAA**, and **CNAME**.
**Record Value**: The value of the DNS record. For an A record, only one IPv4 address
string is allowed. For an AAAA record, only one IPv6 address string is allowed. For a CNAME record, only one FQDN domain name string is allowed, which ends with a period (.).

**Related operations**

**Creat a DNS record**

**Important**

1. Make sure that you know the scope of impact after you submit a Domain Name System
(DNS) record of a domain name. Pay attention to the potential impact of resolution type switching.
2. Operations on DNS records are idempotent. If you add DNS records of the same
resolution type to the same domain name, the new record overwrites the original one.
3. The time-to-live (TTL) of all DNS records under the same domain name and of the same
resolution type must be consistent. By default, the TTL configured for the DNS record that is added in the last operation prevails. The value of TTL is a positive integer of uint32.
4. CNAME records cannot coexist with records of other resolution types. Before you add a
CNAME record to a domain name, remove other records from the domain name. A domain name can have only one CNAME record.
5. You cannot add CNAME records to defined zones in the cloud, such as tbsite.net.
6. You can add domain names only to defined zones in the cloud. You cannot register a
domain name for a zone outside the cloud.
7. It takes 0 to 5 minutes for a new DNS record to take effect.
1. On the **opsDNS Domain Service** page, click **Create DNS Record**.
2. In the dialog box that appears, configure the parameters that are described in the following
table, and thenclick**OK.**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

perations

| Domain Name | The name of a DNS record. Note The domain name consists of a domain name prefix and a domain name suffix. The domain name prefix must meet the following format requirements: i. The domain name cannot contain underscores ( ). It can contain _ only letters, digits, and hyphens (-). ii. The domain name can be started only with letters or digits. iii. The domain name can be ended only with letters, digits, or periods (.). iv. A wildcard domain name is not allowed, which means that *. cannot be placed at the beginning of the domain name. |
|---|---|
| Resource Type | The resource type of the domain name resolution. Valid values: A AAAA CHAME Note i. CNAME cannot coexist with other DNS record types. ii. A domain name can have only one CNAME record. iii. You cannot add CNAME records to defined zones in the cloud, such as tbsite.net. |
| DNS Record | The IP address to which the domain name is mapped. Note i. An A record must be a valid IPv4 address. ii. An AAAA record must be a valid IPv6 address. iii. A CNAME record must be a valid domain name. The requirements for the character set and length of the domain name must be the same as the format requirements for the Domain Name parameter, but the CNAME value cannot be a generic domain name. |
| TTL | The TTL of a DNS record. |

perations

**View the details of a DNS record**

1. On the **opsDNS Domain Service** page, find the DNS record that you want to view and
click**Details** in the **Actions**columnto view the details of the record. You can filter DNS records by**Record Value**.
2. On the**opsDNS Resolution Settings**page, you can also perform the following operations:
**Create a DNS record**: Click**Create DNS Record**. In the Create DNS Record dialog box,
configure the parameters and click**OK**. It takes 0 to 5 minutes for a new DNS record to take effect. perations
**Delete a DNS record**: Find the DNS record that you want to delete and click**Delete** in
the **Actions**column. In the dialog box that appears, read the risk notice and enter
**DELETE**in the field, and then click**OK**.
After 0 to 5 minutes, the DNS record is deleted.

##### 4.1.2.9 Computing access gateways

You can use computing access gateways such as dedicated computing host switches (CHSWs) to connect intelligent computing servers to virtual private clouds (VPCs). This helps implement the centralized management of intelligent computing servers. The system supports operations such as instance management, operation log management, VPC management and Express Connect circuit management of bare metal instances, and O&M configurations to complete routine O&M operations on computing access gateways.

> **Note:** By default, the Computing Access Gateway module is not displayed in the left-side navigation pane. To use this module, click **User Authorities** in the top navigation bar of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. In the left-side navigation pane of the page that appears, click **Menu Management**. On the Menus page, find Computing Access Gateway and click Modify in the Actions column. In the Modify Menu panel, turn on **Show**.

**Manage access gateways**

a. View devices On the **Stacked Networking Devices** tab, you can view the following information about devices: **Computing Access Gateway Name**, **Manage IP Address**, **IBGP**

b. Configure the IBGP role for a device a. In the device list, find the device that you want to manage and click **Manage** in the

Alternatively, select multiple devices that you want to manage and click **Batch**

b. Select an IBGP role from the **IBGP Role** drop-down list. Then, click **OK**. The IBGP role specifies the role of the computing access gateway in the environment. Valid values: Client, Deploy Client and RR on a Device, and Deploy RR on a Device.
**Client**: The computing access gateway serves as the client of the IBGP peer and is
used only for server access.
**Deploy Client and RR on a Device** : The computing access gateway serves as
the RR reflective route of the IBGP peer and is used for server access.
**Deploy RR on a Device**: The computing access gateway serves only as the RR
reflective route of the IBGP peer and cannot be used for server access.

> **Important:** The following list describes the networking requirements for the IBGP role:
> Single-data center deployment: At least one set of computing access gateways is deployed, and the IBGP roles of the computing access gateways are RR roles. The IBGP roles of other devices are Client.
> Multi-data center deployment: A set of computing access gateways is deployed in at least two data centers, and the IBGP roles of the computing access gateways are RR roles. The IBGP roles of other devices are Client.
> RR role recommendations:
> We recommend that you set the role to Deploy Client and RR on A Device.
> If you have higher network stability requirements, we recommend that you set the role to Deploy RR on a Device.

**Manage the IP address of a bare metal instance**

Computing access gateways work with Bare Metal Management Service (BMS). BMS is used to install bare metal instances, assign IP addresses, and complete network configurations. Computing access gateways are used to connect bare metal instances to VPCs. In some scenarios, you may not install bare metal instances or complete network configurations by using BMS, but you must use computing access gateways to connect bare metal instances to VPCs. In such scenarios, the system cannot assign IP addresses to bare metal instances, and you must manually maintain IP address assignment results. This may cause IP address conflicts and poor usability. Therefore, network management of bare metal instances is supported on the Computing Access Gateway page. You can manage IP addresses of bare metal instances in the Bare Metal IP Address Management panel. a. In the bare metal instance list, find the bare metal instance that you want to manage and click **Manage** in the **Bare Metal IP Address** column. b. In the **Bare Metal IP Address Management** panel, click **Apply for Bare Metal IP**
**Address**.
c. In the **Apply for Bare Metal IP Address** dialog box, configure the **Bare Metal NIC**,
**IP**, and **IP Address Description** parameters and click **OK**.

> **Note:** If you leave the **IP** parameter empty, the system automatically generates an IP address.

perations d. After you apply for an IP address for a bare metal instance, view the IP address in the
**Bare Metal IP Address Management** panel. The IP address information includes **ID**,
**IP Address**, **Bare Metal Name/SN**, **Bare Metal NIC**, **Created At**, **Modified At**,
**Description**, **VPC ID**, and **vswitch id**.
Find the bare metal IP address that you want to manage and click **Edit** in the
**Actions** column to modify the **IP** and **IP Address Description** parameters.
Find the bare metal IP address that you want to manage and click **Release** in the
**Actions** column to release the bare metal IP address.

**Apply for a bare metal instance in a VPC**

In O&M emergency scenarios, you can use this feature to add the physical port of the computing access gateway associated with a bare metal instance to the VPC.

> **Warning:** This operation is only for emergency scenarios and must be performed under the guidance of R&D engineers. Otherwise, normal business operations may be affected.
> This feature can be used only to connect a bare metal instance to the port of a computing access gateway but cannot be used to perform operations on the bare metal instance. To configure the network port, IP address, and routing information of the bare metal instance, contact the corresponding product team for guidance.
> In most cases, you cannot use this feature to apply for a bare metal instance in a VPC. You can use the bare metal controller to call an API operation to enable the bare metal network.

**View trunk usage**

You can view trunk usage to obtain up-to-date information about the usage of hardware ports. i. Select **View Trunk Usage** from the drop-down list in the upper-left corner of the tab. perations ii. View the trunk usage in the list. By default, all data in the **idle** state is displayed. and then click **Search** to view the bare metal instance VPNs assigned to all the HSWs. Valid values of the **Status** parameter are **Succeeded** and **Creating**.

#### 4.1.3 Networking services

perations

##### 4.1.3.1 SLB O&M

###### 4.1.3.1.1 SLB cluster management

After you add tags to Server Load Balancer (SLB) clusters, you can easily select clusters in the tenant console. This improves the usability of SLB clusters.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Products** > **SLB O&M** > **SLB Cluster**
**Management**.
4. On the SLB Cluster Management page, select a region ID and click **Search** to view the
cluster information.
5. Find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Edit Tag** in the **Actions** column. In the
dialog box that appears, modify the tag name and click **OK**.

> **Note:** The default cluster tag named **default** cannot be modified.

###### 4.1.3.1.2 SLB management

The SLB Management page displays Layer 4 service resources and monitoring and O&M information of Server Load Balancer (SLB) clusters and SLB instances.

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll is deployed and has reached the desired state.

**SLB clusters**

The SLB Cluster tab displays the basic information, maximum inbound bits per second (BPS), maximum outbound BPS, maximum inbound packets per second (PPS), maximum outbound PPS, maximum number of active connections, maximum number of inactive connections, and usage data of a single node in an SLB cluster.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **SLB O&M** > **SLB**
**Management**.
perations
4. On the **SLB Management** tab, click the **SLB Cluster** tab, and select the cluster that you
want to view from the **Cluster** drop-down list. You can then view information displayed in the **Node Information** and **Cluster Resource Usage** sections. In the **Node Information** section, you can view node information in the columns, including **Node IP Address**, **Working Status**, **Local IP Address**, **Service Unit**, **Site**
**ID**, and **LVS Group ID**.
**View node details**: Click **Details** in the **Actions** column of the node that you want to
view to go to the **SLB Node Details** page. Then, you can view **Node Information** and
**Usage Data**.
perations The **Node Information** section displays the following information: **IP**, **Working**
**Status**, **Local CIDR Block**, **ENIs**, **LVS Group ID**, **Proxy Check Type**, **Site ID**,
**Maximum Active Connections**, **Maximum Inactive Connections**, **Inbound BPS**
**Limit**, **Outbound BPS Limit**, **Inbound PPS Limit**, and **Outbound PPS Limit**.
In the **Usage Data** section, specify **Start and End Time** to view the usage data of the node within the specified time range. For more information about the definitions of the metrics, see the Node and instance usage metrics section of this topic.

> **Note:** The interval between the start time and end time must not exceed 12 hours.
> You can click **Last5Minutes**, **Last30Minutes**, **Last1Hour**, or **Last6Hours** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of all metrics at the point in time.

In the **Cluster Resource Usage** section, specify a time range to view the usage data of the cluster within the specified time range. You can click the **Core Metrics** or **All**
**indicators** tab to view the corresponding information. For more information about the
definitions of the metrics, see Cluster usage metrics.

> **Note:** The interval between the start time and end time must not exceed 12 hours.
> You can click **Last 1 Hour**, **Last 3 Hours**, **Last 6 Hours**, or **Last 12 Hours** to query the usage data within the specified time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of all metrics at the point in time.

**SLB instances**

perations The SLB Instances tab displays the basic information and usage data of SLB instances, including the inbound and outbound BPS and PPS.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **SLB O&M** > **SLB**
**Management**.
4. On the **SLB Management** page, click the **SLB Instances** tab to view the information
about the SLB instances in the columns, including **IP Address**, **Instance ID**, **Network**
**Type**, **Product**, **Zone**, and **Updated At**.
Click **Advanced Filter** and filter SLB instances by **IP Address Version**, **IP Address**,
**Instance ID**, **Product Name**, **Network Type**, or any combination of them.
5. Click **Details** in the **Actions** column of an SLB instance to go to the **SLB Instance Details**
page. On this page, you can view **Instance Information**, **Server Group Information**, and **Usage Data**. perations In the **Instance Information** section, view the basic information about the SLB instance, which can be used by O&M engineers to troubleshoot faults and confirm the ownership of the device. You can click **Modify** next to the **Throttling Rule** parameter to modify the throttling rule of the SLB instance.

> **Note:** You can set the maximum throttling value to 10 for an SLB instance that supports 10 Gigabit Ethernet or 15 for an SLB instance that supports 40 Gigabit Ethernet. Unit: Gbit/s.

In the **Server Group Information** section, view the server group information of the SLB instance, including **Server Group** and **Listener Name**. To view the weight modification details, click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of the desired server group. perations Modify weights a. Click **Modify Weight** in the **Actions** column of a server group. In the panel that appears, change the values in the **Weight** column and click **OK**. perations b. In the message that appears, confirm the information and click **OK**. perations

> **Note:** After maintenance or emergency repair is performed, we recommend that you restore the weight settings. When you perform zone-disaster recovery across two data centers, the system restores the default weight settings. The restored weight settings take effect after your confirmation.
> If an SLB instance is enabled by a tenant, you can go to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console to modify the weight settings of the SLB instance.

In the **Usage Data** section, specify **Start/End Time** to view the usage data of the SLB instance within the specified time range. For more information about the definitions of the metrics, see the Node and instance usage metrics section of this topic.

> **Note:** The interval between the start time and end time must not exceed 12 hours.
> You can click **Last5Minutes**, **Last30Minutes**, **Last1Hour**, or **Last6Hours** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of all metrics at the point in time.

Click **Details** in the upper-right corner of the resource usage chart to view the details of the resource usage of backend servers. perations

**Management**.
perations
4. On the **XGW Cluster Management** page, select a region from the **Region** drop-down list

> **Note:** Only x86-based physical machines can be managed.

**Zone List**: displays the following information: **Region**, **Zone**, and **Secondary Zone**.
**Cluster Topology**: displays the cluster topology.

**Related operations**

**Configure a secondary zone**

> **Note:** You can perform this operation on zones for which the secondary zone is not configured.

1. Find the zone that you want to manage and click **Set Secondary Zone** in the **Actions**
column.
2. In the dialog box that appears, specify **Secondary Zone** and click **OK**.

> **Note:** The cluster that you select as the secondary zone must have the same architecture and reside in the same region as the current cluster.
> The secondary zone that you select cannot be the secondary zone of another zone.

perations

**Remove a secondary zone**

> **Note:** You can perform this operation on zones for which the secondary zone is configured.

1. Find the zone that you want to manage and click **Remove Secondary Zone** in the
**Actions** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**View the change history of a zone**

1. Find the zone that you want to manage and click **View Change History** in the **Actions**
column.
2. In the **View Change History** dialog box, view the change history of the zone.
3. The change history information includes **Workflow ID**, **Plan Name**, **Type**, **Execution**
**Time**, **Execution Result**, **Executed By**, **Description**, and **Execution Parameters**.
4. Find the change record that you want to manage and click **View details** in the **Actions**
column. On the **Execution Details** page, view details of the change record. For more information, see View change plans. perations

###### 4.1.3.3.2 XGW management

The XGW Management module allows you to manage virtual private cloud (VPC) gateways and view the usage data of device nodes and service instances.

**View XGW clusters**

The XGW Management module allows you to view the basic information, status, aggregated traffic, and usage of each device node of XGW clusters.

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll is deployed and has reached the desired state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **XGW O&M** > **XGW**
**Management**.
4. On the **XGW Management** page, click the **XGW Cluster** tab and select a cluster from the
**Cluster** drop-down list to obtain the **Node Information** and **Aggregated Traffic**
information of all devices in the cluster. perations In the **Node Information** section, view the node information. The node information includes **Hostname**, **IDC**, **IP**, and **State**. Find the node that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column. In the panel that appears, view the usage metrics of the node. By default, the data within the last hour is displayed. perations For more information about the metrics, see Cluster-related metrics. perations

> **Note:** You can specify **Start and End Time** to view the usage data of the cluster within the specified time range.
> You can select **Last1Hour**, **Last3Hours**, **Last6Hours**, or **Last1Day** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of the corresponding metrics.
> You can click a metric to view the usage trend chart of the metric.

In the **Aggregated Traffic** section, the system displays the traffic data of device nodes in the current cluster over the last hour by default. For more information about the metrics, see Cluster-related metrics.

> **Note:** You can specify **Start and End Time** to view the usage data of the cluster within the specified time range.
> You can select **Last1Hour**, **Last3Hours**, **Last6Hours**, or **Last1Day** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of the corresponding metrics.
> You can click a metric to view the usage trend chart of the metric.

perations

> **Note:** You can perform this operation on zones for which no secondary zone is configured.

1. Find the zone that you want to manage and click **Set Secondary Zone** in the **Actions**
column.
2. In the dialog box that appears, specify **Secondary Zone** and click **OK**.

> **Note:** The zone that you select as the secondary zone must have the same architecture and reside in the same region as the current cluster.
> The secondary zone that you select cannot be the secondary zone of another zone.

**View the change history of a zone**

column.

The change history information includes **Workflow ID**, **Scheme name**, **Type**, **Execution**
**time**, **Execution result**, **Executor**, **Description**, and **Execution Parameters**.
perations

column. On the **Execution Details** page, view details of the change record. For more information, see View change plans.

###### 4.1.3.4.2 CGW management

The CGW Management module allows you to view the basic information, status, aggregated traffic, and usage of each device node of Cloud Gateway (CGW) clusters.

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll has been deployed and has reached the desired state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **CGW O&M** > **CGW**
**Management**.
4. On the **CGW Management**page, click the **CGW Cluster** tab and select a cluster from the
**Cluster** drop-down list to obtain the **Node Information** and **Aggregate Traffic**
information of all devices in the cluster. perations In the **Node Information** section, view the node information. The node information includes **Hostname**, **IDC**, **IP**, and **State**. Find the node that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column. In the panel that appears, view the usage data of the node. By default, the data within the last one hour is displayed. For more information about metrics, see Metric definitions. perations perations

> **Note:** You can specify **Start and End Time** to view the usage data of the cluster within the specified time range.
> The interval between the start time and end time cannot exceed 24 hours.
> You can select **Last1Hour**, **Last3Hours**, **Last6Hours**, or **Last1Day** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of all metrics at that point in time.
> You can click a metric to view the usage trend chart of the metric.

In the **Aggregate Traffic** section, the system displays the traffic data of device nodes in the current cluster within the last one hour by default. For more information about metrics, see Metric definitions.

> **Note:** You can specify **Start and End Time** to view the usage data of the cluster within the specified time range.
> The interval between the start time and end time cannot exceed 24 hours.
> You can select **Last1Hour**, **Last3Hours**, **Last6Hours**, or **Last1Day** to query the usage data within the selected time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in a chart to view the values of all metrics at that point in time.
> You can click a metric to view the usage trend chart of the metric.

##### 4.1.3.7 VPC O&M

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **VPC O&M** > **VPC-On-ECS**.
4. On the **VPC-On-ECS** page, view the virtual private cloud (VPC) list. By default, VPCs in **All**
**Status** are displayed.
The VPC information is displayed in the following columns: **Region**, **VPC**, **Version**,
**Status**, and **Created At**.
Click **Advanced Filter** and filter VPCs by **VPC ID**, **Status**, **Created At**, or any combination of them. perations
5. Find the VPC that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column or click the
instance ID in the **VPC** column. On the **VPC Details** page, you can view the details of the VPC and its related resources.
**VPC Instance Information**: This section displays **Instance ID**, **Instance Name**,
**Region**, **Owner**, **IPv4 CIDR Block**, **IPv6 CIDR Block**, **Created At**, **Status**, and
**Description** of the VPC.
**vRouter Information**: This section displays **Instance ID**, **System Route Table Name**,
**Created At**, **Description**, and **System Route Table ID**.
Click the ID next to **System Route Table ID** to view the details of the route table.
**Route Table Information**: This section displays **Instance ID**, **System Route Table**
**ID**, **System Route Table Name**, **Created At**, **Description**, and **VPC ID**.
perations
**Route Entries**: This tab displays the following information: **Destination CIDR Block**,
**Status**, **Name**, **Next Hop**, **Type**, and **Remarks**.
**Associated vSwitches**: This tab displays the following information: **vSwitch**, **Name**,
**Status**, and **Destination CIDR Block**.
**vSwitches**: This section displays **Instance ID**, **CIDR Block**, **Capacity**, **Owner**, **Region**,
**Zone**, **Created At**, and **Remarks** about vSwitches.
Click **Advanced Filter** and filter vSwitches by **Instance ID**, **Owner**, **Zone**, **Created At**, or any combination of them.
**Create a vSwitch**: Click **Create vSwitch**. In the dialog box that appears, configure
the following parameters and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Zone | The ID of the zone to which the vSwitch belongs. |
| CIDR Block | The IPv4 CIDR block of the vSwitch. |
| Usage | The purpose of the vSwitch. Valid values: Alibaba Cloud Service Container Network |
| Description | The description of the vSwitch. |

perations
**Delete a vSwitch**: Find a vSwitch that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the
**Actions** column. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

> **Important:** After you delete a vSwitch, the vSwitch cannot be restored. Proceed with caution.

###### 4.1.3.7.2 VPC workflows

This topic describes how to view and manage Business Foundation System workflows in virtual private clouds (VPCs).
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Services** > **VPC O&M** > **VPC**
**Workflow**.
4. On the **Workflow Management** page, view and manage Business Foundation System
workflows in VPCs. perations VPC workflow information includes **Workflow Name**, **Request ID**, **AliUid**, **InstanceId**,
**RegionNo,****Start Time**, **End Time**, and **Execution Node**.
Click **Advanced Filter** and specify the following parameters to filter workflows.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Workflow Name | The name of the workflow. |
| Execution Status | The status of the task. Valid values: SCHEDULABLE: schedulable RUNNING: running PAUSED: suspended. HUMAN PROCESSING: in manual processing _ COMPLETED: complete FAILED: failed TIMEOUT: timed out |
| Request ID | The request ID of the task. |
| AliUid | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| InstanceId | The ID of the instance on which the workflow runs. |

**View workflow details**: Find the workflow that you want to view and click **Details** in
the **Actions** column. On the **Workflow Details Page**, view the information on the
**Activity Details** and **Activity Summary** tab.
On the Activity Details tab, view the workflow details in the following columns: **Activity**
**ID**, **Activity Name**, **Method**, **Execution Status**, **Input**, **Output**, **Failure Cause**,
**Start Time**, and **End Time**.
perations Select an execution status from the **Execution Status** drop-down list to filter activities. In the activity list, find the activity that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Input** or **Output** column. In the message that appears, you can view the process details.
**Terminate a workflow**: Find the workflow that you want to manage, and click
**Terminate** in the **Actions** column to terminate the workflow.
**Retry a workflow**: Find the workflow that you want to manage, and click **Retry** in the
**Actions** column to re-run the workflow.

#### 4.1.4 Network monitoring and alerting

##### 4.1.4.1 Network alert dashboard

The Network Alert Dashboard module displays the alert information of all network components on the platform.

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll has been deployed and has reached the desired state. perations
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Monitoring & Alerting** > **Network**
**Alert Dashboard**.
4. On the **Current Alerts** tab, view the alerts of all network components on the platform. You
can search for alerts by **device name**, **device IP address**, or **alert rule name**.
5. Click **Details** in the **Alert Details** column of an alert to view detailed information about the
alert.
6. Find the reason why an alert is triggered and then handle the alert.
If you have confirmed that the alert does not affect the operation of the system, click
**Ignore** in the **Operation** column. In the message that appears, click **OK** to ignore the
alert. If you have confirmed that the alert is meaningless, click **Delete** in the **Operation** column. In the message that appears, click **OK** to delete the alert. After the alert is handled, you can query it on the **Alert History** tab. Click **View** in the
**Alert Details** column of the alert to view detailed information about the alert.

**What to do next**

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Export alert information | 1. Click Export Table. 2. In the message that appears, click OK to export the alert information to your local device. |
| Delete all alerts | 1. Click Delete All. 2. In the message that appears, click OK to delete all alerts. |

##### 4.1.4.2 Network alert settings

perations

###### 4.1.4.2.1 Monitoring rule management

You can associate the monitoring metrics of a monitored instance with an alert template. When the value of a metric meets the conditions specified in the alert template, an alert event is triggered.

**Prerequisites**

###### 4.1.4.2.3 Trap template settings

This topic describes how to configure and manage trap alert rules of network devices. If the initially configured trap subscriptions do not meet the monitoring requirements, you can add a trap to enhance monitoring coverage. perations

**Prerequisites**

The NetworkBaseServiceCluster cluster for BaseServiceAll is deployed and at desired state.

**Background information**

Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) traps are used in this topic. SNMP trap is a part of SNMP and is a mechanism that enables the managed network devices, such as vSwitches and vRouters, to send SNMP messages to the Network Operation Center (NOC) monitoring server. If an exception occurs on the device being monitored or the vSwitch metrics have an exception, the SNMP agent that is running in the vSwitch sends an alert event to the NOC monitoring server.

**Add a trap**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Monitoring & Alerting** > **Network**
**Alert Settings** > **Trap Template Setting**.
4. On the Trap Template Setting page, click **Create Trap**. In the Create Trap dialog box,
configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Trap Name | The name of the alert event. | linkdown or BGPneighbor down. You can customize the value. |

perations

| Trap OID | The object identifier (OID) of the alert event. | .1.3.6.1.4.1.25506.8.35.12.1.12 The value must be configured based on the device document and cannot be customized. |
|---|---|---|
| Trap Type | The type of the alert event. Valid values: Operation Hardware Protocol Others | N/A |
| Trap Index | The index ID of the alert item. The key-value pair in trap messages, which is used to identify alert objects. Typically, the value of this parameter can be an API name, a protocol ID, or an index ID. You can specify multiple values for this parameter. | The value must be configured based on the device document and cannot be customized. |
| Trap Msg | The message of the alert item. The key-value pair in trap messages, which is used to identify the alert data. Typically, the value of this parameter can be the additional information about the alert item, such as a message about the location of the state machine, a message about the current status, or a system message. You can specify multiple values for this parameter. | The value must be configured based on the device document and cannot be customized. |
| Alert Type | The type of the alert. Valid values: Fault Restore | N/A |
| Alert Association | Specifies whether the alert has a corresponding recovery alert. Note If you select Recovered, you must configure the settings of the associated alert trap. | N/A |

5. Click **OK**. After the configurations are submitted, the system checks whether the values of
the Trap OID and Trap Name parameters are unique. If yes, the trap is added. perations After the trap is added, the alert events of the configured Trap OID are monitored and are displayed on the **Current Alerts** and **Alert History** tabs of **Network Alert Dashboard**.

**What to do next**

**View the alert details of a trap**

1. On the Trap Template Setting page, view the following information about traps: **Trap**
**Name**, **Trap OID**, **Trap Type**, **Recovery Alert**, **Alert Type**, and **Alert Details**.
2. Select **By Name**, **By OID**, or **Type** from the Query Type drop-down list to query a trap.
3. Find the trap that you want to view and move the pointer over **Details** in the **Alert Details**
column to view the alert details of the trap.

**Export trap information**

On the Trap Template Setting page, click **Export Table** to export all trap information to your on-premises machine. In the message that appears, click OK.

**Delete a trap**

1. Find the trap that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Operation** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

##### 4.1.5.6 Network health assessment

The Network Health Assessment module evaluates and diagnoses the health status of each layer of the network based on the dimensions such as performance, capacity, function, and status. This module provides an overview of the network health status and detects issues and risks at all layers of the network in real time to ensure that the network runs as expected.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Intelligent Diagnostics** > **Network Health**
**Assessment**.
4. On the Network Health Assessment page, view the health assessment information of
different network layers in the health overview list.

| Evaluation level name | Description | Dimension |
|---|---|---|

perations

| network product controller | The Network Health Assessment module checks the alerts on the control planes of services such as Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Server Load Balancer (SLB), Alibaba Cloud DNS (DNS), and Network Services Platform (NSP), and identifies issues at the earliest opportunity by checking the monitoring data of the services. | Status health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |
|---|---|---|
| network product instance | The Network Health Assessment module detects the access and configuration issues of a network service instance at the earliest opportunity by checking the features and configurations of the network service instance. | Functional health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |
| overlay network layer | The Network Health Assessment module comprehensively evaluates the health status of services such as eXtreme Global Workspace (XGW), Apsara Virtual Switch (AVS), Content Switched Network (CSW), Converged Gateway (CGW), Smart Network Appliance (SNA), and Hybrid Switch (HSW) by checking the monitoring results of the physical servers, network element nodes, and packet loss of the services. | Status health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |
| physical layer | The Network Health Assessment module evaluates the health status of devices by monitoring the core metrics of the devices. | Performance health assessment score, capacity health assessment score, status health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |
| protocol layer | The Network Health Assessment module checks the status of routing protocols, such as Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) and Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). | Capacity health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |
| network layer | The Network Health Assessment module comprehensively evaluates the health status of the network layer by checking the monitoring data of interconnection status of devices, physical interface of the network, intelligent prediction of the optical module, and network interface controllers (NICs). | Performance health assessment score, status health assessment score, total number of normal and diagnostic items, and overall score of this layer (percentage system) |

5. In the health overview list, find an evaluation layer whose details you want to view and click
**Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the **Health Details** page.
perations In the **KPI details** section, view the list of KPIs. You can click **Advanced Filter** to filter KPIs by **KPI name**, **Status**, **Network**

**Ownership Type**, **Manufacturer**, **Model**, **Status**, **Failure probability**, **Expected**
**residual life**, **Intelligent analysis results**, **Bias current alarm threshold** ,

**Received power**. By default, the metric data of the last week is displayed.

> You can click **Last 7 Days**, **Last 15 days**, **Last 30 days**, or **Last 90** **days** to query the metrics of optical transceiver modules within a specific time range.
> You can move the pointer over a point in time in the chart to view the values of the corresponding metrics.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|

perations

| Temperatu re (°C) | TEMPERAT URE | The temperature of an optical transceiver module affects the performance and life of the optical transceiver module. If the temperature is excessively high or low, the performance of the optical transceiver module may be damaged and the life of the optical transceiver module may be shortened. Excessively high temperature may affect the transmission distance and rate of the optical transceiver module. In addition, the performance of the light emitter and the detector may be compromised, which results in a failure of the optical transceiver module. Excessively low temperature affects the performance and life of the optical transceiver module. |
|---|---|---|
| Bias current (mA) | BIAS CUR _ RENT | The bias current of an optical transceiver module is used to stimulate the laser to emit optical signals and affects the output power of the laser and the transmission distance of the optical transceiver module. Excessively large bias current may cause aging and damage of the laser and shorten the life of the optical transceiver module. Excessively small bias current may lower the output power of the laser and shorten the transmission distance. |
| Voltage (mV) | VOLTAGE | The voltage of an optical transceiver module refers to the voltage that is used to stimulate the laser to emit optical signals and the receiver to receive optical signals. If the voltage is unstable or deviates from the specified range, the optical transceiver module may fail or its performance may degrade. If the voltage is lower than expected, the transmit power of the optical transceiver module may be decreased. If the voltage is higher than expected, the optical transceiver module may fail. |
| Transmit power (dBM) | TX POWER _ | The transmit power of an optical transceiver module refers to the power of the laser to emit optical signals. The transmit power of the optical transceiver module affects the transmission distance and rate of the optical transceiver module. Excessively high transmit power may damage the optical transceiver module. Excessively low transmit power may shorten the transmission distance. |

perations

| Received power (dBM) | RX POWER _ | The received power of an optical transceiver module refers to the power of the receiver to receive optical signals. The received power of the optical transceiver module affects the receiver sensitivity and transmission performance of the optical transceiver module. If the received power exceeds the specified range, issues such as signal transmission interruption, error increase, and transmission distance decrease may occur. In this case, you can monitor the received power to identify and resolve issues at the earliest opportunity. If the received power is higher than expected, you can decrease the transmit power or check the length of the jointed fiber. If the received power is lower than expected, you can increase the transmit power or check the quality of the jointed fiber. |
|---|---|---|

You can use the feature to check and analyze whether a CIDR block contains another CIDR block or is contained in another CIDR block.

The IP address pool feature is applicable to scenarios such as multi-cloud geo-disaster recovery and hybrid clouds. This feature allows you to perform the following operations: Multiple cloud services are deployed in a cloud instance. In O&M scenarios such as network changes and security reviews, you can obtain the CIDR blocks of cloud services based on your business requirements to analyze the scope of changes and security policies. The IP address pool feature allows you to view the CIDR block of each cloud service in a cloud instance. You can also use this feature to add custom CIDR blocks. perations

##### 4.1.6.4 Cloud instance management

This topic describes how to manage the lifecycle of cloud instances, including creating instances, deleting instances, and querying instance status.

**Create a cloud instance**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Network Resources** > **Cloud Instance**
**Management**.
4. On the **Cloud Instance Management** page, choose **Create Instance** > **Create**
**Instance**.
5. On the **Create Instance** page, perform the following steps to create an instance.

**Step 1: Create a VPC**

In the **Create VPC** step, configure the following parameters and click **Create**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Region ID | The ID of the region in which the virtual private cloud (VPC) resides. |
| Cloud Service Instance ID | The ID of the cloud instance. By default, the ID of a random cloud instance is displayed. |
| Tunnel Type | The tunnel type The default value is AnyTunnel. Valid values: SingleTunnel: specifies a SingleTunnel virtual IP address (VIP) that allows a single Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance in the VPC to access external cloud services. AnyTunnel: specifies an AnyTunnel VIP that allows all ECS instances in the VPC to access the specified cloud service. |
| IpVersion | The protocol. The default value is IPv4. Valid values: IPv4 IPv6 |
| CloudInstance IP | The VIP that you want to assign to the instance. If you do not specify a VIP, the system automatically assigns one. |

perations

| vSwitch ID | This parameter is available only when the Tunnel Type parameter is set to SingleTunnel. The ID of any vSwitch in the VPC to which the ECS instance that needs to access external cloud services belongs. |
|---|---|
| UID | This parameter is available only when the Tunnel Type parameter is set to SingleTunnel. The UID of the user that creates the vSwitch. This parameter is required if the user is not the API caller. |
| BID | This parameter is available only when the Tunnel Type parameter is set to SingleTunnel. The BID of the user that creates the vSwitch. This parameter is required if the user is not the API caller. |
| CIDR Type | This parameter is available only when the Tunnel Type parameter is set to AnyTunnel. The CIDR type. Valid values: Link local (Regular Cloud Services): The AnyTunnel VIP assigned to _ Application Load Balancer (ALB) is allocated from a subnet that does not belong to 100.100.100.0/24. Special Inner (ECS META Server) Service: The AnyTunnel VIP assigned to ALB is allocated from a subnet that belongs to 100.100.100.0/24. |

#### 4.1.7 Traffic visualization

The Traffic Visualization module can monitor physical and virtual networks in the cloud platform, and analyze real-time and historical traffic in the networks. This module also analyzes traffic by virtual network, public network, and border physical network and generates visualized charts. You can also troubleshoot issues based on the traffic data or monitored traffic metrics.

> **Note:** By default, the Traffic Visualization module is not displayed. To use this module, perform the following operations: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. In the top navigation bar, choose More > **User Authorities**. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Menu Management**. On the Menu management page, modify the menu settings to display the Traffic Visualization module.

##### 4.1.7.1 Visual settings

Before you use traffic visualization, you must configure items such as analyzers, collection rules, and scenarios to collect, process, and analyze traffic based on your business requirements.

**Workflow**

The following flowchart shows how to initialize traffic visualization.
1. Create an analyzer and an analysis port. For more information, see Manage analysis
devices.
2. Create a collection rule. For more information, see Manage collection rules.
3. Create an analysis scenario. For more information, see Manage scenarios.

**Manage analysis devices**

perations Analysis devices include analyzers and analysis ports. The collection and analysis of traffic depend on the analysis devices. Before you collect and analyze traffic, you must create the required analysis devices.

**Usage notes**

An **analyzer**, also known as a network performance monitor (NPM), refers to a device that performs traffic analysis. The following types of analyzers are supported: NPM physical machines and NPM central control machines. An **analysis port**refers to the traffic collection port of an NPM device. Traffic is received on the port for collection and analysis.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation** > **Networking** > **Network**
**Operations Console**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Traffic Visualization** > **Visual Settings**.
4. On the **System Management** page, click the **Analyze Device Management** tab. On this
tab, you can perform operations that are described in the following table.

Valid values: NPM physical machine: collects and processes traffic. NPM central control machine: displays traffic analysis results. Galaxy Security Gateway: preferentially forwards traffic to the traffic gateway when you configure virtual private cloud (VPC) traffic mirroring rules. #### 4.1.8 Platform management

##### 4.1.8.1 Metric management

###### 4.1.8.1.1 TSDB clusters

This topic describes how to query time series database (TSDB) clusters and view the details of stored time series metrics.

## 5 Storage operations

#### 5.1.1 Operations Guide

##### 5.1.1.1 Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console

**Operations Console**

This topic describes how users such as O&M engineers log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

**Prerequisites**

The endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console and the username and password that are used to log in to the console are obtained from a deployment engineer or an administrator. The endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console is in the following format: regi on-id.ops.console.intranet-domain-id. A supported browser is used. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.
1. Open your browser.
2. In the address bar, enter the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
Press the ENTER key. erations

> **Note:** You can click the current language in the upper-right corner to switch to another language. Simplified Chinese and English are supported.

3. Enter your username and password.
erations

> **Note:** Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Operations Console from a deployment engineer or an administrator.

If you enter an invalid password for three consecutive times, the system enables the image verification logon feature. If you enter an invalid password for five consecutive times, the account is locked. Contact the administrator to unlock the account.

> The first time that you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console, change the password for your username as prompted.
> To enhance security, your password must meet the following requirements:
> The password contains uppercase and lowercase letters.
> The password contains digits.
> The password contains at least one of the following special characters: ! @ # $ %
> The password is 10 to 20 characters in length.

4. Click **Agree to Private Policy and Log On** .

##### 5.1.1.2 Feature overview

Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS is a centralized O&M platform for CDS. CDS-OPS allows you to perform routine O&M on storage clusters and the cloud services that are deployed in the storage clusters, such as Object Storage Service (OSS), Elastic Block Storage (EBS), and Simple Log Service (SLS). This topic describes the features of CDS-OPS. You can use these features based on your business requirements.

> **Note:** If you have questions when you use the features of CDS-OPS, contact Apsara Stack technical support.

**Service overview**

On the CDS-Overview page, you can view the overall information about CDS as O&M engineers, such as the total capacity usage, current alerts, used capacity distribution in different storage services, hardware resources, storage resources, and cluster status. This way, you can understand the overall information about CDS and handle exceptions at the earliest opportunity. For more information, see Service overview.

**Storage management**

As O&M engineers, you can use the storage management features to manage cloud services such as EBS, OSS, and SLS, including their capacity usage and clusters. The following tables describe the storage management features.

> **Note:** The cloud services deployed in and features supported by a cluster vary based on the cluster type. The actual situation prevails.

**CDS-EBS and EBS-2.0 clusters**

erations You can use CDS-OPS to manage CDS-EBS clusters and EBS-1.0 or EBS-2.0 clusters. CDS-OPS provides the same features for CDS-EBS clusters and managed EBS-2.0 clusters.

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Overview of EBS clusters | On the Cluster O&M page, you can view the capacity usage, I/O hangs, resource overview, and current alerts of EBS clusters. You can also view a list of EBS clusters to understand the overall information about the clusters and handle exceptions at the earliest opportunity. |
| Manage cluster details | On the Cluster Details page, you can perform the following operations as needed: View cluster overview. View capacity information. Monitor clusters: allows you to view cluster monitoring information and view the monitoring information of BlockServer nodes. Configure clusters: allows you to configure block rebalance, configure the erasure coding (EC) mode, and configure PANGU. Manage services: allows you to manage BlockMaster nodes, manage BlockServer nodes, manage snapshot servers, and manage PANGU. Manage hosts. |
| View compute nodes | Compute nodes are used to run computing tasks in a cluster. On the Compute Node page, CDS-OPS allows you to view the information about compute nodes in clusters, Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances on compute nodes, and disks associated with ECS instances. This way, you can understand the association among compute nodes, ECS instances, and disks, and quickly identify the compute nodes with abnormal TDC status. |
| Manage storage sets | On the Storage Set page, you can search for an EBS storage set by cluster name or storage set ID, and then perform the following operations to manage the storage set: view the information about the storage set, view disks in the storage set, view capacity usage in each partition of the storage set, and modify the clusters in each partition of the storage set. |
| Manage disks | On the Disk page, you can view the information about disks in all clusters, such as the attributes and monitoring information of disks. EBS-2.0 clusters and CDS- EBS clusters allow you to modify the maximum IOPS and throughput of disks in the clusters. |
| Migrate disks (hot migration) | On the Hot Migration of Disks page, you can create hot migration tasks to migrate disks between EBS clusters. The disks can still be used during the migration. This improves the O&M efficiency of disks. |

erations

| Perform canary O&M | On the Canary O&M page, you can initiate canary O&M tasks to run a common O&M command on multiple hosts at a time. This simplifies O&M operations and minimizes the impact in case of a failure. You can stop running an O&M command at the earliest opportunity if the exit code of the command results is not 0. You can also specify a speed and an observation period for a canary O&M task. This way, the canary O&M task can run an O&M command at an appropriate speed on the specified hosts. During a canary O&M task, you can view the progress and results in real time. |

In the monitoring center, you can select resources on the Resource Monitoring page and view the detailed metrics of the resources on the custom dashboard, view the monitoring data of resources, view the monitoring data of storage metrics, and view the monitoring data of services.

| Handle current alerts | The alerts that are managed by CDS-OPS come from CDS clusters and the clusters that are managed by CDS-OPS. After alerts are triggered in the system, you can view the list of alerts and the details of each alert, including the alert name, module, cluster name, description, resource name, and alert time. We recommend that you handle alerts at the earliest opportunity by confirming or clearing the alerts based on your business requirements. |
| View historical alerts | Alerts that are automatically or manually cleared are displayed on the Alert History page. You can view the information about the alerts within the specified time range, including the alert name, module, cluster name, description, resource name, alert time, auto recovery status, and confirmation status. |

**Routine inspection**

Routine inspection allows you to inspect clusters on a regular basis.

erations

| SLA monitoring | The system monitors the key service level agreement (SLA) metrics of CDS in real time. This provides availability monitoring guarantee for scenarios such as software update, configuration change, and service O&M. This allows you to detect system exceptions at the earliest opportunity, and minimizes the impact when exceptions occur. |
|---|---|

**Intelligent O&M**

You can use the intelligent O&M features to manage the hosts, hard disks, and logs of clusters in an intelligent manner. The following table describes the features.

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| Perform host O&M | You can use the host O&M feature to initiate intelligent O&M workflows for clusters based on O&M scenarios. You can use workflows to track the scaling progress of clusters. This effectively simplifies O&M operations and improves O&M efficiency. If you need to increase the number of physical hosts in a cluster to properly allocate computing and storage resources, you can initiate a CDS Cluster Scale Up workflow. If you need to decrease the number of physical hosts in a cluster to properly allocate computing and storage resources, you can initiate a CDS Cluster Scale Down workflow. If a physical host in a cluster fails and needs to be repaired, you cani nitiate a CDS Cluster Node Maintenance workflow. If you need to improve the availability and fault tolerance of a newly deployed CDS-OSS cluster, you can initiate a CDS Cluster Three-zone Scale Up workflow to scale up the single-data-center cluster to a three-data-center cluster. To scale a lite cluster that contains four or five nodes to a standard cluster that contains six or more nodes, you need to initiate a CDS Cluster Deployment Mode Switch workflow after you add nodes. For more information, see Initiate a CDS Cluster Deployment Mode Switch workflow. After you initiate O&M workflows for clusters, you can view all workflows to check the O&M progress and manage workflows as needed. |
| Maintain hard disks | You can maintain hard disks based on O&M scenarios. If an HDD or Non-Volatile Memory Express (NVMe) SSD disk of a chunk server is corrupted, you can initiate disk hot maintenance after the data of the corrupted disk is backed up. If a healthy hard disk needs to be replaced due to capacity upgrade, performance improvement, or regular maintenance, you can actively replace the disk. After disk hot maintenance is complete, you can view the maintenance history of hard disks. |
| Manage logs | After you identify abnormal services or modules based on an issue, you can manually collect logs to quickly identify and handle the issue. The system stores and indexes the logs of key services in a centralized manner. You can query logs within a specific time range by service type, project, and storage service. |

erations

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|

| View tasks | The system runs time-consuming tasks in an asynchronous manner. You can view the status of asynchronous tasks on the Tasks page. |
| Query audit logs | Audit logs record the modifications that are made by users to the system. During security maintenance, you can filter the audit logs by using different keywords to quickly identify and handle security issues and ensure system security. |
| Perform system cleanup | Task logs are stored on system disks. By default, the feature of automatically triggering compression tasks and deletion tasks is disabled. To prevent system disks from being fully occupied by service logs, you can clear logs by using one of the following methods: Automatically clear logs: You can manage cleanup configurations to manually enable the auto trigger feature. You can also modify auto trigger thresholds and delete cleanup configurations based on your business requirements. After you enable the auto trigger feature, the system automatically compresses or deletes service logs when the storage space reaches the specified threshold. Manually clear logs: You can run cleanup tasks to manually compress or delete logs. |

##### 5.1.1.3 Permission configuration

###### 5.1.1.3.1 Manage permissions on CDS-OPS

erations By default, a system administrator has the permissions to use all features of Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS. To meet the access control requirements for different users, the system supports the following roles for CDS-OPS: CDS administrator, CDS support, and CDS developer. These roles are granted different permissions on CDS-OPS.

**Roles for CDS-OPS**

A role is a collection of access permissions. You can assign different roles to different users to meet your requirements for system access control. The following table describes the permissions of the three roles for CDS-OPS.

| Role |   | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| CDS administrator |   | Has the permissions to perform most read operations and the permissions to perform a few modify operations. In most cases, the CDS administrator role is assigned to O&M staff to monitor the status of CDS. |
| CDS support |   | Has all the permissions of the CDS administrator role and the permissions to perform some regular read and write operations. |
| CDS developer |   | Has all the permissions of the CDS support role and the permissions to perform some high-risk O&M operations. Exercise caution when you assign this role to a user. |

**Add a user**

You can add a user and assign a role for CDS-OPS to the user to control the permissions of the user on CDS-OPS.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **More > User Authorities**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **User Management**.
4. On the **Users** tab of the **Users** page, click **Add**.
5. In the **Add User** dialog box, configure the user information and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Username | The name of the user. The name can be up to 48 characters in length, and can contain digits, letters, underscores ( ), hyphens (-), and periods (.). The _ email format is supported. Consecutive underscores are not supported. |
| Password | The password of the user. The password must be 10 to 20 characters in length, and must contain lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, and special characters. |
| Confirm Password | The same password that you enter to confirm the password. |

erations

| Display name | The display name of the user. |
|---|---|
| Logon Policy | The logon policy of the user. |
| Role | The role of the user, such as product DevOps administrator. |
| Department | The department to which the user belongs. |
| Mobile Phone | The mobile number of the user. |
| Email Address | The email address of the user. |
| Allowed to Create AccessKey ID | Specifies whether to allow the user to create AccessKey pairs. By default, users are not allowed to create AccessKey pairs. |

##### 5.1.1.5 Storage management

###### 5.1.1.5.1 Before you begin

You can view, monitor, configure, manage, or maintain the clusters of various storage services. The features supported by a cluster vary based on the cluster type. The actual features that are available prevail.

**Supported cluster types**

The following table describes the types of clusters that you can manage in Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS.

> **Note:** Various services may be deployed in a cluster. In this case, the cluster belongs to multiple cluster types.

| Cluster type | Description |
|---|---|

erations

| OSS cluster | Object Storage Service (OSS) is a secure, cost-effective, and highly reliable cloud storage service of Apsara Stack. OSS allows you to store and obtain various unstructured data objects, such as text, images, audio, and videos, over networks at any time. You can use CDS-OPS to manage CDS-OSS clusters and OSS clusters. CDS- OPS provides the same features for CDS-OSS clusters and managed OSS clusters. You can manage OSS clusters and PANGU clusters under the CDS- OSS module. For more information, see Overview of OSS clusters. For CDS-OSS clusters, the base of PANGU clusters is PANGU V2.0. You can use CDS-OPS to manage PANGU V2.0 clusters. For managed OSS clusters, the base of PANGU clusters is PANGU V1.0. You cannot use CDS-OPS to manage PANGU V1.0 clusters. |
|---|---|
| SLS cluster | Simple Log Service (SLS) is an all-in-one log data management service. You can use SLS to collect, consume, query, and analyze log data without the need to invest in in-house data collection or processing systems. SLS allows you to process large amounts of data to improve the O&M efficiency. You can use CDS-OPS to manage CDS-SLS clusters. You can manage SLS clusters and PANGU clusters under the CDS-Log Storage module. For more information, see Overview of SLS clusters. |
| EBS cluster | Elastic Block Storage (EBS) provides the elastic block storage service in the distributed storage architecture and the on-premises disks of physical machines. You can use CDS-OPS to manage CDS-EBS clusters and EBS-1.0 or EBS-2.0 clusters. CDS-OPS provides the same features for CDS-EBS clusters and managed EBS-2.0 clusters. For managed EBS-1.0 clusters, you can view and perform basic O&M operations on the clusters in CDS-OPS. You can manage EBS clusters and PANGU clusters under the CDS-Elastic Block Storage module. For more information, see Overview of CDS-EBS and EBS-2.0 clusters and Overview of EBS-1.0 clusters. |

**Usage notes**

OSS and EBS can be deployed together only in CDS clusters. You cannot use CDS-OPS to manage the PANGU clusters of managed OSS clusters. Exercise caution when you perform high-risk operations, such as modifying cluster configurations, restarting servers, restarting services, and deleting files. If you need to perform the preceding high-risk operations, contact Apsara Stack technical support.

###### 5.1.1.5.2.2 Manage cluster details

View cluster overview On the Overview tab of an Elastic Block Storage (EBS) cluster, you can view the physical capacity usage, number of disks, number of snapshots, and inspection items of the cluster. This way, you can understand the overall information about the cluster and promptly handle exceptions.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. erations ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-EBS > Cluster O&M**.
3. In the **Clusters** section of the **Cluster O&M** page, click the cluster name.

> **Note:** You can also select a cluster from the drop-down list in the upper-right corner of the Cluster O&M page.

4. On the **Overview** tab, view the overall information about the cluster.

**Cluster overview**

You can view the physical capacity usage, number and status of BlockMaster nodes, number and status of BlockServer nodes, number of disks, and number of snapshots. The following table describes the metrics.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| Physical Capacity Usage | The physical capacity usage of the cluster, including the percentage of used physical capacity, used physical capacity, and total physical capacity. Total Physical Capacity: the total physical capacity of the EBS cluster that is allocated by the PANGU layer. Used Physical Capacity: the physical capacity that is used by the EBS layer, including the capacity occupied by internal data and user data. |
| Master Server BlockMaster | The total number of BlockMaster nodes, the number of normal BlockMaster nodes, and the number of abnormal BlockMaster nodes. |
| Storage Server BlockServer | The total number of BlockServer nodes, the number of normal BlockServer nodes, and the number of abnormal BlockServer nodes. |
| Cloud Disks | The total number of disks in the cluster. |
| Snapshots | The total number of snapshots that are created for disks in the cluster. |

**Inspection items**

You can view the name, statistics, last execution time, and remarks of each inspection item. You can click the number in the **Statistics** column of an inspection item to view details of the last execution on the **Inspection Results** page. You can also click the time in the
**Last Executed At** column to view the time of the last execution on the **Inspection**
**History** page.

**Monitoring data**

You can specify a time range or click a time range to view the monitoring data within the specified time range, including the cloud disk and snapshot trend chart, cluster read/write latency, total cluster IOPS, and total cluster throughput of the EBS cluster. erations The following table describes the metrics.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| Cloud Disk and Snapshot Trend Chart | The usage of disks and snapshots in the cluster. You can query the disk and snapshot usage of the cluster only by day. The monitoring data is generated on a daily basis. You can view the following monitoring data in the trend chart: Disks: the total number of disks. Snapshots: the total number of snapshots. |
| Read/Write Latency for Cluster | The average read/write latency of the cluster. You can view the following monitoring data in the trend chart: Read Latency: the average read latency. Write Latency: the average write latency. |
| Total Cluster IOPS | The total numbers of read/write operations per second in the cluster. You can view the following monitoring data in the trend chart: Read IOPS: the total number of read operations per second in the cluster. Write IOPS: the total number of write operations per second in the cluster. |
| Total Cluster Throughput | The total throughput of data reads and writes in the cluster. You can view the following monitoring data in the trend chart: Read: the total throughput of data reads in the cluster. Write: the total throughput of data writes in the cluster. |

You can click the name of a metric to show or hide the monitoring data in a chart. For example, you can click Disks in the disk and snapshot trend chart to show only the relevant monitoring data. Move the pointer over a trend chart to view the value at a specific point in time. In the **Actions** column of each metric, you can select **Download Data** to download the monitoring data to your computer, or select **Save as Image** to save the monitoring data as an image. You can perform operations such as cluster scale-up or scale-down based on the predicted capacity usage. This prevents cluster failures that may be caused by exhausted storage capacity and ensures the security and stability of the cluster. Note The predicted capacity usage is for reference only. Perform operations based on the actual capacity usage. Capacity prediction depends on the accumulation of sufficient samples. If the capacity data in a cluster is insufficient, the system cannot predict the capacity usage. No prediction data is available for a newly deployed cluster. Configure clusters erations Configure the EC mode By default, clusters use erasure coding (EC) to ensure the reliability and consistency of user data. EC helps improve storage reliability. Compared with triplicate storage, EC can provide higher data reliability at lower data redundancy levels.

**Usage notes**

After you modify the EC configurations for a cluster, the configurations take effect on both existing and new disks. You cannot modify EC configurations when O&M operations are being performed on hosts in the cluster. Wait until the O&M operations are complete and try again. After the EC mode is enabled for a cluster, you cannot disable this mode for the cluster. This means that you cannot switch to the triplicate storage mode. Proceed with caution. You can modify the current EC configurations only by switching to a lower level of data redundancy. The system automatically calculates EC configurations with a lower level of data redundancy.

**Specify an EC type for a cluster**

1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-EBS > Cluster O&M**.
3. In the **Clusters** section of the **Cluster O&M** page, click the cluster name.

> **Note:** You can also select a cluster from the drop-down list in the upper-right corner of the Cluster O&M page.

4. On the **Configuration** tab, click **EC Configurations**.
5. In the EC Configuration section of the **EC Configurations** tab, modify the **Configuration**
**Type** parameter to specify an EC type based on your business requirements.
The EC types supported by the cluster are displayed in the drop-down list. After you select a configuration type, the value of the Replicas parameter is displayed, which is calculated based on the selected configuration type.

> **Note:** Some clusters do not support the Configuration Type parameter. The actual page prevails.

6. Click **Save**.

**View the distribution of EC configurations for the disks in a**

**cluster**

The EC configurations of disks in a cluster are the same as the EC configurations of the cluster. In the **EC Configuration Distribution For Cloud Disks In A Cluster** section of the
**EC Configurations** tab, view the distribution of EC configurations for the disks in the cluster.
After you modify the EC configurations of the cluster, the existing disks are automatically switched to the new EC mode. In the EC Configuration Distribution For Cloud Disks In A Cluster section, check whether all existing disks have switched to the new EC mode. erations

**View the number of folded chunks**

Typically, the number of folded chunks in a cluster is 0. If the number of available servers drops below N + M because some servers are faulty or enter the sub-healthy state, partial chunks in the cluster are folded. You can view the number of folded chunks within a specific time period to measure the volume of folded data.

> **Important:** Only lite clusters support data folding.

Data may be folded in a cluster due to server-related errors. We recommend that you check and handle related alerts at the earliest opportunity. For more information, see Handle current alerts.
1. On the **Configuration** tab, click **EC Configurations**.
2. In the **Number Of Folded Chunks** section of the **EC Configurations** tab, select a time

If data is unevenly distributed because BlockServer nodes are added or stopped, the corresponding cluster automatically balances the number of segments on BlockServer nodes. This way, the resources of the cluster can be properly used.

**Background information**

O&M engineers can determine whether the segments are evenly distributed by checking the average number of segments on each BlockServer node and the variance in the number of segments on all BlockServer nodes.

Configure replica traffic control You can configure the maximum and minimum replication speeds as required to control data replica traffic. If you need to quickly replicate data, you can increase the maximum and minimum replication speeds. If you do not want the replication to consume a large amount of resources, you can reduce the maximum and minimum replication speeds.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-EBS > Cluster O&M**.
