###### 5.1.1.9.1.5 Initiate a CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow

**Availability Zones Scale Up workflow**

You can initiate a Cloud Defined Storage (CDS) Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow only for a cluster that uses the CDS_OSS_ZRS storage architecture. After a cluster that uses the CDS_OSS_ZRS storage architecture is deployed in the first data center and reaches the desired state, the cluster works in single-data center mode. You must initiate a
**CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up** workflow to add the machines in the
second and third data centers to the cluster and switch the working mode of the cluster to three-data center mode. This implements high availability and fault tolerance across data centers.

**Background information**

A three-zone cluster distributes the system across three different zones. This ensures that, even if one zone becomes unavailable due to network disconnection, power outage, or a disaster, the other two zones can continue to provide services, thereby ensuring business continuity and data security. When a single zone fails, CDS can still provide strongly consistent services. This way, the failover process is transparent to users, with no data loss. This also implements a recovery point objective (RPO) of zero and a recovery time objective (RTO) approaching zero for key business systems.

**Usage notes**

You can initiate a CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow only for a newly deployed cluster that uses the CDS_OSS_ZRS storage architecture. After you deploy a CDS- OSS cluster across three data centers, you must scale up the cluster from a single-zone cluster to a three-zone cluster by initiating a CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow. Do not initiate a CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow for any OSS cluster or CDS-OSS cluster that is executing tasks. erations When you scale up a CDS-OSS cluster to a three-zone cluster, you must select two data centers and the hosts in them. In addition, the number of selected hosts in a single data center must be equal to the number of hosts in the cluster that you want to scale up. Otherwise, the scale-up fails.

**Prerequisites**

The cluster that you want to scale up is deployed in the first data center and has reached the desired state. The cluster does not contain machines in the second and third data centers, and the cluster contains at least seven hosts.

> **Important:** If the number of hosts in the cluster does not meet the requirements for a three-zone scale-up, initiate a cluster scale-up workflow to increase the number of hosts before you proceed. For more information, see Initiate a CDS Cluster Scale Up workflow.

You can perform the following steps to check the number of hosts in the cluster: i. Log in to the CDS-OPS console. ii. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-OSS > Cluster O&M**. iii. In the **Clusters** section of the **Cluster O&M** page, find the cluster that you want to scale up and click its name to go to the Cluster Details page. iv. Click the Host tab. On the **Host** tab, view the information about hosts and check the number of hosts. The available hosts in the clusters of the buffer project reside across two data centers, the number of available hosts in a single data center is equal to the number of hosts in the cluster that you want to scale up, and the models of the available hosts are the same as those in the cluster that you want to scale up. You can perform the following steps to check whether hosts are available in the clusters. i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**
**Management > Resource Management**.
iii. On the **Product & Cluster O&M** page, enter **buffer** in the **Product | Cluster** field. iv. Find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column. On the Cluster Details page, click the **Machines** tab. A list of available hosts in the buffer cluster is displayed. Make sure that the yunchi service of the cluster is running as expected. If the service is not deployed or is in an abnormal state, contact Apsara Stack technical support. You can perform the following steps to view the status of the yunchi service in the cluster. i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**
**Management > Resource Management**.
iii. On the **Product & Cluster O&M** page, enter **cds** in the **Product | Cluster** field. iv. Find the cds-cdsmanagementcluster cluster and click **Cluster Details** in the **Actions** column. v. On the **Services** tab, find a service and click its name. In this example, the cds-0 service is used. vi. On the service details page, view the status of the yunchi component and yunchi servers. erations If the yunchi component is in the **Ready** state and the yunchi servers are in the **Running** state on the **Workload** tab, the yunchi service is running as expected.
1. Log in to the CDS-OPS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Intelligent O&M > Host O&M**.
3. On the Host O&M page, click the **Initiate Workflow** tab. On the Initiate Workflow tab, find
the CDS Cluster Three Availability Zones Scale Up workflow and click **Initiate** in the

4. In the **Initiating Workflow [Three Availability Zones Scale Up]** panel, select the

> **Important:** Make sure that the number of hosts selected for the destination data centers is equal to the number of hosts in the destination cluster.

When you select scalable hosts, **Same Machine Model** is enabled by default to filter hosts. Only the hosts of the same model as the hosts in the selected cluster are displayed. We recommend that you select such hosts to ensure the overall performance and stability of the cluster.

###### 5.1.1.9.1.6 Initiate a CDS Cluster Deployment Mode Switch workflow

**Mode Switch workflow**

To scale a lite cluster to a standard cluster that contains six or more nodes, you need to initiate a CDS Cluster Deployment Mode Switch workflow after you add nodes. This operation switches the deployment mode of the cluster to CdsEbsSsd to use the extended cluster capabilities.

**Background information**

In most cases, the smallest Elastic Block Storage (EBS) cluster contains six nodes. To meet requirements for small-scale cluster deployment, EBS provides lite clusters that use all-flash storage media. A lite cluster contains only four or five nodes.

A lite cluster is scaled up. For more information, see Initiate a CDS Cluster Scale Up workflow. The number of hosts is greater than or equal to 6.

3. Click the **Initiate Workflow** tab. In the Actions column of the **CDS Cluster Deployment**
**Mode Switch** workflow, click **Initiate**.
4. In the **Initiating The Workflow [Deployment Mode Switch]** pane, select the
destination cluster and deployment mode.

| Parameter | Description |

###### 5.1.1.9.2 Maintain disks

###### 5.1.1.9.2.1 Maintain corrupted disks

When a hard disk drive (HDD) or Non-Volatile Memory Express (NVMe) SSD disk of a chunk server is corrupted, you can view the information about the corrupted disk in real time and initiate a disk replacement process and disk hot maintenance after the data of the corrupted disk is backed up. After the disk hot maintenance is complete, you can view the maintenance record in the maintenance history.

> **Note:** Tablestore clusters, Cloud Parallel File Storage (CPFS) clusters, Elastic Block Storage (EBS)-1.0 clusters, and Object Storage Service (OSS)-1.0 clusters do not support the disk maintenance feature.

**Usage notes**

To ensure data security, you cannot initiate multiple disk replacement processes in the same cluster at a time. The disk replacement process and host O&M workflow cannot be performed at the same time. Disks can be mounted in EXT4 or USSOS mode. The replacement operations vary based on the mounting methods. The following high-risk operations exist during the hot disk maintenance process. If the process is not complete as expected, contact Apsara Stack technical support for assistance. Detach the damaged disk: The disk is removed from the file system, and data cannot be read from or written to the disk. Replace the damaged disk: The drive letters may change. Initialize the new disk: Partitions are formatted, and data on the disk is completely deleted and cannot be restored.

**Replace a data disk mounted in EXT4 mode**

1. Log in to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS Operation**
**CDS-OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Intelligent O&M > Disk Maintenance**.
3. On the Disk Maintenance page, click the Corrupted Disks tab. On the **Corrupted Disks** tab,
view and maintain corrupted disks. erations You can view information about the corrupted disks in the following columns: Cluster, Chunk Server, Disk ID, Disk Type, Device Name, Status, Backup Status, and Process Status. When a disk is corrupted, the cluster automatically backs up the data of the disk. If the value of the **Backup Status** column of the disk is **Backup Completed**, the data of the disk is backed up.

> **Warning:** To prevent data loss, make sure that the data stored on a corrupted disk is backed up before you replace the disk.

i. Optional. Assist on-site maintenance personnel in locating the disk by turning on and off the disk light. a. Click **Replace Disk** in the **Actions** column of the corrupted disk.

> **Note:** You can also click **Locate Disk** in the **Actions** column of the corrupted disk.

b. In the **Locate Disk** dialog box, click **On** next to **Disk Light Status**. After the disk light is turned on, you can click **Off** to turn off the light.

> **Note:** If the light fails to be turned on or the device does not support lighting, manually locate the corrupted disk. For more information about how to manually locate a disk, see Locate the physical location of a corrupted disk.

c. After you locate the disk, select the **I have confirmed the location of the damaged**
**disk and understand the risk of disk replacement** check box and click **Initiate**
**Process**.
ii. The system automatically performs a pre-check and unmounts the corrupted disk. iii. Manually replace the disk: Locate the corrupted disk based on the corrupted disk location and replace the disk. Then, click **Execute New Disk Identification**.

> **Note:** If the new disk is not recognized, the system returns a warning message. The warning message does not interrupt subsequent steps.

If the disk is in a RAID architecture, the system obtains the location of the disk. You can locate the corrupted disk by turning on and off the disk light. If the disk does not have a RAID controller, you can locate the disk based on the corrupted disk locating process. You can verify whether the disk is correctly replaced by using the serial number. iv. Manually initialize the new disk: Make sure that the device name of the new disk is correct, and click **Execute Initialize**. By default, the system uses the drive letter adopted by the disk. A drive letter is automatically assigned even if no new disk is recognized. If the drive letter cannot be retrieved before the disk replacement is initiated, you need to manually enter and confirm a drive letter. erations v. The system automatically mounts the new disk, publishes the new disk, and verifies the result of the disk replacement. After the disk replacement is complete, you can view the maintenance history of the disk on the **Disk Maintenance History** tab.

**Replace a data disk mounted in USSOS mode**

1. Log in to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS Operation**
**CDS OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Intelligent O&M > Disk Maintenance**.
3. On the Disk Maintenance page, click the Corrupted Disks tab. On the **Corrupted Disks** tab,
view and maintain corrupted disks. You can view information about the corrupted disks in the following columns: Chunk Server, Chunk Server IP Address, Disk ID, Disk Type, Status, Backup Status, and Process Status. When a disk is corrupted, the cluster automatically backs up the data of the disk. If the value of the **Backup Status** column of the disk is **Backup Completed**, the data of the disk is backed up.

> **Warning:** To prevent data loss, make sure that the data stored on a corrupted disk is backed up before you replace the disk.

i. Initiate a disk replacement process. a. Click **Replace Disk** in the **Actions** column of the corrupted disk. b. In the **Initiating [Disk Replacement] procedure** dialog box, select the **I have**

**confirmed the location of the damaged disk and understand the risk of disk**

**replacement** check box and click **Initiate Process**.

> **Note:** Disks mounted in USSOS mode cannot be located by turning on the disk light. Locate the disk to be replaced based on the disk location or the disk light status.

c. ii. The system automatically performs an environment check, performs a backup check, and unmounts the corrupted disk. iii. Manually replace the disk: Locate the corrupted disk based on the corrupted disk location or the disk light status, replace the disk, and click **Execute Verify**.

> **Important:** Make sure that the corrupted disk information matches the information about the disk whose disk light is off.

If the disk is in a RAID architecture, the system obtains the location of the disk. You can locate the corrupted disk by turning on and off the disk light. If the disk does not have a RAID controller, you can locate the disk based on the corrupted disk locating process. You can verify whether the disk is correctly replaced by using the serial number. erations iv. The system automatically switches the new disk to the user mode, initializes the new disk, publishes the new disk, and verifies the result of the disk replacement. After the disk replacement is complete, you can view the maintenance history of the disk on the **Disk Maintenance History** tab.

**Related operations**

On the **Corrupted Disks** tab, you can perform more operations based on your business requirements.

| View the details of a disk status change task | When you manually replace a disk, you must change the status of the disk that is working normally to Error. To view the details of a disk status change task, clickD isk Status Change Task Details. On the Tasks page, view the details. |

**What to do next**

After the disk replacement is complete, you can view the maintenance history of the disk on the **Disk Maintenance History** tab. For more information, see View disk maintenance history.

If a hard disk to be replaced is in the Normal state, the system changes its state to **Error** before disk replacement. Do not manually restart the ChunkServer service during disk replacement. You can replace only one hard disk at a time in a cluster.

4. Submit an active disk replacement request.
erations i. On the **Actively Replace Disk** tab, select a cluster name, a chunk server, and a hard disk. The system automatically changes the state of the hard disk.
5. Identify the hard disk to be replaced and initiate the process.
i. In the **Locate Disk** dialog box, identify the hard disk to be replaced based on the indicator light and select **I have confirmed the location of the damaged disk** . ii. Click **Create Process**.

###### 5.1.1.9.3 Log Management

###### 5.1.1.9.3.1 Collect log data

erations After you identify abnormal services or modules based on an issue, you can manually collect their run logs to quickly identify and handle the issue.

**Usage notes**

> **Warning:** The operations on user logs must be authorized by a user, such as collecting or exporting log data. You must follow the principle of least privilege and collect only the logs of the services that are related to the issue to be handled.

Logs are asynchronously collected with a specific latency. You can view the progress of a log collection task on the Tasks page. For more information, see View tasks. Newly collected logs overwrite previously collected logs.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Intelligent O&M > Log Collection**.
3. On the **Log Collection** page, click **Data Collection**.
4. In the **Data Collection** dialog box, configure the Type, Service Name, Cluster Name, Host
Name, and Time Range parameters, and click **Initiate Collection**. The **Service Name** parameter is displayed only if you set the **Type** parameter to
**Service Logs**. You can select multiple values for the Type, Service Name, and Host
Name parameters. After the log collection task is complete, you can view the logs that are generated in the specified time range. To save the logs to your computer, you can find the log collection record and click
**Download** in the **Result File** column. A message indicating that the certificate is not
secure may appear. Click Trust to download the logs. The downloaded log file is in the tar.gz format. Decompress the file and view the logs.

###### 5.1.1.9.3.2 Query logs

The system centrally stores and indexes logs of key services. You can query logs within a time range by service type, project, and storage service.

**Background information**

Logs are not permanently stored. The system automatically clears logs on a regular basis. The log retention period varies based on service. The log retention period is determined by the size and the importance of logs, but cannot exceed 30 days.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS) O&M platform console.

###### 5.1.1.10.4 System Cleanup

###### 5.1.1.10.4.1 Manage cleanup configurations

By default, the feature of automatically triggering compression tasks and cleanup tasks is disabled. You can manually enable the feature based on your business requirements. After you enable the auto trigger feature, the system automatically compresses service logs or clears tasks when the storage space reaches the specified threshold. You can also modify the automatic cleanup configurations such as enabling or disabling the auto trigger feature, modifying the thresholds, or deleting log cleanup configurations.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. erations ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-System Management > System Cleanup**.
3. On the **System Cleanup** page, click **Automatic Cleaning Configuration** in the upper-
right corner.
4. On the **Clean up Configurations** page, view the quota and auto trigger threshold of each
service, and perform operations as required. Enable or disable the auto trigger feature By default, the auto trigger feature is disabled. You can turn on the switch in the
**Auto Trigger** column to enable the auto trigger feature.
After you enable the auto trigger feature, you can turn off the switch in the **Auto**
**Trigger** column to disable the auto trigger feature.
Modify service quotas and auto trigger thresholds Find the service that you want to manage and click **Modify** in the **Actions** column. In the dialog box that appears, configure the parameters and click **OK**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Service Quota | The maximum storage space that the service can use. |
| Safe Usage Level | The safe storage usage for the service logs. If the auto trigger feature is enabled and the storage space occupied by logs is lower than the safe storage usage, the service logs are not compressed or cleaned up. |
| Usage Level for Compression | The log compression threshold. If the auto trigger feature is enabled and the storage space occupied by service logs exceeds the log compression threshold but is lower than the log cleanup threshold, the system compresses the services logs until the storage space occupied by service logs drops below the specified usage level for compression. The logs are compressed in chronological order from the earliest data to the latest data. You need to manually compress the logs generated before a specific date. For more information, see Clear tasks. |
| Usage Level for Cleanup | The log cleanup threshold. If the auto trigger feature is enabled and the storage space occupied by logs exceeds the log cleanup threshold, the system clears the logs until the storage space occupied by logs drops below the log cleanup threshold. The logs are cleared in chronological order from the earliest data to the latest data. You need to manually clear the logs generated before a specified date. For more information, see Clear tasks. |
| Auto Trigger | Specifies whether to enable the auto trigger feature. By default, this feature is disabled. After the auto trigger feature is enabled, the system automatically executes log compression and cleanup tasks based on the thresholds that you specify. |

erations Delete the log cleanup configurations

> **Important:** You can delete the log cleanup configurations of a service only after the service is stopped.

Find the service that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. In the
**Confirm Deletion** message, click **OK**.
If the log cleanup configurations of a service are deleted but the service is still running, the log cleanup configurations are displayed again when the service generates logs. If the service is stopped and does not generate logs, the log cleanup configurations are no longer displayed.

Task logs are stored on system disks. You can compress or delete the logs based on your requirements to save storage on the system disks and improve the stability of system services.

**Usage notes**

Logs are asynchronously compressed or deleted with a specific latency. You can view the progress of a log compression or deletion task on the Tasks page. For more information, see View tasks.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.

service, or a component to query logs. You can view the information about the logs, such as the size, space usage, and compression status.
4. Find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Clear** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Clear Logs** dialog box, adjust the slider to select a date. The system checks the logs
that are generated before the selected date, and calculates the number of files that can be compressed and deleted, and the space that can be released. To compress the logs, click **Start Compression**. In the message that appears, click
**Confirm** to start the compression task.
To delete the logs, click **Start Cleanup**. In the message that appears, click **Confirm** to start the deletion task.

###### 5.1.1.11.2 Use HDR-OPS

###### 5.1.1.11.2.1 Before you begin

Hybrid Disaster Recovery (HDR)-OPS is a centralized O&M management tool for HDR. Before you use HDR-OPS, read the following information to understand the features and concepts of HDR.

**Background information**

HDR is a service that provides cloud-based disaster recovery for enterprise-level applications in data centers. HDR provides disaster recovery services with a recovery point objective (RPO) of a few minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of a few minutes for enterpriselevel applications that are deployed on Alibaba Cloud. HDR can effectively ensure data security and business continuity. HDR provides cross-cloud and cross-zone disaster recovery capabilities based on the async replication feature to meet various business requirements. If a fault occurs on the primary system, your business is switched to the disaster recovery system. This effectively prevents system failures caused by regional disasters, ensures business availability, and meets the RPO and RTO goals of your business. erations

**Features**

| Feature | Description | References |
|---|---|---|
| View site information | HDR-OPS automatically obtains the disaster recovery site pairs created in the HDR console. You can view the site pairs that you create and the details about the site pairs in the site pair list. The details include the information about protection groups, infrastructure, and historical tasks. | View site pair information |
| View alert information | The alerts that are managed by HDR-OPS are triggered by the resources of HDR. When an alert is triggered, you can view the current alert information in the alert list. The alerts that are triggered by time series data are displayed in the alert history after they are automatically cleared. Event-triggered alerts are displayed in the alert history after they are manually handled. You can query historical alerts in a specified time range. | View alert information |
| View inspection tasks | Inspection tasks are created to check the virtual private cloud (VPC) availability, network availability, security group availability, and security group policy consistency of site pairs. In the inspection task list, you can view the overall information about historical inspection tasks and view the details of an inspection task. The system periodically runs inspection tasks. The system generates alerts if the system detects changes in computing, network, and storage information at the production site and the disaster recovery site. | View inspection tasks |
| Manage O&M tasks | If operations cannot be performed on a protection group at the production site or the disaster recovery site due to data loss or corruption, you can use the Clear Protection Group feature to forcibly delete the protection group. If you want to perform an operation such as clearing a protection group, a corresponding O&M task is created and displayed in the O&M center. To prevent accidental operations, the system runs an O&M task only after the O&M task is confirmed by an O&M engineer. After a task is executed, the task execution status is displayed. | Manage O&M tasks |
| Configure O&M settings | You can adjust the inspection interval and cross- cloud configuration switch status. You can view O&M configurations, modify common configuration items, and add or delete configuration items. | Manage O&M configurations |

###### 5.1.1.11.2.3 View alert information

The alerts that are managed by Hybrid Disaster Recovery (HDR)-OPS are triggered by the resources of HDR. When an alert is triggered, you can view the current alert information in the alert list. The alerts that are triggered by time series data are displayed in the alert history after they are automatically cleared. Event-triggered alerts are displayed in the alert history after they are manually handled. You can query historical alerts in a specified time range.

**Background information**

System alerts can be triggered by time series data and events. Alerts triggered by time series data: Alerts are triggered based on metric thresholds. Alerts are cleared when the related metrics no longer meet the trigger conditions. The system continuously monitors metrics of site pairs, such as the recovery point objective (RPO). If a metric exceeds the specified threshold, the system generates an alert. Event-triggered alerts: Alerts are triggered based on events. In most cases, you must manually handle event-triggered alerts because event-triggered alerts cannot be automatically cleared. The system automatically checks the virtual private cloud (VPC) availability, network availability, security group availability, and security group policy consistency of site pairs. The system generates alerts if the system detects changes in computing, network, and storage information at the production site and the disaster recovery site.
1. Log on to the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Product Operation > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Data Service > HDR OPS**.
3. On the **Alert List** tab, view the current alerts or historical alerts.

**View current alerts**

On the **Current alert** page, set the alert type, Alibaba Cloud account ID, and fault instance ID. The system displays the information about the current alerts that meet the specified conditions, such as the alert level, trigger reason, and occurrence time.

> **Note:** After you receive a system alert, handle the alert based on the description of the trigger reason in a timely manner.

erations On the **Alarm history** page, set the time type and time range, fault instance ID, Alibaba Cloud account ID, and alert type. The system displays the information about the historical alerts that meet the specified conditions, such as the alert level, trigger reason, occurrence time, and recovery time.

###### 5.1.1.11.2.7 Manage cloud sites

By default, the system displays the Hybrid Disaster Recovery (HDR) information of the current cloud. Before you establish a disaster recovery relationships between two clouds, you need to configure the HDR information for the clouds, and add the HDR information of the destination cloud to the cloud site list of the current cloud, and then view and manage the HDR information.

**Background information**

Cross-cloud disaster recovery indicates disaster recovery for Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances between the production site and the disaster recovery site that are deployed on different clouds. The production site and disaster recovery site are deployed on two clouds. After the cloud organization mapping is configured and a protection group is created, a channel is established between the production site and the disaster recovery site. The channel is used to replicate data from the production site to the disaster recovery site in real time. If the production site fails, services at the production site are failed over to the ECS instances at the disaster recovery site. After the production site is recovered, the services are failed back to the ECS instances at the production site. This ensures business continuity. Procedure:
1. Configure the cloud sites on the HDR OPS page of the Cloud Defined Storage (CDS)-OPS
console.
2. Create cloud configurations in the HDR console and create a mapping for the clouds of the
production site and the disaster recovery site.
3. Perform disaster recovery in the HDR console.

**Prerequisites**

The following services are accessible across clouds and the network configurations are correct: Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console: CDS-Elastic Block Storage (EBS) in CDS-OPS Apsara Uni-manager Management Console: HDR, EBS, ECS, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), and Apsara Name Service and Distributed Lock Synchronization System The HDR API address, AccessKey pair (including the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret) of the HDR user, the AccessKey pair for Ops O&M, and cloud regions of the current region and the destination region are obtained.

**Important**

erations To ensure security, create an account for an HDR user in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and an account for an O&M engineer in the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. Then, create an AccessKey pair for each account. The cross-cloud configuration switch is enabled for the cloud sites. (The value of multiCloudDrConfig is set to true.) For more information, see Manage O&M configurations.
1. Log on to the CDS-OPS console.
i. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console. ii. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products > Storage > CDS - OPS**.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **CDS-Data Service > HDR OPS**.
3. Click the **List of Cloud Sites** tab. On the List of Cloud Sites tab, edit cloud sites.
Before you establish a disaster recovery relationship between clouds, you must configure HDR information on the cloud where the production site is located and the cloud where the disaster recovery site is located, such as the cloud name, HDR API address, AccessKey pair of the HDR user, and AccessKey pair for Ops O&M. i. Find the desired could site and click **Edit** in the **Operation** column. ii. In the **Edit a cloud site** dialog box, modify the cloud site information.

> **Note:** To ensure security, the AccessKey pairs are not displayed when you modify a cloud site. To change an AccessKey pair, you must enter the complete AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret.

iii. Click **OK**. If **Link status** of the cloud site is **Connected**, the configuration is correct.
4. Add a cloud site.
After the HDR information of the current cloud and the destination cloud is configured, you need to add the HDR information of the other side to the current cloud or the destination cloud. i. Click **Create a cloud site**. ii. In the **Create a cloud site** dialog box, configure the following parameters: Cloud ID, Cloud name, HDR API address, HDR User AccessKey ID, HDR User AccessKey Secret, Ops O & M AccessKey ID, Ops O & M AccessKey Secret, Cloud Region list, and Http proxy. iii. Click **OK**. If **Link Status** of the new cloud site is *************, the configuration is correct. If cross-cloud disaster recovery is no longer required, you can delete the HDR configuration of other clouds. Click **Delete** in the ************* column of the cloud site.

**What to do next**

Add a cross-cloud disaster recovery site pair in the HDR console. For more information, see "Cross-cloud Disaster Recovery" in "Disaster Recovery in the Cloud" under "HDR" of **CDS**
**User Guide**.
O&M

#### 6.1.1 Log on to the ApsaraDB Operations and Maintenance System

**Maintenance System**

This topic describes how to log on to the ApsaraDB Operations and Maintenance System.

**Prerequisites**

The URL of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console and the username and password used to log on to the console are obtained from a deployment engineer or an administrator. The URL of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console is in the format of ops.asconsole.intranet-domain-id.com. A web browser. We recommend that you use Google Chrome.
1. Open your browser.
2. In the address bar, enter the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
Press the Enter key. O&M

> **Note:** You can select a language from the drop-down list in the upper-right corner of the logon page.

3. Enter your username and password.

> **Note:** Obtain the username and password that are used to log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Operations Console from a deployment engineer or an administrator.

If you enter an invalid password for three consecutive times, the system enables the image verification logon feature. If you enter an invalid password for five consecutive times, the account is locked. Contact the administrator to unlock the account.

> The first time that you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console, change the password for your username as prompted.
> To enhance security, your password must meet the following requirements:
> The password contains uppercase and lowercase letters.
> The password contains digits.
> The password contains at least one of the following special characters: ! @ # $ %
> The password is 10 to 20 characters in length.

4. Click **Agree to Private Policy and Log On** .

**References**

The performance metrics of an instance vary with the engine, engine version, and storage types of the instance. The following table lists the common performance metrics of ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instances. For instances that run other engines or versions, the performance metrics displayed in the console shall prevail.

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| MySQL NetworkTraffic _ | The average volume of inbound traffic to the RDS instance per second and the average volume of outbound traffic from the RDS instance per second. Unit: KB/s. |
| MySQL QPSTPS _ | The average number of SQL statements executed per second and the average number of transactions executed per second. |

O&M

| MySQL Sessions _ | The number of active connections and the total number of connections. Unit: counts. |
|---|---|
| MySQL InnoDBBufferRatio _ | The read hit ratio, usage, and dirty ratio of the InnoDB buffer pool. Unit: %. |
| MySQL InnoDBDataReadWriten _ | The average volume of data that InnoDB reads per second and the average volume of data that InnoDB writes per second. Unit: KB. |
| MySQL InnoDBLogRequests _ | The average number of reads from the InnoDB buffer pool per second and the average number of writes to the InnoDB buffer pool per second. Unit: count/s. |
| MySQL InnoDBLogWrites _ | The average number of log write requests per second, the average number of physical writes to log files per second, and the average number of writes performed by calling the fsync() function to log files per second. Unit: count/s. |
| MySQL TempDiskTableCreates _ | The number of temporary tables that are automatically created on the hard disk during statement execution. Unit: tables. |
| MySQL MyISAMKeyBufferRatio _ | The average usage, read hit ratio, and write hit ratio of the MyISAM key buffer per second. Unit: %. |
| MySQL MyISAMKeyReadWrites _ | The average number of reads from the buffer pool by MyISAM per second, the average number of writes to the buffer pool by MyISAM per second, the average number of reads from the hard disk by MyISAM per second, and the average number of writes to the hard disk by MyISAM per second. Unit: count/s. |
| MySQL COMDML _ | The average number of DELETE statements executed per second, the average number of INSERT statements executed per second, the average number of INSERT SELECT statements _ executed per second, the average number of REPLACE statements executed per second, the average number of REPLACE SELECT statements executed per second, the average _ number of SELECT statements executed per second, and the average number of UPDATE statements executed per second. Unit: count/s. |
| MySQL RowDML _ | The average number of rows read from InnoDB tables per second, the average number of rows updated in InnoDB tables per second, the average number of rows deleted from InnoDB tables per second, the average number of rows inserted into InnoDB tables per second, and the average number of physical writes to log files per second. Unit: row/s or count/s. |

O&M

| MySQL MemCpuUsage _ | The CPU utilization and memory usage of the non-serverless ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instance within the entire operating system. Unit: %. |
|---|---|
| MySQL IOPS _ | The input/output operations per second (IOPS) of the RDS instance. Unit: count/s. |
| MySQL DetailedSpaceUsage _ | The details about the disk usage of the RDS instance. These details include the total amount of disk space occupied by the RDS instance, the amount of disk space occupied by data files, the amount of disk space occupied by log files, the amount of disk space occupied by temporary files, and the amount of disk space occupied by system files. Unit: MB. |
| slavestat | The latency of data replication to the read-only RDS instance of the RDS instance. Unit: seconds. |
| MySQL ThreadStatus _ | The number of active threads and the number of threads connected. Unit: threads. |
| MySQL ReplicationDelay _ | The latency of data replication to the secondary RDS instance of the RDS instance. Unit: seconds. |
| MySQL ReplicationThread _ | The status of the I/O thread and the status of the SQL thread. The value 1 indicates that the thread is normal, and the value 0 indicates that the thread is lost. |
| MySQL ROW LOCK _ _ | The maximum time of a row-level lock that has been waited for in milliseconds, the average time of row-level locks that have been waited for in milliseconds, and the number of times the row-level locks have been waited for. |
| MySQL SelectScan _ | The number of times that full table scans are performed on the RDS instance. Unit: scans. |

down list to view the status of the task.

##### 6.1.6.2 Manage temporarily closed tasks

This topic describes how to manage temporarily closed tasks.
1. Log on to the ApsaraDB Operations and Maintenance System.
2. In the left-side navigation pane of the **ApsaraDB Operations and Maintenance System** ,
click **Task management**. In the upper-left corner of the Instance tasks page, select
**Temporarily Closed tasks** from the drop-down list.
Click the **name** of a task. In the message that appears, view the steps during the execution of the task. Click the **operation object** of a task to view the tasks for this operation object. Click the **executor** of a task to view the information of the executor. Click **Operation** in the **Operation** column of a task to view the reason why the task is temporarily closed. ### 6.2 Data Transmission Service

#### 6.2.1 DTS O&M console overview

The Data Transmission Service (DTS) O&M console is a backend system for DTS. This topic describes the features of the DTS O&M console.

**Features**

The DTS O&M console provides the following features: You can view the information about DTS tasks, such as the basic information, source database information, and destination database information. You can view the information about performance monitoring and alerts. You can manage clusters. You can manage various resources of DTS.

#### 6.2.2 Log on to the DTS O&M console

This topic describes how to log on to the Data Transmission Service (DTS) O&M console as a role such as an O&M engineer.

**Prerequisites**

1. In the address bar, enter the endpoint of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
Press the ENTER key. O&M

> **Note:** You can click the current language in the upper-right corner to switch to another language. Simplified Chinese and English are supported.

2. In the top navigation bar of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console, click **Products**.
3. Choose **Databases** > **Data Transmission Service**. Then, you are navigated to the **DTS**
**O&M console**.

#### 6.2.3 Task management

##### 6.2.3.1 Manage tasks

You can view and manage all existing tasks and asynchronous tasks on the Task Management page.
1. Log on to the Data Transmission Service (DTS) O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
O&M
3. In the upper part of the page, you can enter a keyword in the search box and click **Search**
to search for tasks.

> **Note:** You can also click **Advanced Options** to specify more filter conditions to filter tasks.

4. Find the task that you want to manage and click the task name.
5. On the **Task Details** page, perform the following operations based on your business
requirements: View the details of the task. You can view the instance information, task information, source database information, destination database information, and DStore information. View the basic information of a module. a. Find a module such as the Schema Migration, Full Data Migration, or Data Synchronization module and click **Details**. b. On the **Basic Information** tab, you can view the basic information of the module, including the task ID, the IP address of the server on which the module is run, and the running version.

> **Note:** For example, the value of the Running Version parameter without the core- prefix indicates the running version.

View the point in time at which the latest data record is synchronized to the destination database. a. Find the Data Synchronization module and click **Details**. b. On the **Basic Information** tab, view the **Checkpoint** parameter whose value indicates the point in time at which the latest data record is synchronized to the destination database. Perform full data verification. In the upper-right corner of the Task Details page, click **Full Data Verification**. In the dialog box that appears, configure the parameters and click **OK**.

> **Note:** This feature is supported only if both the source and destination databases are MySQL databases.

View user operation records. In the **Task Information** section, click **View User Actions** next to Task ID to view the operation records of the task. Modify the consumption checkpoint. This feature applies only to change tracking tasks. In the **Task Information** section, click **Modify** next to **Consumption Checkpoint**. In the dialog box that appears, enter the UNIX timestamp that corresponds to the consumption checkpoint and click **OK**. Modify the description of the task. O&M In the **Task Information** section, click **Modify** next to **Task Description**. In the dialog box that appears, enter the description and click **OK**. Modify the configurations of the task. In the **Task Information** section, click **Modify Configurations** to modify the configurations of the task. Release the task. In the **Task Information** section, click **Release Task**.

> **Warning:** After a task is released, all the data of the task is deleted and cannot be retrieved. Proceed with caution.

Update the change tracking information. This feature applies only to change tracking tasks. In the **Task Information** section, click **Update Information**. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

##### 6.2.3.2 Manage the modules of a task

A Data Transmission Service (DTS) task contains multiple modules. This topic describes how to manage the modules of a task.
1. Log on to the DTS O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the task that you want to manage and click the task name.
4. In the upper part of the **Task Details** page, the status of each module of the task is
displayed.

> **Note:** The color of a module indicates the state of the module:
> Red: the Abnormal state.
> Blue: the Running state.
> Yellow: the Paused state.
> Green: the Complete or Not Delayed state.

5. Find a module and click **Details** to go to the management page of the module.
6. On the management page of the module, perform the following operations based on your
business requirements: O&M

> **Note:** In this example, the operations that can be performed on the Schema Migration module are described. You can refer to the operations that can be performed on the Schema Migration module to manage other modules.

On the **Basic Information** tab, you can perform various operations. For example, restart, pause, or skip the module, change the server on which the module is run, or modify the running memory. On the **Migration Objects** tab, you can view the information, status, and table creation statements of the objects involved in the module. On the **Operation History** tab, you can view the O&M operation records of the module. On the **Operation Logs** tab, you can view the operation logs of the module. You can also perform operations on the logs, such as pulling, tracking, previewing, and downloading the logs. On the **User-visible Operation Logs** tab, you can filter and search for operation logs based on specific conditions. On the **Task Progress** tab, you can view the progress of the task.

##### 6.2.8.3 Practices for managing data migration and data synchronization tasks

**data synchronization tasks**

This topic describes how to perform O&M operations on a data migration or data synchronization task in the Data Transmission Service (DTS) O&M console.

**Background information**

On the **Task Details** page, most modules of a data migration task are the same as those of a data synchronization task, except for the last module. When you perform O&M operations on the Task Details page, you can refer to the following examples for both data migration and data synchronization tasks. Figure 1. Modules of a data migration task Figure 2. Modules of a data synchronization task

**Block a precheck item**

If a task fails the precheck and you want to skip the failed precheck item, you can block the precheck item in the DTS O&M console.

> **Note:** Before you block a precheck item, you must be aware of the issues that are detected in the precheck and the impact of the block. For example, if you block a precheck item for permissions on the source database, you may fail to complete a data migration or data synchronization task due to insufficient permissions.

1. Log on to the DTS console.
2. In the left navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the target task and click the task name.
4. On the **Task Details** page, find the **Precheck** module and click **Details**.
5. On the **Precheck** page, click the **Check Items** tab.
6. Find the precheck item that you want to block and click **Block** in the **Actions** column.
7. After you block the precheck item, you can restart the task in the DTS console to perform a
precheck again.

**Troubleshoot schema migration issues**

The Schema Migration module is used to migrate the schemas of the objects to be migrated from the source database to the destination database, such as tables and views.
1. Log on to the DTS console.
2. In the left navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the target task and click the task name.
4. On the **Task Details** page, find the **Schema Migration** module and click **Details**.
5. On the **Basic Information** tab, you can view the IP address of the server on which the
Schema Migration module is run. If the schema migration fails due to a whitelist issue, you can add the IP address to the whitelist of the source or destination database. O&M
6. Click the **Migration Objects** tab. In most cases, you can troubleshoot schema migration
issues on this tab.
7. Find a failed object and click the Failed icon in the Status column. For example, the error
message indicates that the schema migration fails due to a syntax issue. In this case, click
**View Creation Syntax** in the Actions column to view the table creation statements that
DTS obtains from the source database.
8. Troubleshoot the issue based on the obtained statements. In this example, the view
definition cannot be obtained due to insufficient permissions of the database account. As a result, the schema migration fails. To resolve the issue, grant the required permissions to the database account.

**Troubleshoot full data migration issues**

1. Log on to the DTS console.
2. In the left navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the target task and click the task name.
4. On the **Task Details** page, find the **Full Data Migration** module and click **Details**.
5. Click the **Basic Information** tab and perform the following operations.

> **Note:** You can also click the **Migration Objects** and **Run Logs** tabs to troubleshoot issues.

View the IP address of the server on which the Full Data Migration module is run. If the migration fails due to a whitelist issue, you can add the IP address to the whitelist of the source or destination database. Troubleshoot the issue based on the error message. In this example, the request data

**Troubleshoot data synchronization or incremental data**

**migration issues**

1. Log on to the DTS console.
2. In the left navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the target task and click the task name.
4. Perform the following operations based on your needs:
Troubleshoot a data synchronization issue On the **Task Details** page, find the **Data Synchronization** module and click **Details**. Troubleshoot an incremental data migration issue On the **Task Details** page, find the **Incremental Data Migration** module and click

5. Click the **Basic Information** tab and check the following parameters.
O&M

> **Note:** You can also click the **Run Logs** tab to troubleshoot issues.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Run Node | The IP address of the server on which the module is run. If the synchronization or migration fails due to a whitelist issue, you can add the IP address to the whitelist of the source or destination database. |
| Checkpoint | The point in time at which the module writes the latest data record. This parameter can help you check the accuracy of latency. |
| Latency | The latency of the synchronization or migration. If the Checkpoint parameter indicates that a latency exists, you can troubleshoot the issue based on the logs. |
| Traffic | The traffic generated during the synchronization or migration. The traffic changes in normal cases. If the value remains 0, an error may occur when DTS writes incremental data. |
| Error Message | The error logs displayed for troubleshooting. |

In this example, the error message indicates that the synchronization or migration fails due to an incorrect database account or password. You can return to the **Task Details** page, and click **Modify Configurations** to modify the database account or password. Then, restart the task.

##### 6.2.8.4 Practices for managing change tracking tasks

###### tasks

This topic describes how to perform O&M operations on a change tracking task in the Data Transmission Service (DTS) O&M console.

**Background information**

Change tracking tasks are divided into the new version and the old version: New version: A change tracking task of the new version contains a Precheck module and an Incremental Data Service module. The O&M operations that you can perform on change tracking tasks are the same as those on data migration or data synchronization tasks. For more information, see Practices for managing data migration and data synchronization tasks. Old version: For a change tracking task of the old version, the Task Details page contains only the **Basic Information** section. In this example, a change tracking task of the old version is used.
1. Log on to the DTS console.
2. In the left navigation pane, choose **Task Management > All Tasks** or **Task**
**Management > Asynchronous Tasks**.
3. Find the target task and click the task name.
4. On the **Task Details** page, check the consumption checkpoint and timestamp range. The
consumption checkpoint must be within the timestamp range. O&M
5. In the lower part of the page, copy the endpoint of the topic in the **DStore Information**
section.
6. In DRC Workbench, find the topic based on the endpoint and manage the topic. For more
information, see Manage change tracking tasks in DRC Workbench.
7. On the **Incremental Management** tab of DRC Workbench, find the store that you want to
manage and click the **+** icon next to the store name to view the start consumption checkpoint, current consumption checkpoint, and status of the store.

#### 7.1.3 Broker management

This topic describes how to view the basic information and configurations of a broker.

**Background information**

e O&M In ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ, broker management is essential to ensure the efficient and stable operation of the message system. As one core component of ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ, brokers are responsible for storing, forwarding, and querying messages.

**View broker information**

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Broker Management**.
3. On the **Broker Management** page, select a cluster from the **Cluster name** drop-down
list.
4. Optional. You can search for a broker by broker name.
5. In the broker list, view the basic information about the brokers.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Broker name | The unique name of a broker group. |
| Master/Slave | Indicates the role of the broker instance in the cluster to which it belongs. It can be the primary node or a secondary node. |
| Host IP | The address of a single broker in the network, which consists of an IP address and a port number. |
| Status | The status of the broker. readonly: indicates that the broker is in read-only mode. online: indicates that the broker is online and working properly. offline: indicates that the broker is offline and may be unable to provide services due to faults or other reasons. |
| HA status | The operational status of the current broker instance. SYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the synchronous state. ONLY MASTER: indicates that the broker is _ the only primary node and does not have a corresponding secondary node. ASYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is _ in the asynchronous state, that is, data is being synchronized from the primary node to the secondary node. HAIF STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the semi-synchronous state. |

e O&M

| Inflow TPS | The number of inbound messages per second. Click a value in the Inflow TPS column. In the Top 10 Business production traffic analysis dialog box, view information about the top 10 topics with the most messages sent by current producers, including Topic, TPS, and Timestamp. |
|---|---|
| Outflow TPS | The number of outbound messages per second. Click a value in the Outflow TPS column. In the Top 10 Business consumption traffic analysis dialog box, view information about the top 10 topics with the most consumed messages and the corresponding consumer groups, including Topic, Group, TPS, and Timestamp. |

6. On the **Broker Management** page, click the name of a broker or click **View** in the
**Operation** column to view the details of the broker.
On the **Basic information** tab, view **Basic information** and **Key indicators** of the broker.
**Basic information**: displays the information about the primary and secondary nodes
of the broker.
**Key indicators**: displays information such as **Send tps**, **Pull tps**, **Disk Usage**, **Disk**
**space**, and **Save duration** of the broker. You can also analyze the trend charts of
**in/out tps**, **CPU**, **Memory**, **Disk IO**, and **Network IO** over a period of time. You can
specify a time range of **15 minutes**, **1 hour**, **6 hours**, or a custom time range. On the **Configuration information** tab, view **Key**, **Value**, and **Description** of the configuration items. You can click **Modification** in the **Operation** column to modify
**Configuration Value**.
On the **VPC management** tab, view the virtual private cloud (VPC) information about the broker cluster, including **VPC ID/name**, **Switch ID**, **Region**, **Cluster**, **broker VIP**, and
**nameserver VIP**.

**Prohibit the write operation on a broker**

In ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ, you can prohibit the write operation on a broker to prevent new messages from being written to the broker during maintenance, troubleshooting, or emergencies. This prevents data inconsistency or other potential issues.

> **Note:** Only brokers in the **online****state** support write prohibition.

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Broker Management**.
3. On the **Broker Management** page, find the broker that you want to manage and click
**Write forbidden** in the **Operation** column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Restore the write operation on a broker**

e O&M If you want to write new messages to the broker, you can restore the write operation on the broker.

> **Note:** Only brokers in the **readonly** state support the restoration of write operation.

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Broker Management**.
3. On the **Broker Management** page, find the broker that you want to manage and click
**Release write prohibition** in the **Operation** column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Unpublish/publish a broker**

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Broker Management**.
3. On the **Broker Management** page, find the broker that you want to manage and click
**Offline**/**Online** in the **Operation** column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Restart a broker**

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Broker Management**.
3. On the **Broker Management** page, find the broker that you want to manage and click
**Restart** in the **Operation** column.
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

A hot upgrade of ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ refers to a version update or configuration adjustment without service interruption to reduce system downtime and maintain service continuity.

An upgrade approval task exists in the current system.
1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Copilot > Upgrade**.
3. On the **Hot upgrade** page, click **create a hot upgrade task** .
4. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Broker name | The unique name of a broker group. |
| Broker address | The address of a single broker in the network, which consists of an IP address and a port number. |
| Master/Slave | Indicates the role of the broker instance in the cluster to which it belongs. It can be the primary node or a secondary node. |

e O&M

| HA status | The operational status of the current broker instance. SYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the synchronous state. ONLY MASTER: indicates that the broker is _ the only primary node and does not have a corresponding secondary node. ASYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is _ in the asynchronous state, that is, data is being synchronized from the primary node to the secondary node. HAIF STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the semi-synchronous state. |
|---|---|
| Update time | The time when the HA status was last updated or checked. |
| Upgrade Status | The upgrade status of the broker. |
| Whether to disable writing | Indicates whether to prohibit writing messages to the broker. Yes: indicates that messages cannot be written to the broker. No: indicates that messages can be written to the broker. |

In the Top 10 Business consumption traffic analysis message, view information about the top 10 topics with the most consumed messages and the corresponding consumer groups, including Topic, Group, TPS, and Timestamp. |

5. Make sure that **HA status** of the broker in the broker cluster to be upgraded is
**SYNC_STATE**.

> **Note:** In this example, a group of primary and secondary nodes is upgraded. You can repeat Step 6 through Step 9 to upgrade other groups of primary and secondary nodes.

6. Disable writing for a group of primary/secondary nodes.

i. After **Upgrade Status** of the primary and secondary nodes changes to **Upgradeable**, click **Upgrade** in the **Operation** column of the primary node. In the message that appears, click **OK**. ii. After **Upgrade Status** of the primary node changes to **Upgrade completed**, click

##### 7.1.6.2 Disaster recovery deployment

This topic describes how to deploy disaster recovery for a single cluster and scale out a disaster recovery cluster.

**Background information**

After the delivery phase ends, the efficiency of deploying ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ disaster recovery must be improved to reduce the impact on online business. Disaster recovery relationships need to be established in the O&M phase, and O&M personnel schedule and implement related changes.

**Prerequisites**

The cluster is normal. The upgrade and scale-out operations in the primary and secondary data centers follow the standard processes. The primary data center is started normally, whereas the secondary data center is blocked. Through the broker_location, you can view the information about the primary and secondary nodes, and a broker_name table has been successfully allocated in the primary data center.

**Usage notes**

A cluster that contains topics of globally ordered messages does not support disaster recovery deployment. Check the models for the physical nodes where all brokers of ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ are located in the primary and secondary data centers. Make sure that a group of primary and secondary physical nodes uses the same model and disk capacity. When you select a node in the secondary data center for the disaster recovery deployment, make sure that the model of the selected node in the secondary data center is the same as the model of the selected node in the primary data center. If you cannot select physical nodes with the same model from the primary and secondary data centers, proceed with caution or submit a ticket to contact the planner to assess the model risk.

**Deploy disaster recovery for a single cluster**

e O&M

> **Note:** You can terminate a task in the completed or uncompleted state. If you click **End** **disaster recovery task**, the task information table is cleared.

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Copilot > Disaster Recovery**.
3. On the **Disaster recovery setup** page, click **Create a disaster recovery task** .
4. In the dialog box that appears, configure the **Cluster** and **Main engine room** parameters
and click **OK**. This operation triggers task creation. The system checks whether an unfinished deployment task exists. If no unfinished deployment task exists, the existing cluster information is synchronized to the new task. The new brokers in the primary data center are displayed at the end of the list and will be published. In addition, the metadata file of a primary broker in the cluster is cached.

> **Note:** In this example, a group of primary and secondary nodes is upgraded. You can repeat Step 5 through Step 10 to upgrade other groups of primary and secondary nodes.

6. Unpublish the secondary node.
i. When the traffic drops to 0, click **Downline** in the Operation column of the secondary node. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the secondary node in the secondary data center is added, click **Go online** and then click **OK**. ##### 7.1.6.3 Disaster recovery removal

This topic describes how to remove a disaster recovery relationship.

**Background information**

Disaster recovery relationships between brokers can be removed to scale in a disaster recovery cluster into a single-data center cluster, perform a cluster migration, or implement phased migration to the IT Application Innovation (ITAI) ecosystem.

**Prerequisites**

The cluster is normal. The upgrade and scale-out operations in the primary and secondary data centers follow the standard processes. The primary node is deployed in the primary data center.

**Applicable scope**

A disaster recovery data center needs to be converted into a single data center. A cluster needs to be migrated across data centers. Phased migration to the ITAI ecosystem is required.

> **Note:** The following procedure uses a group of brokers as an example. The procedure is the same for other groups of brokers.

1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Copilot > Disaster Recovery Remove**.
3. On the **Release of disaster recovery relationship** page, select a cluster from the
**Cluster name** drop-down list.
4. The list displays the basic information about brokers.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Broker name | The unique name of a broker group. |

e O&M

| Master/Slave | Indicates the role of the broker instance in the cluster to which it belongs. It can be the primary node or a secondary node. |
|---|---|
| Host IP | The address of a single broker in the network, which consists of an IP address and a port number. |
| Status | The status of the broker. readonly: indicates that the broker is in read-only mode. online: indicates that the broker is online and working properly. offline: indicates that the broker is offline and may be unable to provide services due to faults or other reasons. |
| HA status | The operational status of the current broker instance. SYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the synchronous state. ONLY MASTER: indicates that the broker is _ the only primary node and does not have a corresponding secondary node. ASYNC STATE: indicates that the broker is _ in the asynchronous state, that is, data is being synchronized from the primary node to the secondary node. HAIF STATE: indicates that the broker is in _ the semi-synchronous state. |
| Inflow TPS | The number of inbound messages per second. Click a value in the Inflow TPS column. In the Top 10 Business production traffic analysis dialog box, view information about the top 10 topics with the most messages sent by current producers, including Topic, TPS, and Timestamp. |
| Outflow TPS | The number of outbound messages per second. Click a value in the Outflow TPS column. In the Top 10 Business consumption traffic analysis dialog box, view information about the top 10 topics with the most consumed messages and the corresponding consumer groups, including Topic, Group, TPS, and Timestamp. |

5. Disable writing for a group of primary/secondary nodes.
e O&M On the **Release of disaster recovery relationship** page, click **Write forbidden** in the
**Operation** column for a group of primary and secondary nodes. In the message that
appears, click **OK**. This operation disables the write feature of the corresponding node and observes that the traffic drops to 0.
6. Click **Remove the disaster recovery relationship** in the **Operation** column of the
secondary node, and then click **OK**. This operation stops the broker and removes the information about the node from the broker_name table.
7. After the disaster recovery relationship is removed, you can clear the metadata. Click
**Clean up data** in the **Operation** column of the secondary node to delete files other than

```
 /home/admin/store/broker.conf ,  /home/admin/store/config/topics.json , and
 /home/admin/store/config/subscriptionGroup.json .
```

##### 7.1.6.4 Capacity analysis

You can view the performance metrics of a cluster within a specified time range, including the cluster-level resource usage overview and historical resource usage trends.

**Background information**

Capacity analysis is designed to provide an intuitive and comprehensive visualization platform for you to evaluate and monitor the current load status and capacity usage trends of an ApsaraMQ for RocketMQ cluster. This supports scientific decision-making and proactive O&M.
1. Log in to the RocketMQ 4.x Operations Console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Copilot > Capacity Analyze**.
3. On the **Capacity Analysis** page, specify **Cluster name** and **Time range**, and select a
Broker specification.
4. The page displays the Transactions Per Second (TPS) trend and save time trend.

> **Note:** Move the pointer over a chart to view the detailed values at the current time point.

**tps trend**: displays the trend charts of the inbound message rate, outbound message
rate, and total throughput of the cluster. The dotted orange line in the chart represents the theoretical maximum TPS of the broker specification.
**Save time trend**: displays the trend chart of the retention period of messages on the
broker. The default message retention period is 72 hours. e O&M

## 8 Big data O&M

### 8.1 Bigdata Manager

#### 8.1.1 Apsara Big Data Manager

Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) is an operations and maintenance (O&M) platform tailored for big data services. ABM supports monitoring, management, and O&M in multiple dimensions, such as business, services, clusters, and hosts. Customer O&M teams or on-site personnel can easily complete unified O&M of big data services based on the service capabilities of ABM. ABM supports the following services: MaxCompute DataWorks Realtime Compute (Blink) Quick BI DataHub MaxCompute DataWorks Realtime Compute Quick BI Graph Analytics DataHub ABM supports O&M on big data services from the perspectives of business, services, clusters, and hosts. ABM also allows you to update big data services, customize alert configurations, and view the O&M history. ABM provides the following features: Allows you to view and configure MaxCompute projects. Allows you to perform O&M on big data services from the perspectives of business, services, clusters, and hosts. Allows you to manage jobs, accounts, alerts, patches, and health check items of various services. Allows you to manage data stored in Tablestore and Object Storage Service (OSS).

#### 8.1.2 Common operations

The data tables and legends in the ABM console help you perform common operations. This topic uses MaxCompute to describe the common operations.

**Search**

You can search for an item in a table by column, which is similar to filtering projects. For example, you can perform the following steps to search for a checker: &M
1. Log on to the ABM console. In the upper-left corner of the ANM console, click the More icon
and select MaxCompute. In the upper-right corner of the **MaxCompute** page, click **O&M**. On the page that appears, click the **Clusters** tab. On the Clusters page, click the **Health**
**Status** tab.
2. In the checker list, click the **Filter** icon in a column and enter a keyword in the search box.
3. Click **Search**. The checkers that meet the requirements appear.
4. If the search result is not met your business requirements, you can continue performing
this operation on other columns.

**Sort items based on a column**

You can sort items based on a column in ascending or descending order. The procedure and display method are different from those described in Common operations.
1. Log on to the ABM console. In the upper-left corner of the ANM console, click the More icon
and select MaxCompute. In the upper-right corner of the **MaxCompute** page, click **O&M**. On the page that appears, click the **Clusters** tab. On the Clusters page, click the **Health**
**Status** tab.
2. In the checker list, click a column heading or the sort icon in the column heading to sort
checkers in ascending order or descending order. The highlighted up arrow indicates that the checkers are sorted in ascending order. The highlighted down arrow indicates that the checkers are sorted in descending order. &M

**View the trend charts for a MaxCompute cluster**

Log on to the ABM console. In the upper-left corner of the ANM console, click the More icon and select MaxCompute. In the upper-right corner of the **MaxCompute** page, click **O&M**. On the page that appears, click the **Clusters** tab. On the Clusters page, you can view relevant metrics, such as CPU and memory usage, of the desired cluster. The following example describes the CPU usage of a cluster. The trend chart displays the trend lines of the total CPU usage (cpu), CPU usage for executing code in kernel space (sys), and CPU usage for executing code in user space (user) for the specified cluster over time in different colors. Click in the upper-right corner of the chart to zoom in the chart. You can specify the start time and end time in the upper-left corner of the enlarged chart to view the CPU utilization of the cluster in the specified period.

&M In the ABM console, the procedures of viewing the cluster running status for different services are the same. This topic uses one of the services as an example.

in the upper-left corner and then click a service.
