###### 8.1.5.2.2 Create and configure a zone-disaster recovery project in MaxCompute

**recovery project in MaxCompute**

This topic describes how to create and configure a zone-disaster recovery project in MaxCompute.

**Background**

To avoid competition among clusters for resources such as bandwidth and storage space, you can create disaster recovery projects based on your business requirements.

**Usage notes**

When you configure a disaster recovery project, take note of the following items: If the **EnableEvent** parameter is set to `true` , the data in the project is synchronized immediately after it is changed. Additionally, the amount of data that is synchronized each time is all data in the table or partition. For example, if a non-partitioned table contains 1 TB of data and one data entry needs to be inserted into the table, the entire 1 TB of data must be copied to the secondary data center. If the data entry is written 10 times within 1 minute, the 1 TB of data is copied to the secondary data center 10 times within 1 minute. As a result, 9 TB of data needs to be recycled. Therefore, we strongly recommend that you disable real-time replication to reduce the bandwidth and storage pressure on data centers. We also recommend that you configure a periodic replication policy. For example, you can set the **ScanMetaInterval** parameter to 6 hours, which means that the metadata is scanned and replicated every 6 hours. That is,
**EnableEvent** = `false` and **ScanMetaInterval** = `21600` . Note that 6 hours is equal to
21,600 seconds. To prevent MaxCompute from consuming the full bandwidth of the cluster during peak hours, we recommend that you specify the **InstanceCount** parameter to limit synchronization bandwidth. Each InstanceCount uses approximately 10 MB to 50 MB of bandwidth. If the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is always greater than the synchronization interval, the amount of data to be synchronized is very large and all data cannot be synchronized at a time. Solutions: i. Check the disk space usage of the secondary cluster and determine whether the data synchronization failure is caused by insufficient cluster disk space. You can use one of the following methods for inspection: Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to view the disk space usage of the secondary cluster. Log in to the MaxCompute AG in the secondary data center and run the following command to view the disk space usage of the secondary cluster. The unit of disk space is bytes (B). To convert a value in bytes to gigabytes (GB), divide the value by 1024 × 1024 × 1024. The ${projectName} parameter needs to be replaced with the actual project name.

```
pu quota /product/aliyun/odps/${projectName}
```

ii. Adjust the following two parameters based on the actual volume of data to be synchronized and the bandwidth and RPO requirements: Increase the value of the ScanMetaInterval parameter. This results in a larger RPO but ensures data consistency to the maximum extent. &M Increase the value of the InstanceCount parameter. This results in a larger bandwidth used for data synchronization. Therefore, pay attention to the bandwidth of the primary and secondary data centers to avoid affecting data synchronization of other services. We recommend that you specify the value of the InstanceCount parameter as available bandwidth × 0.5/project data to be synchronized/50 MB based on the bandwidth of the on-premises primary and secondary data centers. For example, if the acceptable RPO is 1 day and the amount of data to be synchronized is 1 TB, the value of the InstanceCount parameter is calculated as 1 TB/(24 × 60 × 60) . To ensure sufficient bandwidth, you can multiply the calculated result by 2.

**Create a disaster recovery project**

Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator and create a multi-cluster project. For more information, see **Apsara Stack Help CenterBig Data Services > MaxCompute**
**> User Guide > Preparations > Create Project**.

> **Note:** Single-cluster projects do not support disaster recovery.

**Configure the disaster recovery project**

1. Log in to the Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) console.
2. Click the
icon in the upper-left corner and choose **Big Data Computing >**
**MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the page that appears, click Operation and maintenance. The
**Business operation and maintenance** tab is displayed by default. In the left-side
navigation pane, choose **Project Management > Project List**.
4. Find the project that you want to configure, and click **Resource replication** in the **Actions**
column.
5. In the **View Multi-Cluster Replication configuration** panel, set the **Open** parameter to
**true** and specify the required information in the **Configuration** field.
&M The following table describes the key configuration items.

| Parameter | Key parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Open | / | Valid values: true: enables multi-cluster replication. false: disables multi-cluster replication. Default value: false. |
| Configuration | ScanMetaInteva l | Specifies the data synchronization interval. Unit: seconds. |
|   | InstanceCount | Limits the data synchronization bandwidth. |
|   | SyncObject | Specifies the synchronization cluster and the type of data to be synchronized. Change the name of the MaxCompute cluster to the name of the on-premises primary or secondary cluster, as shown in the preceding figure, to enable full data replication in MaxCompute. Important Note that the name of the MaxCompute cluster must be in uppercase letters. |

&M

|   | EnableEvent | Specifies whether data is synchronized in real time. When this parameter is set to true , any data in the primary cluster changes is immediately synchronized to the secondary cluster, and the ScanMetaInteval parameter becomes invalid. Important If you enable real-time synchronization or specify a short data synchronization interval, more network bandwidth is consumed. We recommend that you disable real-time synchronization and increase the data synchronization interval when you need to synchronize a large amount of data. |
|---|---|---|

6. Optional. After you modify the parameters in the**Configuration**field, click**Compare**
**Versions**to view the highlighted version differences.
7. Confirm the correctness of parameter configurations and click **Run**.

> **Note:** If the modified configurations do not take effect, the reason may be that the zone- disaster recovery feature of ABM is not enabled. In this case, contact Apsara Stack technical support.

#### 8.1.6 Management

##### 8.1.6.1 Overview

The management module is the configuration and software management center of Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM). It is an important functional module that supports and customizes O&M items for services. The management module supports the following features: Jobs: allows you to run jobs to perform O&M operations on big data products. API Management: allows you to manage the permissions of ABM APIs. Health Checks: allows you to create health check items and apply them to service hosts. Operation Logs: allows you to view the job execution records and other service O&M operations in ABM.

##### 8.1.6.2 Jobs

###### 8.1.6.2.1 Overview

This topic describes the UIs for job management and terms related to jobs in Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM). ABM allows you to run jobs to perform O&M operations on big data services. Jobs in ABM are run to perform O&M operations on physical devices in a cluster. The Job Services module contains the **Job Execution** page. &M

**Terms**

Terms related to jobs include: Ordinary job: A job that can only be manually run. No timer settings is specified. Cron job: A job that is automatically run based on timer settings.

**Job Execution page**

The **Job Execution** page contains the following tabs:

| Tab | Description |
|---|---|
| Jobs | You can view and run ordinary jobs, and view their execution history. You can search, copy, export, and delete ordinary jobs. |
| Cron Jobs | You can enable, disable, view, or run cron jobs, and view their execution history. You can search, copy, export, and delete cron jobs. |
| Execution History | You can view the execution history of ordinary and cron jobs. You can search, view details of, and preview job execution history. |

###### 8.1.6.2.2 Jobs

###### 8.1.6.2.2.1 Manually run a job

After you create an ordinary job in the Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) console, you must manually run the job to perform O&M operations on the corresponding service. You can also manually run a cron job.

**Prerequisites**

An ABM administrator account is obtained.
1. Log in to the ABM console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Job Services**.
&M
4. On the **Job Execution** page, click the **Jobs** tab.
If you need to manually run a cron job, click the **Cron Jobs** tab. The procedure for manually running a cron job is the same as that for an ordinary job. This topic uses an ordinary job as an example.
5. On the **Jobs** page, find a job and click **Run** in the Actions column.
6. In the dialog box that appears, configure the required parameters in the **Configure target**
**group and parameters** step and click **Next Step**.
7. Perform the **Confirm Risk** operation and click **Confirm**.
After you click Confirm, an execution record is automatically generated on the **Execution**
**History** page. For more information, see View the execution history.
8. On the Job Execution page, click **Start** at the top to run the job.
If you exit the Job Execution page without performing any operations, you can find the execution record about a job on the **Execution History** page and click **View** to go to the detailed execution page. &M

###### 8.1.6.2.2.2 Enable or disable a cron job

By default, cron jobs are disabled in the Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) console and do not take effect. You need to manually enable cron jobs. If you do not need a cron job to run during a specified period of time, you can manually disable it.

**Prerequisites**

An ABM administrator account is obtained.
1. Log in to the ABM console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Job Services**.
4. On the **Job Execution** page, click the **Cron Jobs** tab.
5. On the **Cron Jobs** page, you can enable or disable a cron job.
To enable a cron job in the Inactive status, click **Enable** in the Actions column of the cron job. After a cron job is enabled, its **Status** changes to **Active**, and the **Enable** button changes to **Disable**. To disable a cron job in the Active status, click **Disable** in the Actions column of the cron job. After a cron job is disabled, its **Status** changes to **Inactive**. The **Disable** button changes to **Enable**.

###### 8.1.6.2.2.3 View the execution history of a job

Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) allows you to view the execution history of a specific job to learn its execution status.

**Prerequisites**

An ABM administrator account is obtained.

**Background information**

After you confirm to run a job, ABM generates logs for the job execution. You can learn the execution status by using the log data. The **Execution History** page provides the following features: Provides information such as the trigger mode, current status, start time, and end time of each job. Provides job execution details and parameter configuration information, and allows you to download job execution details. Allows you to perform certain operations depending on the job status. For example, you can
**Start** a job that is in the **Pending** state or **Retry** the execution of a job that is in the
**Exception** state.
This topic describes how to view the execution history of an ordinary job. You can follow a similar procedure to view the execution history of a cron job.
1. Log in to the ABM console.
&M
2. In the upper-right corner of the ABM console, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the page that appears, click **Job Services**.
3. On the **Job Execution** page, click the **Jobs** tab.
4. On the **Jobs** page, click **History** in the Actions column of an ordinary job. The **Execution**
**History** page appears.
On the **Execution History** page, you can view the execution history of this job. For more information, see View the execution history.

###### 8.1.6.2.2.4 View execution history

Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) allows you to view the execution history of jobs and schemes to learn about their execution details.

**Prerequisites**

An ABM administrator account is obtained.

**Background information**

After you confirm the execution of a job or scheme, a record is automatically generated on the Execution History page. The **Execution History** page provides the following features: Provides information such as the trigger mode, current status, start time, and end time of each job. Provides job execution details and parameter configuration information, and allows you to download job execution details. Allows you to perform certain operations depending on the job status. For example, you can run a job that is in the **Pending** state or retry the execution of a job that is in the
**Exception** state.
1. Log in to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the ABM console, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the page that appears, click **Job Services**.
3. On the **Job Execution** page, click the **Execution History** tab.
4. If many records are displayed, you can filter the records by specifying the Instance Name,
Time Range, and Execution Status. Then, click **Search** to find specific records.
5. Click **Details** in the Actions column of a record to view the job execution details.

| Execution status | Feature | Procedure |

If the step contains a command, the Commands and Execution Parameters pages will appear. You can view the command content and the command execution parameters. |

&M

When the step that has exceptions is reset to the Pending state, the execution status becomes Paused. If the step contains a command, the Commands and Execution Parameters pages will appear. You can view the command content and the command execution parameters. |
|   | Retry the failed step | In the failed step, click Retry to execute the step again. |
|   | Skip the failed step | In the failed step, click Skip to skip this step and execute the subsequent steps. |

&M

| Failed |   |   |
|---|---|---|

When the failed step is reset to the Pending state, the execution status becomes Paused. You can click Continue in the upper-right corner of the job details page to execute the step again. |

##### 8.1.6.3 Health management

###### 8.1.6.3.1 Health management

Apsara Big Data Manager (ABM) provides a wide variety of built-in checkers for each big data service. These checkers are used to check service faults and send alerts. This helps you detect and fix faults in a timely manner.

**Prerequisites**

Your ABM account is granted the required permissions on services on which you want to perform O&M. The alert sources and checkers of the monitoring items are obtained.

**Background information**

Different services have different scheduling and monitoring items, but the configuration and operations that can be performed on services are the same. This topic describes the scheduling and monitoring items of MaxCompute. &M Scheduling: Checkers run scheduling scripts on the servers of specific TianJi roles and generate raw alert data. Raw alert data provides information about the checker, server, alert severity, and alert content. Raw alert data is stored in the ABM database. Monitoring: You can mount checkers to service pages in ABM. You can configure filter policies to display alerts about high priority checkers. Both the scheduling items and monitoring items are built-in and you cannot add more scheduling and monitoring items. However, you can modify some parameters of the items, such as whether to enable an item, running parameters, and description. In addition, you can configure mount points of the monitoring items or delete monitoring items.

**View details and mount points of scheduling items**

The mount points of scheduling items are built-in and you cannot add, modify, or delete mount points. The mount points of the scheduling items correspond to the list of all hosts corresponding to the Apsara Infrastructure Management role that runs the scheduling script.
1. Log on to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the ABM console, click the
icon and select **MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the MaxCompute page, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the **Management** page, click **Health Checks**. The **Scheduling** tab appears. The **Scheduling** tab displays all scheduling items of the current product.
4. On the **Scheduling** tab, find the desired scheduling item and click **View** in the Actions
column to view the details of the scheduling item.
5. Click the plus sign to expand a scheduling item. Then, view the mount points of the
scheduling item. &M

**Modify a scheduling item**

You can configure the scheduling interval and running parameters of a scheduling item, and configure whether to enable the scheduling item.
1. Log on to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the ABM console, click the
icon and select **MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the MaxCompute page, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the **Management** page, click **Health Checks**. The **Scheduling** tab appears.
4. On the **Scheduling** tab, find the desired scheduling item and click **Edit** in the Actions
column. In the Modify Checker dialog box, configure relevant parameters. &M
**Type**: The value **System Default** indicates that parameters, such as **Execution Interval**
and **Parameters**, use the default settings. The value **Custom** indicates that the parameters can be customized.

> **Note:** Configure the **Execution Interval** parameter based on the **crontab** command.

5. Click **OK**. The scheduling item is modified.

**View faulty hosts**

You can view all the faulty hosts in the current cluster.
1. Log on to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the ABM console, click the
icon and select **MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the MaxCompute page, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the **Management** page, click **Health Checks**. The **Scheduling** tab appears.
4. In the upper-right corner of the Scheduling tab, click **Faulty Servers** to view the faulty
hosts in the cluster. &M The list of the faulty hosts shows all faulty hosts in the current cluster and the role of each host in the Apsara Infrastructure Management.

**Modify a monitoring item**

You can modify the name and description of a monitoring item and determine whether to enable the monitoring item. The alert sources and checkers of monitoring items are built-in. We recommend that you do not modify them.
1. Log on to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the ABM console, click the
icon and select **MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the MaxCompute page, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the **Management** page, click **Health Checks**.
4. On the **Health Management** page, click the **Monitoring** tab. The **Monitoring** tab
appears. The **Monitoring** tab displays all monitoring items of the current service.
5. On the **Monitoring** tab, find the desired monitoring item and click **Modify** in the Actions
column to modify the configuration of the monitoring item. &M
6. Click **OK**. The scheduling item is modified.

**Add a mount point for a monitoring item**

After a mount point is added for a monitoring item, the monitoring item mounts the raw alert data to the O&M page of each service in the ABM console.
1. Log on to the ABM console.
2. In the upper-left corner of the ABM console, click the
icon and select **MaxCompute**.
3. In the upper-right corner of the MaxCompute page, click **Management**. In the left-side
navigation pane of the **Management** page, click **Health Checks**.
4. On the **Health Management** page, click the **Monitoring** tab. The **Monitoring** tab
appears.

in the upper-left corner, and then click **MaxCompute**.

| Exception | Click Retry to run the step again. Click Skip to skip this step and execute the subsequent steps. Click Rollback to roll back to the complete status of the previous step. Click Parameter Configuration to view the parameter configuration of the task. Click Cancel to cancel the task. |

##### 8.2.2.1 Cluster list

When you have large numbers of clusters, you can search clusters by cluster ID or customer ID, or filter clusters by namespace. View the basic information of a cluster, including the ID, status, health status, version, number of data nodes, customer ID, and namespace of the cluster. Delete a cluster. ##### 8.2.2.2 Create a cluster

We recommend that you create clusters in the user-side console. If the clusters in the userside console cannot meet your business requirements, you can create clusters in the O&Mside console after assessing the O&M risks. For example, you can create clusters of low specifications for testing or create clusters of Elasticsearch versions other than the suggested versions in the O&M-side console. This topic describes how to create an Elasticsearch cluster in the O&M-side console. &M

> **Note:** For more information about how to create a cluster in the user-side console, see the **Create a cluster** topic in **Elasticsearch User Guide**.

1. Log in to the Elasticsearch O&M console.
2. On the Instance Management page, click **Create Instance**. In the message that appears,
click **Confirm**.
3. In the **Basic Configuration** step, select a zone, chip architecture, and Elasticsearch
version. Then, click **Next**.

> **Note:** We recommend that you select V7.10.0 or V6.8.13.

4. Configure the parameters as described in the following table and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Describe |
|---|---|
| Customer ID | The UID of the organization to which the user belongs. You can perform the following steps to obtain the UID: i. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. In the top navigation bar, click Enterprise. ii. On the Organizations page, click the organization that you want to manage. iii. On the right side of the organization list, click Manage AccessKey Pairs iv. In the Manage AccessKey Pairs dialog box, view the UID of the organization. |
| namespace | The namespace of the Elasticsearch cluster. The namespace is generated by the system and cannot be changed. |
| Cluster Name | Enter the name of the cluster. |

&M

| Instance Specification | Click Modify to modify the resource configuration of each node type. Note We recommend that you create dedicated master nodes and client nodes separately for production clusters. The following example shows how to configure data nodes. Resource Limit: the amount of resources that the current node uses. Storage Type: the type of disk used by the node. The following disk types are supported: fast-disks (HDD), fast-disks-ssd (SSD), and yoda-lvm (shared disk). You can mount yoda-lvm disks to master nodes to optimize resource utilization. We recommend that you use SSDs in scenarios other than logging scenarios. We recommend that you do not mount yoda-lvm disks to data nodes due to high security risks. Node Count: the number of data nodes in the cluster. Data nodes are enabled by default and cannot be disabled. By default, three data nodes are created. You can change the number based on your business requirements. Note If you configure only two data nodes for a cluster that does not contain dedicated master nodes, the cluster has a greater risk of split-brain. This may cause service unavailability. You cannot change the number. Per-node Storage Space: the storage space of each node in the cluster. After you configure this parameter, the system automatically allocates a qualified local disk to each data node based on the storage space that you specified. The specifications of the cluster depend on the size of a single disk. The disk does not support sharing or capacity expansion. Fully Dispersed Required: specifies whether to redeploy data nodes. This avoids deploying multiple data nodes on one physical machine and improves the availability of the cluster. If the number of physical machines is less than the number of data nodes, the cluster fails to be created. Configure this parameter based on your business requirements. |
|---|---|
| Plugin Configuration | Select the Elasticsearch and Kibana plug-ins to be installed when you create the cluster. |
| elasticsearch.yml | Customize the YML file of the Elasticsearch cluster. The file uses YAML in the format of key: value . The colon ( : ) must be followed by a space character. |

&M

| kibana.yml | Customize the YML configuration file of the Kibana cluster. Note This parameter is available only when Kibana nodes are enabled. |
|---|---|

5. Click **Next** to configure network and system parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Network Type | Dedicated Network (single tunnel): The organization to which the virtual private cloud (VPC) and vSwitch belong must be the same as that specified by the Customer ID parameter. Dedicated Network (any tunnel): Do not select this network type unless it is necessary. Note IPv4 is supported by default. To use IPv4/IPv6 dual stack, make sure that the IPv4/IPv6 dual stack switch is turned on. Then, contact the technical support of Alibaba Cloud to modify the configuration file of the cluster. Change the values of the vip protocols and _ elasticsearch.vip protocols parameters in _ .spec.parameters to ipv4+ipv6 , and trigger the cluster to perform a rolling update to complete the configuration. |
| Login Name | elastic: the default account, which cannot be changed. It is used to access Elasticsearch and log in to Kibana. monitoring collector: the account used to manage services. Some _ management features need this account. Note The password must meet the following requirements: The password must contain at least three of the following character types: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and special characters. Supported special characters: ! @ # $ % ^ & * ( ) + - = _ The password must be 12 to 32 characters in length. |

|   | vip protocols _ |
|---|---|
| elasticsearch.vip protocols _ |   |
| .spec.parameters |   |

6. Click **Start Creation**.

##### 8.2.2.6 Backup and recovery

###### 8.2.2.6.1 Snapshots

This topic describes how to use the snapshot feature to configure automatic backup and manually create snapshots.

**Prerequisites**

An Elasticsearch instance is created, and the instance is in the normal state. For more information, see Create an instance.

**Usage notes**

The scheduled backup feature occupies CPU, memory, and disk resources, which may compromise the performance of your instance.
1. Log on to the Search & Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Instance Management**.
3. On the **Instance Management** page, click the target **Instance ID**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Snapshot Backup > Automatic Backup**.
5. On the **Automatic Backup** page, select a repository and click **Save Repository**
**Configuration**.
If no repositories are available, you must first add a repository from the Platform &M Management page. For more information, see Add a repository.
6. Click **Modify Settings**. In the dialog box that appears, specify the backup interval, cycle,
and time, and click **Confirm**.

> **Important:** The first snapshot is a backup of all cluster data. The amount of time required for creating the first snapshot depends on the data volume. We recommend that you create snapshots during off-peak hours.
> The scheduled backup feature compromises the query and write performance of the cluster. Therefore, you need to specify a proper backup frequency and interval. We recommend that you do not specify a short backup interval.

After you confirm the configuration, the system periodically creates backups based on the specified backup cycle. If you want to create a backup immediately, click **Backup Now**. After automatic backup is complete, you can click **Disable Automatic Backup** to disable the feature. If you enable the feature again, you must re-associate a repository. The existing backup records are not affected. You can also query snapshots and refresh the snapshot list.

> **Note:** The snapshot list automatically clears automatic backup records once every hour. Only the latest 10 records are retained. The snapshot list does not clear manual backup records that are generated after you click **Backup Now**.

###### 8.2.2.6.2 Restore data from snapshots

The snapshot restoration feature allows you to restore Elasticsearch data from snapshots with a few clicks. It is suitable for auto and manual data restoration from snapshots. You can use this feature to restore data from snapshots of other Elasticsearch clusters.
1. Log on to the Search & Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Instance Management**.
3. On the **Instance Management** page, click the target **Instance ID**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Snapshot Backup > Snapshot Restore**.
5. On the **Snapshot Restore** page, configure the snapshot from which you want to restore
data.

| Parameter | Description |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bucket | The Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket that stores the cluster snapshot. You can run GET snapshot to view the snapshot. _ |   |   |
| Storage Path | The path of the snapshot in the bucket. Example: snapshot/gyytest-buxuyao.es-essen/ . You can run GET snapshot to view the path. _ |   |   |
|   |   | GET |   |
| Snapshot ID | The ID of the snapshot. After a snapshot is created, a snapshot ID is generated. |   |   |

|   |   | snapshot/gyytest-buxuyao.es-essen/ |
|---|---|---|
|   | snapshot _ |   |

&M

| Access Key | The AccessKey ID of your Apsara Stack tenant account. |
|---|---|
| Secret Key | The AccessKey secret of your Apsara Stack tenant account. |
| Advanced Parameters | Specify the indexes to be restored in the snapshot. Refer to the es restore syntax. The default is {}. _ For example, you can restore the indexes index1 and index2 in the snapshot. {"indices":"index1,index2"} |

6. Click **Restore**.

###### 8.2.2.7.1 Install, update, and uninstall plug-ins

You must install a plug-in before you can use it. Built-in plug-ins are installed by default. This topic describes how to install a non-built-in plug-in.

**Prerequisites**

2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Instance Management**.
3. On the **Instance Management** page, click the target **Instance ID**.
4. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Plugin Management > Elasticsearch Plugin**.

> **Note:** Elasticsearch plug-ins are used as an example in this topic. You can install other plug- ins by following the same procedure.

5. Install or update a plug-in.
Install a plug-in If the page displays large numbers of plug-ins, enter the name of the desired plug-in into the search box to find the plug-in. Fuzzy match is supported. Install a plug-in: Click **Install** in the **Update** column of the plug-in that you want to install. Install multiple plug-ins at a time: Select the plug-ins you want to install and click
**Batch Install**.
&M

> **Warning:** Plug-in installation triggers cluster restarts. Proceed with caution.

Update a plug-in If a new version is available for the current plug-in, the system automatically displays the new version in the **Updatable Plugin Version** column. To update the current plug-in to the new version, find the plug-in that you want to update, click **Update**, and then click **Confirm**. If the plug-in cannot automatically restart due to the update, click **Restart** in the upper-right corner to restart the plug-in. After the plug-in is installed or updated, you can click **Uninstall** or **Batch Uninstall** to uninstall the plug-in.

##### 8.2.2.8 Configure cluster O&M

You can use the cluster O&M feature to update the kernel version, diagnose cluster health, and upgrade the deployment mode. You can also modify the password, specifications, and YML file of an Elasticsearch cluster. This topic describes how to use the cluster O&M feature.

**Prerequisites**

An Elasticsearch cluster is created, and the cluster is in the Normal state. For more information, see Create a cluster.

**Go to the Cluster Operations page**

1. Log in to the Elasticsearch O&M console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Instance Management**.
3. On the **Instance Management** page, click the target **Instance ID**.
4. Click the ID of a cluster in the list. In the left-side navigation pane of the page that appears,
click **Cluster Operations**.

**Update the kernel version**

**Usage notes**

Kernel version updates cannot be rolled back. We recommend that you perform an inspection and back up important data before you update the kernel version. Do not directly update the kernel version of an Elasticsearch cluster that has custom plug-ins installed. To reduce the impact on the cluster, make sure that the number of replica shards of each index in the cluster is greater than one. The update operation triggers a cluster image update and restart. This may cause business interruptions. Perform this operation during off-peak hours and pay close attention to the monitoring data of the cluster. &M
1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Version Upgrade**.
3. If the current cluster has a version or kernel image available for update, click **Impact**
**Analysis** to view the content of the update.
If the current cluster does not have any version or kernel image available for update, you can skip this step.
4. Click **Upgrade**.
5. In the message that appears, click **Confirm**.
After the update is complete, the cluster enters the Normal state, and the cluster and cluster image are updated to the latest versions.

**Security settings**

**Enable HTTPS**

Hyper Text Transfer Protocol over Secure Socket Layer (HTTPS) is a security-enhanced version of HTTP. HTTPS works with Secure Socket Layer (SSL) to ensure the security of data transmission. HTTPS uses HTTP for communication. SSL is used to encrypt data. To ensure data security, we recommend that you enable HTTPS.
1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, turn on the switch below **HTTPS Protocol** based on your
business requirements.

**Change the port of the Elasticsearch cluster**

After you create an Elasticsearch cluster, you can change the port of the cluster.
1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Settings**.
3. In the **ES Port Number** section of the **Security Settings** page, enter the desired port
number and click **Modify** to change the port.

> **Note:** The default port is 9200. After your modification succeeds, a message is prompted, and the new port number is displayed.

**Configure a VPC whitelist**

Before you access an Alibaba Cloud Elasticsearch cluster over a virtual private cloud (VPC), you need to add the IP address of your device to a VPC whitelist of the cluster. If you fail to access an Elasticsearch cluster, you can follow the instructions in this topic to check whether you have added the correct IP address to a VPC whitelist of the cluster.
1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **VPC Private Network Access Whitelist**.
4. Click **Add IP Whitelist**. In the **IP Whitelist** dialog box, configure **VPC** and **Whitelist**.
5. Click **Confirm**.

**Account security settings**

&M You can specify whether the specified user can log in to the Kibana console and configure a whitelist to improve cluster and system security. After you create a cluster, you must configure a whitelist. Otherwise, you may encounter issues such as failure to collect monitoring data and failure to log in to the Kibana console.
1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **Account Information** to view and modify account
information.
**Login Name**:
elastic: the administrator account, which has all permissions. You cannot modify its whitelist.

> **Important:** If you reset the password of the elastic account for an Elasticsearch cluster, only access to the cluster by using the elastic account is affected. Access to the Elasticsearch cluster by using other accounts is not affected. We recommend that you use a custom account to access your Elasticsearch cluster. The custom account must be assigned a role with the required permissions.

monitoring_collector: the account used by the control service. The account has the aliyun-ops permission. Some control features, such as monitoring data collection and automatic backup, rely on this account. The account is granted the least control permissions. It cannot be used to access user data. The whitelist of this account must contain all possible IP addresses of the control components. If the whitelist is improperly configured, some control features will become unavailable. For example, you may be unable to view monitoring data, enable automatic backup, or perform disaster recovery failovers through Apsara Stack Resilience. kibanaserver: the account is used by the Kibana service. The account has the kibana_system permission and is granted only the least permissions required for initializing Kibana. The account cannot be used to access user data. The whitelist of this account must contain the IP address of the Kibana service. If the whitelist is improperly configured, Kibana cannot be accessed.
**Can Login to Kibana**:
After you enable Logon to Kibana Console, you must add the IP address of the Kibana service to the whitelist of the corresponding account. Otherwise, you cannot use the account to log in to the Kibana console.
**Change Password**:
Click **Change Password** to change the password of an account. This operation does not require cluster restarts.
**Modify Whitelist**:
Click **Modify Whitelist** to modify the whitelist. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas (,). Example: `127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2` . Specify an IP address range by entering a CIDR block. For example, `1.2.3.4/24` indicates that all IP addresses in the 1.2.3.X CIDR block are allowed to access the Elasticsearch cluster. By default, the whitelist is set to `127.0.0.1` , which means that the corresponding account is not allowed to remotely access the Elasticsearch cluster. &M

**Certificate information**

This section displays the certificate used by Elasticsearch nodes to communicate with each other. Only nodes with the same certificate can access each other.

> **Important:** The certificate is randomly generated by the system. If you want to use the Cross Data Center Replication (XDCR), Cross-Cluster Search (CCS), or Cross-Cluster Reindex feature in Elasticsearch, make sure that the primary and secondary clusters use the same certificate.
> You can use custom certificates. If you want to change the certificate, contact the O&M engineer.

**Obtain the IP addresses**

**Method 1: Obtain the IP address of the kibana/essen/exporter**

**pod**

> **Note:** When you run the following commands on the ops machine, remove ${ } and keep only the enclosed content.

```bash
# Obtain the pod IP address. The namespace of kibana/exporter is the same as that of th
e cluster. The namespace of essen is essen.
 kubectl get pod -n ${Namespace of the service} -owide
```

**Method 2: Obtain the CIDR block of the**

**kibana/essen/exporter/snapshot service**

> **Important:** The reason why you need to use Method 2 is that the pod IP address in Method 1 drifts after the pod restarts. To avoid this issue, you can add the CIDR block of the service to the whitelist. However, make sure that the CIDR block added to the whitelist is the smallest. To obtain the smallest CIDR block, consult the delivery or security engineer.

To obtain the CIDR block of the corresponding Elasticsearch service, you need to obtain the subnet information of the current environment.

```bash
 kubectl get subnet
```

&M IP address ranges are represented by using CIDR blocks. In hybrid deployment mode, any CIDR block can be allocated to the service. In dedicated deployment mode, resources related to the Elasticsearch cluster are deployed on dedicated machines. The control service may fall into all CIDR blocks.

> **Important:** This method is for reference only. For more information, consult the delivery or security engineer.

**Troubleshoot errors and exceptions**

Failure to log in to the Kibana console Error message: Elasticsearch V6.X/7.X: kibana server is not ready yet Elasticsearch V5.X: Authorization Exception Cause: The whitelist of the kibanaserver account is improperly configured. Solution: Modify the whitelist of the kibanaserver account and add the IP address of the Kibana service to the whitelist of the kibanaserver account. You can still log in to the Kibana console after the Kibana whitelist is disabled Exception: You can still log in to the Kibana console after the Kibana whitelist is disabled. Cause: The Kibana page is not reinitialized. Solution: Contact the O&M engineer to restart the pod that runs the Kibana service. No monitoring data is displayed Exception: "no data" is displayed on the Grafana monitoring page. Cause: The whitelist of the monitoring_collector account is improperly configured. Solution: Modify the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account and add the IP address of the exporter service to the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account. An error is thrown when you access the Elasticsearch plug-in page Error message: 403 Forbidden:[Ip 23.5.**.** is not allow in ip white/black list] Cause: The whitelist of the monitoring_collector account is improperly configured. Solution: Modify the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account and add the IP address of the essen service to the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account. An error is thrown when you access the automatic backup page Error message: proxy request fail Cause: The whitelist of the monitoring_collector account is improperly configured. Solution: Modify the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account and add the IP address of the essen service to the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account. Automatic backup does not take effect Exception: The snapshot is not taken normally after the specified time point. &M Cause: The whitelist of the monitoring_collector account is improperly configured. Solution: Modify the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account and add the IP address of the snapshot service to the whitelist of the monitoring_collector account. Kibana login error Exception: The account password is correct, but a login error is thrown (monitoring_collector is used as an example). Cause analysis: The whitelist of the account is not configured properly, or **Can Login to**
**Kibana** is not selected.
Solution: Add the IP address of the Kibana service to the whitelist of the account and select **Can Login to Kibana**. Cross-cluster access error Error message: [][22.0.x.x:9300] general node connection failure Cause: The clusters that need to intercommunicate use different certificates. Solution: Contact the O&M engineer or refer to the cluster management operations in the O&M guide.

**Modify cluster specifications**

1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specification Configuration**.
3. Click **Modify** for a node.
4. Enter the node configuration.
For more information about the parameters, see Create a cluster.

> **Warning:** After you modify the configuration, the cluster is restarted. Proceed with caution.

5. Click **Save**.

**Modify the YML file of the cluster**

1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Configuration Modification**.
3. In the **elasticsearch.yml** text box, enter the YML configuration.

> **Warning:** After you modify the configuration, the cluster is restarted. Proceed with caution.

4. Click **Save**.

**Upgrade the deployment mode**

You can upgrade the deployment mode of an Elasticsearch cluster. For example, you can upgrade the deployment mode from single-zone to multi-zone. &M

> **Note:** The deployment mode upgrade feature applies only to Elasticsearch clusters that are deployed across two or more zones.

1. Go to the Cluster Operations page.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Deployment Mode Upgrade**.
3. On the **Deployment Mode Upgrade** page, check whether the deployment mode of the
current cluster can be upgraded. If the system prompts that no deployment mode is available, you cannot upgrade the deployment mode of the cluster. To upgrade the deployment mode of the cluster in this case, go to the Platform Management page and modify the zone configuration of the cluster. For more information, see Zone configuration. If the page displays the ID and name, deployment mode (before upgrade), and deployment mode (after upgrade) of the current cluster, you can upgrade the deployment mode of the cluster by performing the following steps.

> **Note:** You can upgrade the cluster only to the deployment mode selected on the Availability Zone Configuration page of the Platform Management module, and downgrades are not supported.

4. In the **Basic Check** step, check whether the cluster meets the upgrade conditions based on
the on-screen instructions. If yes, click **Next**.
5. In the **Resource Assessment** step, assess resources based on the on-screen instructions.
If the resources meet the condition, click **Next**.
6. In the **Risk Confirmation** step, confirm the risks. Then, click **Start**.
7. In the message that appears, click **Confirm**.
Then, the system starts to upgrade the deployment mode and restarts the cluster at the same time. After the cluster enters the Normal state, the upgrade is complete.

###### 8.2.2.8.1 Upgrade the version

This topic describes how to upgrade the kernel version during cluster Operations and Maintenance (O&M).

**Prerequisites**

An instance is created and its status is Normal. For more information, see Create an instance.

**Limits**

Only Elasticsearch instances support this feature. OpenSearch instances do not.

**Notes**

The upgrade process does not support rollbacks. Before you upgrade, perform a basic inspection and back up critical data. Do not directly upgrade clusters that have custom plugins installed. To reduce the impact on the cluster, ensure that the number of replicas for all indexes in the cluster is greater than 1. &M The upgrade operation triggers a cluster image update and restart. This may cause service jitter. Perform this operation during off-peak hours and monitor the cluster.

**Go to the cluster O&M page**

1. Log on to the Search and Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Instance Management**.
3. On the **Instance Management** page, click the target **instance ID**.
4. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Cluster O&M**.

**Upgrade the kernel version**

1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Version Upgrade**.
3. If an upgradable version or kernel image is detected for your instance, click **Impact**
**Analysis** to view the upgrade details.
If no upgradable version or kernel image is detected, no action is required.
4. Click **Upgrade**.
5. In the dialog box that appears, click **Confirm**.
After the upgrade is complete, the cluster status is Normal, and the instance version and image version are updated to the latest versions.

###### 8.2.2.8.2 Security settings

Security settings let you enable the HTTPS protocol with one click, change the ES port number, manage the VPC internal-facing access whitelist, modify account information, and view certificate details.

**Use the HTTPS protocol**

HTTPS (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol Secure) is a secure version of HTTP that uses SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) to encrypt data during transmission. To protect your data, use the HTTPS protocol.

> **Important:** By default, this feature is disabled for Elasticsearch instances. Enable it manually. For OpenSearch instances, this feature is enabled by default and cannot be disabled.

1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **Https Protocol**. Then, turn on the switch for this
feature as needed.

**Change the ES port number**

After creating an instance, you can change the port number as needed.
1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, in the **Port Number** area, enter the new port number and
click **Modify** to update it. &M

> **Note:** The default port number is 9200. After a successful modification, a success message appears and the port number updates to the new value.

**Configure the VPC internal-facing access whitelist**

When you access an Alibaba Cloud Elasticsearch (ES) instance over an internal network, you must first add the IP address of the accessing device to the instance's whitelist. If you cannot access the ES instance, check whether the correct IP address is in the whitelist.
1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **VPC Internal-facing Access Whitelist**.
4. Click **Add IP Whitelist**. In the **IP Whitelist** dialog box, configure the **VPC** and **Whitelist**
**Information**.
5. Click **OK**.

**Account security settings**

Improve cluster and system security by specifying which users can log on to Kibana or the dashboard and by setting up a proper whitelist. After you create a new cluster, you must set up a whitelist first. Otherwise, you may encounter issues such as failing to collect monitoring data or being unable to log on to Kibana.
1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **Account Information** to view and modify account
details. View logon names elastic (or admin): The logon name is elastic for Elasticsearch instances and admin for OpenSearch instances. The elastic/admin account is the administrator account and has all superuser permissions.

> **Important:** Resetting the password affects access to the instance with the elastic/admin account. It does not affect access with other non-elastic/admin accounts. For this reason, do not use the elastic/admin account to access the instance from your programs. Instead, use a custom user with the necessary permissions.

kibanaserver: This is the account used by the Kibana service. It has the kibana_system permission, which includes only the least privilege required for Kibana initialization. It cannot read user data. The whitelist for this account must include the IP address where the Kibana service is located. If not configured correctly, Kibana will be inaccessible. &M monitoring_collector: This is the account used by the management service. It has the aliyun-ops permission. Some management features, such as collecting monitoring data and running automatic backups, depend on this account. It includes only the least privilege required for management and cannot read user data. The whitelist for this account must include all possible IP addresses of the management components. If not configured correctly, some management features will be degraded and become unavailable. For example, you cannot view monitoring data, enable automatic backups, or perform a switchover using ASR. Change password Click **Change Password** to change the password for the account. You do not need to restart the cluster. Modify whitelist

> **Important:** Currently, only Elasticsearch instances support whitelist modification. OpenSearch instances do not.

Click **Modify Whitelist** to change the whitelist configuration. To configure multiple IP addresses, separate them with a comma (,). For example,

```
 127.0.0.1,127.0.0.2 .
```

Specify an address range using CIDR notation. For example, `1.2.3.4/24` allows access to the ES instance from IP addresses in the 1.2.3.X CIDR block. `127.0.0.1` is the default empty whitelist. An account configured with this whitelist cannot remotely access the ES instance.

**View certificate information**

This certificate is used for communication between ES nodes. Nodes can access each other if the fingerprints of their issued certificates are the same.
1. Go to the cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Security Settings**.
3. On the **Security Settings** page, click **Certificate Information** to view the certificate
details.

> **Important:** The current certificate is randomly generated by the system. To use the XDCR feature, CCS feature, or cross-cluster reindex in ES, the certificates of the primary and secondary clusters must be identical to establish a connection.
> Custom certificates are supported. To change a certificate, contact an on-site O&M engineer.

**Related information**

**Get an IP address**

**Method 1: Get the pod IP address for kibana, essen, or**

**exporter**

&M

> **Note:** When you run the command on a terminal server, remove ${ } and keep the content inside.

```bash
 # Get the pod IP address. The namespace for kibana/exporter is the same as the cluster
's namespace. The namespace for essen is essen.
 kubectl get pod -n ${service_namespace} -owide
```

**Method 2: Get the IP CIDR block for the kibana, essen,**

**exporter, or snapshot service**

> **Important:** The reason for getting the IP CIDR block is that the pod IP address from Method 1 can change if the pod restarts. Configuring a CIDR block avoids this issue. However, you must configure the whitelist with the least privilege granularity. For the effective CIDR block with the least privilege, consult the delivery or on-site security team.

To get the possible IP CIDR blocks for the corresponding Elasticsearch service, obtain all CIDR block information for the current environment:

```bash
 kubectl get subnet
```

The address range is expressed in CIDR notation. For a shared deployment, any CIDR block may be allocated. For a dedicated deployment, ES instance resources are deployed on dedicated machines, but management services may still be located in any CIDR block.

> **Important:** This method is for reference only. For specific details, consult the delivery or on-site security team.

Cannot log on to the Kibana interface &M Error message: Version 6.x/7.x: kibana server is not ready yet Version 5.x: Authorization Exception Cause: The whitelist for the kibanaserver account is configured incorrectly. Solution: Modify the whitelist for the kibanaserver account. Add the IP address of the Kibana service to the whitelist. Can still log on to Kibana after the whitelist is disabled Symptom: You can still log on to Kibana after the whitelist is disabled. Cause: The Kibana interface was not re-initialized. Solution: Contact an on-site O&M engineer to restart the pod where Kibana is located. No monitoring data Symptom: The Grafana monitoring page shows "no data". Cause: The whitelist for the monitoring_collector account is configured incorrectly. Solution: Modify the whitelist for the monitoring_collector account. Add the IP address of the exporter service to the whitelist. Error when accessing the Elasticsearch plugin page Error message: 403 Forbidden:[Ip 23.5.**.** is not allow in ip white/black list] Cause: The whitelist for the monitoring_collector account is configured incorrectly. Solution: Modify the whitelist for the monitoring_collector account. Add the IP address of the essen service to the whitelist. Error when accessing the automatic backup page Error message: proxy request fail Cause: The whitelist for the monitoring_collector account is configured incorrectly. Solution: Modify the whitelist for the monitoring_collector account. Add the IP address of the essen service to the whitelist. Automatic backup does not work Symptom: A snapshot is not created at the scheduled time. Cause: The whitelist for the monitoring_collector account is configured incorrectly. Solution: Modify the whitelist for the monitoring_collector account. Add the IP address of the snapshot service to the whitelist. ###### 8.2.2.8.3 Instance specifications

You can modify the specifications of an instance to change the size of its nodes.

###### 8.2.2.8.5 Upgrade the deployment method

You can upgrade the deployment method of a cluster, such as from a single-zone to a multizone deployment.

**Limits**

Only Elasticsearch instances support this feature. This feature is not supported for OpenSearch instances.

**Upgrade the deployment method**

> **Important:** Deployment method upgrades are available only for clusters that were initially configured for dual-zone or multi-zone deployment.

1. Go to the Cluster O&M page.
2. In the navigation pane on the left, click **Deployment Method Upgrade**.
3. On the **Deployment Method Upgrade** page, check if the deployment method of the
current instance can be upgraded. If a message indicates that no deployment methods are available for upgrade, the current instance cannot be upgraded. To enable an upgrade, go to the Platform Management page and change the zone configuration. For more information, see Zone Configuration. If the page shows the instance ID/Name, Deployment Method (Before Upgrade), and Deployment Method (After Upgrade), the instance can be upgraded. Follow the subsequent steps to perform the upgrade.

> **Note:** The deployment method can only be upgraded to the one specified in the zone configuration on the Platform Management page of the O&M console. Downgrades are not supported.

4. In the **Basic Check** section, follow the prompts to check if the instance meets the upgrade
requirements. After confirming that the requirements are met, click **Next**.
5. In the **Resource Assessment** section, assess the resources as prompted on the page.
After confirming that the resources meet the requirements, click **Next**.
6. In the **Risk Warning** section, review and confirm the risks as prompted. After confirmation,
click **Start**.
7. In the dialog box that appears, click **OK**.
&M After you click OK, the system begins to upgrade the deployment method, and the cluster restarts. The upgrade is complete when the cluster status changes to Normal.

#### 8.2.3 Platform management

##### 8.2.3.1 Repository management

This topic describes how to use the repository management feature to manage the snapshot repositories of Elasticsearch. The automatic backup feature of Elasticsearch clusters relies on repositories. You can use this feature to query, add, modify, and delete repositories.

**Go to the Repository Management page**

1. Log on to the Search & Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Platform Management > Repository**
**Management**.

**Add a repository**

1. Go to the Repository Management page.
2. In the upper-right corner of the page, click **Add**.
3. In the dialog box that appears, enter a repository name, modify the repository
configuration, and then click **Confirm**. After the repository is added, you can view the repository in the list.

> **Note:** If you cannot find the repository, click **Refresh** in the upper-right corner of the page.

**Query repositories**

1. Go to the Repository Management page.
2. Select a query condition from the drop-down list above the list.
You can query repositories by **Repository Name** or **Repository Type**.
3. Enter the keyword.
Then, the system searches for repositories in fuzzy match mode.

**Modify a repository**

1. Go to the Repository Management page.
2. In the repository list, click **Edit** in the **Action** column of a repository.
3. In the dialog box that appears, modify the repository configuration and click **Confirm**. The
repository name is not modifiable.

> **Important:** If automatic backup is enabled, the configuration of automatic backup remains unchanged after you modify the repository. If automatic backup is disabled and you enable the feature after modifying the repository, such as changing the bucket name, the automatic backup feature uses the modified repository configuration, such as pointing to the new bucket. In this case, you cannot view the previous automatic backup data.

&M

**Delete a repository**

1. Go to the Repository Management page.
2. In the repository list, click **Delete** in the **Action** column of a repository.

> **Warning:** A deleted repository cannot be restored. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

3. In the message that appears, click **Confirm**.

##### 8.2.3.2 Plug-in management

The plug-in management feature allows you to manage Elasticsearch plug-ins, Logstash plugins, and Kibana plug-ins. The plug-ins described in this topic are platform plug-ins, which are separately managed by Elasticsearch cluster version. The installation and updating of plugins rely on the plug-in library of the platform.

**Go to the plug-in management page**

1. Log on to the Search & Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Platform Management**.
3. Click **Elasticsearch Plugin**, **Logstash Plugin**, or **Kibana Plugin** below **Plugin**
**Management** to go to the corresponding page.

**View platform plug-ins**

1. Go to the plug-in management page.
2. In the upper-left corner of the page, select an Elasticsearch version to view the supported
plug-ins. The following figure shows how to view Elasticsearch plug-ins.

**Upload a plug-in**

1. Go to the plug-in management page.
2. In the upper-left corner of the page, select an Elasticsearch version.
3. Click **Upload Plugin**.
4. In the **Upload Plugin** dialog box, upload the plug-in installation package.
5. Click **Upload**.
After the upload is complete, the plug-in is displayed in the plug-in list. &M

> **Note:** If you cannot find the plug-in, click **Refresh** in the upper-right corner of the page.

**Update a plug-in**

1. Go to the plug-in management page.
2. In the upper-left corner of the page, select an Elasticsearch version.
3. Click **Update** in the **Action** column of a plug-in.

> **Important:** 不支持更新内置插件。

4. In the **Update Plugin** dialog box, upload the plug-in installation package.
5. Click **Upload**.

**Delete a plug-in**

1. Go to the plug-in management page.
2. In the upper-left corner of the page, select an Elasticsearch version.
3. Click **Delete** in the **Action** column of a plug-in.

> **Warning:** Proceed with caution because you must reinstall the plug-in if you want to use the plug-in again.
> If an existing cluster uses a plug-in that has been deleted, the cluster fails to perform the rolling, scale-out, and restart operations.

4. Click **Confirm**.

The operation control feature allows you to manage and control the use of AnyTunnel and operations performed by other users to modify Elasticsearch clusters. This topic describes how to control the use of AnyTunnel and the operations performed by other users to modify Elasticsearch clusters.

clusters and the operations that can be performed to modify Elasticsearch clusters.

**Current cloud platform Elasticsearch product new instance network type**

**control setting is** You can select **Allow AnyTunnel usage** or **Disallow AnyTunnel**
**usage**.

**usage**. The change takes effect only on clusters created after you make the change. The
existing clusters are not affected.

If you select **Disallow all changes**, other users are not allowed to create clusters, scale out clusters, modify cluster configurations, or install plug-ins in the user console or O&M console. ##### 8.2.3.6 Benchmark test

To assess whether the configuration of a newly created Elasticsearch cluster meets your business requirements, you can use the benchmark test feature provided by Apsara Stack Elasticsearch to benchmark the read and write performance of the cluster with a few clicks.

**Introduction to benchmark test plans**

The benchmark test consists of the following content: Machine performance test: tests the performance of cluster hardware, such as the CPU, memory, and disk I/O. Key metrics: CPU speed: the computing capability (single-core) CPU dispatch speed: the scheduling capability for context switching memory write speed: the memory write speed memory read speed: the memory read speed disk IO read speed: the disk read speed disk IO write speed: the disk write speed ESRally stress testing: tests the write and query performance of a cluster. The following table describes the stress testing configuration.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Rally configurations | The default Rally tracks are used. |
| Datasets | The http logs dataset provided by Rally is used. _ |
| Number of shards | Primary shards: 5. Replica shards: 0. |
| bulk size _ | 5,000 documents are submitted in each batch. |
| bulk indexing client _ _ s | 8 clients are used in parallel to manage indexes in batches. |
| Output result | The report is generated as a CSV file. |

> **Important:** The benchmark test requires you to read data from and write data to the Elasticsearch cluster, which affects the read and write performance of the cluster. Proceed with caution when you benchmark a production cluster.

&M
1. Log on to the Search & Analysis Service O&M console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Platform Management**.
3. Then, choose **Benchmark Testing > Benchmark Testing**.
4. Create a benchmark test.
i. Enter the ID, username, and password of the Elasticsearch you want to benchmark. ii. Select a benchmark test plan and specify whether to forcefully run the test. Default benchmark: uses Rally for the benchmark test. Default benchmark and delete test index after completion: uses Rally for the benchmark test and deletes all testing indexes after the test is complete. iii. Click **Confirm**. The new test is displayed on the Benchmark Testing page.
5. View the benchmark test result.
Wait until the test is complete and click **View Results** in the Action column of the test. In the dialog box that appears, view the benchmark test result of the cluster.
6. Optional. Delete the benchmark test results.
On the Benchmark Testing page, click **Delete** in the **Action** column of the test to delete the benchmark test results. You can also select multiple tests and click **Batch Delete** to delete the benchmark test results of these tests at a time.

##### 8.2.4.2 View Elasticsearch monitoring metrics

This topic describes how to view Elasticsearch monitoring metrics on a custom dashboard.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top menu bar, choose **Monitoring and Alerts > Monitoring Management >**
**Cloud Platform Monitoring Dashboard**.
3. In the navigation pane on the left, choose **Data Dashboards > Custom Dashboards**.
4. In the **Dashboard Catalog** list, select **ElasticSearch Monitoring Dashboard**.
5. Click the dashboard name **Elasticsearch** or **OpenSearch** to view the monitoring metrics
on the dashboard. The key monitoring metrics are described in the following tables. The metrics displayed on the UI prevail.

**Elasticsearch monitoring metrics**

| Metric category | Metric | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Cluster | Cluster health | The health status of the cluster. Colors indicate overall availability: green means all shards are allocated; yellow means replica shards are unassigned, indicating a potential risk; red means primary shards are unassigned, indicating data loss. |
|   | Node state | The role status of nodes. This metric shows node role types, such as data nodes and client nodes, and their distribution. |
|   | Data state max | The maximum resource usage of data nodes. This metric monitors peak utilization of CPU, JVM heap memory, and disk space on data nodes. |
|   | Coordinating state max | The maximum resource usage of client nodes. This metric monitors peak load of CPU and JVM heap memory on client nodes (non-data/ingest nodes). |
|   | Index State | Core status metrics for an index. These include doc values memory usage, segment count, and total document count, which reflect the health of the underlying index structure. |
|   | Pending tasks | The number of pending tasks in the cluster. This metric shows cluster-level operations waiting for execution, such as index creation and shard allocation. A consistently non-zero or increasing value indicates that the master node is overloaded or tasks are blocked. |

&M

|   | Tripped for breakers | The number of times the circuit breaker was tripped. This metric tracks requests rejected due to memory overload. A value greater than 0 indicates high memory pressure on the node. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Open file descriptors per cluster | The total number of file descriptors in the cluster. This metric reflects the total number of open file handles across all nodes. An excessively high value can lead to system resource exhaustion. |
|   | Active shards | The total number of active shards. This is the sum of primary and replica shards providing services normally in the cluster. |
|   | Active primary shards | The number of active primary shards. This is the number of primary shards providing write services normally in the cluster. |
|   | Shard per node | The shard load balancing on nodes. This metric calculates the average number of primary shards each data node carries. An excessively high value can cause hot spot issues. |
| Shards |   |   |
|   | Unassigned shards | The number of unassigned shards. This is the number of shards not successfully allocated to any node. A value greater than 0 indicates that data may be inaccessible or query performance is degraded. |
|   | Initializing shards | The number of initializing shards. This is the number of shards being recovered or created. A consistently high value indicates slow cluster recovery. |
|   | Relocating shards | The number of relocating shards. This is the number of shards being migrated between nodes. This metric reflects the intensity of cluster load balancing activities. |
|   | Delayed shards | The number of delayed unassigned shards. This is the number of shards whose allocation is delayed due to a timeout or unmet conditions. |
| Nodes & Indices | Nodes stats | The real-time resource status of nodes. This metric shows node-level monitoring of CPU, JVM memory, disk space, system load, and the number of index storage units, documents, and segments. |
| Document Version: 20 | 260703 117 |   |

| tform Operation and M e Operations Guide·Big |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | Index stats | Core performance metrics for an index. These include key statistics such as shard document distribution, total document count, storage size, active queries, and segment memory. |
| JVM Garbage Collection | Young GC count | The rate of garbage collection (GC) in the young generation space. This is the frequency at which GC is triggered in the JVM young generation space per unit time. A high frequency may indicate that objects are being created too quickly. |
|   | Old GC count | The rate of GC in the old generation space. This is the frequency at which GC is triggered in the JVM old generation space per unit time. A high frequency may indicate a memory leak or insufficient heap configuration. |
|   | Young GC time | The rate of time spent on GC in the young generation space. This is the amount of CPU time consumed by GC in the JVM young generation space per unit time. This affects write and query latency. |
|   | Old GC time | The rate of time spent on GC in the old generation space. This is the amount of CPU time consumed by GC in the JVM old generation space per unit time. Long pauses can cause service stuttering. |
| Translog | Total translog operations | The rate of change in the total number of transaction log operations. This is the number of operations written to the transaction log per unit time. This metric reflects the intensity of the write load. |
|   | Total translog size in bytes | The rate of change in the transaction log size. This is the number of bytes the transaction log grows by per unit time. An excessively large size can affect recovery speed. |
| Breakers | Tripped for breakers | The number of times the circuit breaker was tripped. This metric tracks requests rejected due to memory overload. A value greater than 0 indicates high memory pressure on the node. |
|   | Estimated size in bytes of breaker | The estimated memory usage of the circuit breaker. This metric compares the estimated memory consumption of the current request in bytes with the circuit breaker threshold to prevent out-of-memory (OOM) errors. |

&M &M

| CPU and Memory | CPU usage | The CPU usage of the node. This is the percentage of CPU resource consumption at the operating system level. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Young - JVM heap memory used | The amount of used heap memory in the young generation space. This is the amount of heap memory currently used in the JVM young generation space (Eden/Survivor areas). |
|   | Load1 average | The 1-minute system load average. This is the average CPU load of the node over the last minute, reflecting short-term pressure. |
|   | Old - JVM heap memory used | The amount of used heap memory in the old generation space. This is the amount of heap memory currently used in the JVM old generation space. A continuous increase may indicate a memory leak. |
|   | Load5 average | The 5-minute system load average. This is the average CPU load of the node over the last 5 minutes, reflecting the medium-term pressure trend. |
|   | JVM non-heap memory usage | The JVM non-heap memory usage. This is the percentage of memory occupied by non-heap areas such as Metaspace and thread stacks. |
|   | Load15 average | The 15-minute system load average. This is the average CPU load of the node over the last 15 minutes, reflecting the long-term pressure trend. |
|   | JVM peak memory usage | The peak JVM memory usage. This is the historical maximum memory usage in bytes, used for capacity planning. |
|   | JVM heap memory used | The percentage of used heap memory in the JVM. This is the ratio of currently used heap memory to maximum heap memory. A value over 75% requires attention. |
|   | Disk IO throughput | The disk I/O throughput. This is the amount of data read from and written to the disk per unit time (KB/s). This metric reflects storage performance bottlenecks. |

| e Operations Guide·Big |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Disk and Network |   |   |
|   | Total Disk Operations rate | The rate of disk operations. This is the total disk input/output operations per second (IOPS), including read and write operations, per unit time. A high value may affect query latency. |
|   | Disk usage size | The used disk space. This is the disk space in bytes occupied by the Elasticsearch data directory on the node. |
|   | Network usage sent | The outbound network traffic. This is the number of data bytes transmitted outward from the node per unit time, such as for shard recovery and replica synchronization. |
|   | Disk usage | The percentage of used disk space. This is the ratio of used space in the data directory to total space. If the value exceeds 85%, you need to scale out the disk space. |
|   | Network usage received | The inbound network traffic. This is the number of data bytes received by the node per unit time, such as from client writes and cross-node queries. |
